93278c0595bfcb2b.title: MSME training programme held at VIT in Vellore
93278c0595bfcb2b.summary: Published - November 05, 2026 12:50 am IST - VELLORE Collector P.S. Leela Alex inaugurates the training programme in the presence of G. Viswanathan, founder and president, VIT, and other dignitaries at VIT campus. | Photo Credit: Special Arrangement A month-long smartphone servicing and repair training programme under an entrepreneurship skill development initiative, which was organised by the Micro, Small and Medium Enterprises (MSME) sector, was held at the campus of Vellore Institute of Technology (VIT) in Vellore on Wednesday. Collector P.S. Leela Alex inaugurated the training programme in the presence of G. Viswanathan, founder and president, VIT, Sankar Viswanathan, vice-president, VIT, and Reshma Rajeevan, deputy director, Department of MSME. In his presidential address, Mr. Viswanathan said that the MSME sector forms the backbone of the Indian economy. After agriculture, it is the second-largest employer, providing jobs to around 33 crore people in the country. “Around seven crore MSMEs are registered across the country with Maharashtra leading with one crore MSMEs, followed by Uttar Pradesh with 85 lakh MSMEs. Tamil Nadu comes third with 62 lakh MSMEs. The sector contributes 45 per cent to manufacturing output and 46 per cent to exports,” he said. The Chancellor said that VIT has been implementing a free scholarship scheme - Support The Advancement of Rural Students (STARS) - for government school students. Around ₹103 crore worth of scholarships under the scheme have been distributed to students since the scheme was started, in 2008. VIT has also provided free admissions to 1,200 students between 2008 and 2026 under the scheme. “VIT plans to expand the scheme to the entire country, where beneficiaries will get free education, accommodation, and food. At present, the scheme has been executed only in Tamil Nadu, Andhra Pradesh, and Madhya Pradesh, “ he said. Published - November 05, 2026 12:50 am IST Terms & conditions | Institutional Subscriber Comments hav

85edcbb69df72812.title: Cabinet clears ₹14,500 cr funding scheme for battery energy storage systems
85edcbb69df72812.summary: The Union Cabinet on Wednesday approved Rs 14,500 crore in viability gap funding for 92 GWh of grid-scale energy storage systems between FY27 and FY31. This development is significant given India's ambitious target of 500 GW of renewable energy by 2030. The scheme is aimed at supporting the development of 92 GWh storage capacity across three technologies -- Battery Energy Storage System (30 GWh), Pumped Storage Projects (60 GWh) and Emerging Storage Technologies (2GW), Information and Broadcasting Minister Ashwini Vaishnaw said in a media briefing here. The minister said the scheme will be implemented for five years till 2030-31.

94436e0dedf1355a.title: Helping hand: On Cyclones Arnab and Murasu
94436e0dedf1355a.summary: Updated - November 05, 2026 01:47 am IST Long-term preparedness and a swift response by authorities minimised casualties when the back-to-back cyclones Arnab and Murasu hit two places of the Andhra Pradesh coast. In Andhra Pradesh, damage from Cyclone Arnab , which made landfall on October 28 was estimated at roughly ₹4,526 crore. Initial estimates of the damage by Cyclone Murasu, which crossed the coast on November 3, indicate that about 52,500 hectares of standing crops were affected. The State reported 12 deaths from the two cyclones. The first cyclone damaged nearly 90,000 hectares of standing crops in southern parts of Odisha. After preliminary on-the-spot assessment of flood-hit areas, the Union government is expected to soon release the first instalment of funds to the affected States. Personnel from Karnataka, Telangana and Tamil Nadu have also gone to the rescue of Andhra Pradesh. The deployment of the Real Time Governance Society (RTGS) and other technologies has significantly reduced human casualties and property damage. During Cyclone Hudhud in October 2014, Andhra Pradesh reported 63 deaths and damage estimated at nearly ₹22,000 crore. As natural disasters become more frequent in India, greater collaboration is needed between higher learning institutions, especially in science and technology, and central and State government agencies. Authorities must develop an effective compensation framework for saving crops/crop losses. The Pradhan Mantri Fasal Bima Yojana, a crop insurance scheme that was launched by the Union government a decade ago, has not provided farmers with comprehensive safety cover, as they suffer due to the vagaries of nature. f1be7d22672b238e.title: What the BRICS carbon market partnership needs
f1be7d22672b238e.summary: Updated - November 05, 2026 12:34 am IST ‘A common framework for measurement, reporting and verification should be the partnership’s first deliverable’ | Photo Credit: Getty Images/iStockphoto On September 12, at the 18th BRICS Summit in New Delhi, the New Delhi Declaration confirmed that BRICS members look forward to implementing the Memorandum of Understanding on the BRICS Carbon Markets Partnership. The commitment remains modest: on capacity-building and experience-sharing, with no trading framework, targets or timeline. The Rio summit acknowledged the memorandum in 2025, and New Delhi has reiterated it. With India’s BRICS presidency entering its final quarter, operationalising the partnership requires not so much a common trading platform as a common rulebook. Eight BRICS members reportedly operate voluntary markets, and Brazil, China, India and Indonesia host over a third of the carbon credit projects registered worldwide. Compliance systems are maturing, too. China’s emissions trading system (ETS) — added steel, cement and aluminium through its 2024-25 allocation plan. India’s Carbon Credit Trading Scheme (CCTS) has notified emission-intensity targets for 490 entities across nine sectors and opened an offset mechanism. Brazil’s Law of 2024 establishes the Brazilian Greenhouse Gas Emissions Trading System (SBCE), a cap-and-trade system. However, none of these markets is linked to another. 267e6e0b1edf3f44.title: SC upholds states' power to levy additional tax on sales tax under pre-GST regime
267e6e0b1edf3f44.summary: NEW DELHI: The Supreme Court on Wednesday reaffirmed states’ power to impose an additional tax, surcharge or cess calculated on an existing sales tax, settling a legal question that had remained unresolved for nearly three decades. A seven-judge Constitution Bench upheld a 1974 judgment that recognized such levies as an exercise of states’ taxation powers under the pre-GST regime. A bench headed by Chief Justice Surya Kant held that an additional levy calculated as a percentage of the sales tax payable by a dealer amounts to an increase in the sales-tax rate. It therefore falls within Entry 54 of the State List, which empowered states to tax the sale or purchase of goods, other than inter-state sales, before the introduction of the goods and services tax (GST) in 2017. The ruling reaffirms the Supreme Court’s 1974 decision in S. Kodar vs State of Kerala , which upheld an additional sales tax imposed by Tamil Nadu on dealers whose annual turnover exceeded specified limits. The court had held that the levy, calculated as a percentage of sales tax payable, was an increase in the sales-tax rate rather than a tax on dealers’ income. Entry 54 provided the constitutional basis for states’ sales-tax powers before GST . Following the introduction of GST, states have retained the power to tax certain products outside its ambit, including petrol, diesel, crude oil , natural gas, aviation turbine fuel and alcoholic liquor for human consumption. In a concurring judgment, Justice K.V. Viswanathan said Kodar was correctly decided and remained good law, requiring no reconsideration. The bench also held that there was no conflict between Kodar and the Supreme Court’s 1983 judgment in Hoechst Pharmaceuticals, which had upheld a similar surcharge on sales tax. The court observed that the broader reference had become academic following the introduction of GST in 2017 and subsequent changes to the constitutional provisions and state taxation laws. A former public health official who has never held elected office, he rose from a double-digit defeat in Michigan's Democratic gubernatorial primary eight years ago to win a seat in the US Senate. El-Sayed overcame massive outside spending in both the Democratic primary and general election with a grassroots campaign built around universal health care, removing outside money from elections and sharp criticism of Israel. And, some more mandals in the two districts received very heavy rainfall between 150 mm and 204 mm. Of the two, Bhadradri Kothagudem did not get a break from the extremely heavy rain on Wednesday as a mandal there received 278.5 mm, as per Telangana Development Planning Society’s rainfall data till 8.00 p.m. The highest of 278.5 mm in Aswaraopet was followed by 188.3 mm in Malkaram in Dammapeta mandal, 175 mm in Ankampalem in Dammapeta and 149.8 mm in Mulakalapally. India Meteorological Department-Hyderabad Centres in its impact weather bulletin issued at 11 a.m. has placed Bhadradri Kothagudem under orange alert indicating heavy to very heavy rain on Wednesday. Moderate to heavy rain was predicted in Mulugu and Khammam. The highest amount of rainfall in Khammam was 13.5 mm in JVR OCP I&II, 6.3 mm in Pedapalli and 4.5 mm in Mancherial. The highest of 235 mm in Mulakapalle of Bhadradri Kothagudem was followed by 204.7 mm in Vemsoor of Khammam, as per Telangana Development Planning Society’s latest weather report issued in the morning on Wednesday (November 4, 2026). Of the two, Bhadradri Kothagudem did not get a break from the extremely heavy rain on Wednesday as a mandal there received 278.5 mm, as per Telangana Development Planning Society’s rainfall data till 8.00 p.m. The highest of 278.5 mm in Aswaraopet was followed by 188.3 mm in Malkaram in Dammapeta mandal, 175 mm in Ankampalem in Dammapeta and 149.8 mm in Mulakalapally. India Meteorological Department-Hyderabad Centres in its impact weather bulletin issued at 11 a.m. has placed Bhadradri Kothagudem under orange alert indicating heavy to very heavy rain on Wednesday. Moderate to heavy rain was predicted in Mulugu and Khammam. The highest amount of rainfall in Khammam was 13.5 mm in JVR OCP I&II, 6.3 mm in Pedapalli and 4.5 mm in Mancherial. The highest of 235 mm in Mulakapalle of Bhadradri Kothagudem was followed by 204.7 mm in Vemsoor of Khammam, as per Telangana Development Planning Society’s latest weather report issued in the morning on Wednesday (November 4, 2026). 46c2bf304f6451ed.title: Iran exempts Indian ships from Hormuz curbs, citing medicine imports
46c2bf304f6451ed.summary: Iran has exempted commercial ships from four countries, including India and China, from transit restrictions in the Strait of Hormuz, a top Iranian official has said, amid continued attacks on vessels attempting to cross the strategic waterway. Amir Hayat Moghadam, Deputy Chairman of the Iranian Parliament's National Security and Foreign Policy Committee, made the announcement in an interview with the Iranian Students' News Agency (ISNA) on Tuesday. "We have currently exempted four countries - India, China, Iraq and Qatar - from transit restrictions in the Strait of Hormuz. Ships from these countries pass freely, and the Americans do not intercept them either," he was quoted as saying by the semi-official news agency. Moqaddam said the exemptions were based on specific considerations and mutual interests. He said that facilitating the passage of Indian ships was intended to allow imports of medicines from India, while the exemption for Chinese vessels was intended to secure Beijing

4f0905bdfb61cff0.title: Class 3 student dies after collapsing in classroom, police register case
4f0905bdfb61cff0.summary: Published - November 05, 2026 04:30 am IST A nine-year-old Class 3 student died after collapsing inside her classroom at a school in Mayur Vihar, east Delhi, on Wednesday morning. The police have registered a case under Section 194 of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita in connection with the death and examined the CCTV footage to ascertain the circumstances leading to the incident. The incident occurred around 9.20 a.m., when the girl returned to her classroom after a sports period and collapsed while standing in front of her class teacher, Deputy Commissioner of Police (East District) Rajeev Kumar said. According to the police, a Police Control Room (PCR) call reporting the incident was received around 9.52 a.m. The school authorities rushed her to Vimla Devi Hospital and subsequently shifted her to Malik Radix Health Care in Nirman Vihar, where she was declared brought dead. The CCTV footage showed the girl attempting to approach her class teacher before suddenly collapsing. The teacher immediately rushed to her aid and tried to make her sit on a chair, while other students gathered around her. Some of her classmates rushed out to alert the school authorities. The victim’s family alleged that she was not given timely medical attention or CPR. The police, however, clarified that CCTV footage showed the teacher attending to her immediately. School principal Dr. Bhavna said the hospital informed the school authorities that the girl had suffered a cardiac arrest. She added that the school staff had also informed the girl’s family members. a98e4d254a85d381.title: Mobile orthopaedic and spine care unit launched
a98e4d254a85d381.summary: Updated - November 05, 2026 12:48 am IST It will facilitate the early assessment of conditions such as arthritis, osteoporosis, fractures, and spinal disorders. Kauvery Hospital Vadapalani, in collaboration with Hexaware Technologies, launched a Mobile Orthopaedic and Spine Care Unit, as part of a Corporate Social Responsibility initiative to extend specialised orthopaedic and spine care to rural and remote communities. The unit is equipped with a digital X-ray system, which is provided with an onboard reader and Bone Mineral Density (BMD) assessment facilities. The initiative places special emphasis on senior citizens, people with mobility limitations, as well as those facing challenges in travelling to hospitals for medical consultations and investigations. It will facilitate the early assessment of conditions such as arthritis, osteoporosis, fractures, and spinal disorders. Digital X-rays will help doctors evaluate bone and joint conditions, fractures, and spinal abnormalities, while BMD assessments will help identify individuals who are at risk of low bone density and osteoporosis, according to a press release. 6afd482cd8ed8670.title: Celebrations among NDA alliance leaders after landslide victory
6afd482cd8ed8670.summary: Published - November 05, 2026 01:22 am IST - VIJAYAWADA Celebrations broke out among NDA alliance leaders and workers in Vijayawada following the alliance’s emphatic victory in the Vijayawada Municipal Corporation elections. MP Kesineni Sivanath, East MLA Gadde Ramamohan, NTR district parliamentary constituency in-charge M. Mallikarjuna Rao, BJP NTR district president Gadde Anuradha and others participated in the programme. They felicitated the newly-elected Mayor Vangaveeti Radha Krishna on Wednesday. Speaking on the occasion, Mr. Sivanath pointed out that people have demonstrated their confidence in the NDA alliance through the election results. Despite the relatively low voter turnout, people had given the alliance such a decisive mandate, he said. The MP said the victory had placed greater responsibility on the alliance and assured that they would live up to people’s expectations by developing Vijayawada in all sectors. The MP said the delay in finalising seat-sharing arrangements within the alliance and certain other factors had cost them victory in another three to four divisions. He said they were always willing to consider constructive suggestions from anyone, including former IPS officer A.B. Venkateswara Rao, if they were beneficial to the people and the party. Later, Mr. Radha Krishna expressed his gratitude to Jana Sena Party president and Deputy Chief Minister Pawan Kalyan for giving him the opportunity to serve as Mayor and to Chief Minister N. Chandrababu Naidu for encouraging him. He also thanked the people of Vijayawada for their confidence in him. They expressed confidence that the city would be transformed into a developed urban centre by prioritising infrastructure, sanitation, drinking water supply, roads and the resolution of public grievances, in line with the hopes and aspirations of Vijayawada residents. flags: UAPA was enacted in 1967, but Section 51A does not exist in the original 1967 act; the Unlawful Activities (Prevention) Act was amended in 2019, and Section 51A is not a standard section number associated with UAPA implementation in this context.
UNSC Resolution 1988 was adopted in 2011, but the phrasing '1988(2011)' is non-standard; typically, resolutions are cited by year and number (e.g., Res. 1988 (2011)).
SEBI (Securities and Exchange Board of India) does not implement UAPA or manage UN sanctions lists; this is the responsibility of the Ministry of Home Affairs and the UN Security Council.
The title conflates unrelated legal and regulatory bodies (UAPA, UNSC, SEBI) in a way that is factually incoherent.

f5694e718054dbc5.title: Police ARSI suspended for allegedly reporting for duty drunk, misbehaving with public
f5694e718054dbc5.summary: Published - November 05, 2026 12:57 am IST - Bengaluru The public also demanded that the officer undergo an alcohol breathalyser test to establish whether he was drunk while on duty. | Image for representational purposes only | Photo Credit: File photo An Assistant Reserve Sub-Inspector (ARSI) attached to the CAR Western Squad has been placed under immediate suspension following allegations of misconduct while allegedly under the influence of alcohol during bandobast duty within the limits of Annapoorneshwari Nagar Police Station. The suspended officer has been identified as Gopal B. Rathod. According to sources, members of the public objected to his behaviour after noticing that he was allegedly intoxicated. A heated argument ensued, which escalated when some people allegedly roughed him up before handing him over to Hoysala patrolling police personnel. The public also demanded that the officer undergo an alcohol breathalyser test to establish whether he was drunk while on duty. One of the people present recorded the incident on a mobile phone and circulated the video on social media, tagging the Home Minister and the Bengaluru City Police Commissioner and demanding action against the officer. The video and the incident reportedly caused embarrassment among senior police officials, who directed the jurisdictional Deputy Commissioner of Police (DCP) to conduct an inquiry and initiate strict action. Following the incident, Gopal B. Rathod was placed under immediate suspension pending a departmental inquiry. 4395ff41a3d444f2.title: Police Inspector awarded two-month imprisonment in contempt case
4395ff41a3d444f2.summary: Published - November 05, 2026 12:58 am IST - HYDERABAD The Telangana High Court awarded two-month imprisonment to a police officer of the rank of Inspector, holding him guilty in a contempt of court case. Justice C.V. Bhaskar Reddy of the HC also imposed a fine of ₹ 2,000 on Inspector M. Prem Kumar. The sentence, however, was suspended for two weeks providing an opportunity to the Inspector for an appeal. The contempt case was filed by A. Sekhar Babu and seven others contending that the Inspector failed to provide aid to protect their plots despite specific orders from the HC - passed in 2023. The petitioners, majority of them senior citizens, stated that despite a specific direction from a single judge of the HC to provide protection to them from illegal interference by three persons (who were made respondents in the writ petition), the then Station House Officer Prem Kumar failed to act. The Inspector contended that he had no knowledge of the earlier order of the HC in the matter. “However, the absence of prior knowledge of the an order cannot justify inaction. It was incumbent upon him to examine the order and take appropriate steps in accordance with law to ensure its implementation,” the judge noted. f86538e708eec70e.title: Police seize 72 kg of ganja, gutka in Vellore, Tirupattur
f86538e708eec70e.summary: Published - November 05, 2026 12:54 am IST - VELLORE Searches, using sniffer dogs, were held at public places such as railway station on Wednesday. | Photo Credit: Special Arrangement In a special drive, the District Police in Vellore and Tirupattur have seized 72 kilograms of ganja and gukta in various public places and arrested six drug peddlers on Wednesday. The police identified the arrested persons as Rajesh Kumar, 32, Ali Khan, 52, Suresh, 37, Akbar, 53, Harish, 35, and Balaraman, 65. They belonged to Vellore and Tirupattur. Based on orders of Superintendent of Police N.U. Sivaraman and Akshay Anil Wakhare of Vellore and Tirupattur districts respectively, special teams were formed to conduct surprise checks at public places in these districts. The police said sniffer dogs were also roped in during searches at railway stations, bus termini, and other public places during the day-long drive. The teams seized 35 kg of ganja and 37 kg of gukta in these two districts. The police said most of the contraband were sourced from agents in Andhra Pradesh, for sale in industrial regions such as Ranipet, Sriperambadur, Vaniyambadi, Ambur, Vellore and Cheyyar. Cases were registered and arrested persons were lodged in prison. A probe is under way. db9af969a6cac92d.title: Two 17-year-old students sexually assaulted at party, two booked under PoCSO
db9af969a6cac92d.summary: Published - November 05, 2026 01:02 am IST - HYDERABAD Two 17-year-old girl students were allegedly sexually assaulted after being made to consume alcohol at a party in Balanagar on the night of October 1. Police have registered a case under the Protection of Children from Sexual Offences (POCSO) Act against two youths in connection with the incident. The suspects have been identified as Ganesh alias Ghana, 19, and Tarun, 26, who is married. Ganesh was in a relationship with one of the victims and had invited her to the party. She took a friend along with her. According to Madhura Nagar police Inspector H. Prabhakar, after taking the two students to the venue, the youths allegedly made them consume alcohol before sexually assaulting them. “The students had consumed one beer each. One of the victims later fell unwell and was taken to a hospital, where suspicion arose of a possible sexual assault,” said the officer, adding that when questioned, the students disclosed what had happened. Their statements were subsequently recorded at a Bharosa Centre. The students were admitted to a hospital in Madhuranagar following the incident. They later approached the Madhuranagar police and lodged a complaint, based on which a case was registered and an investigation taken up. The case will be transferred to Balanagar police on jurisdictional grounds. 6660dd9e7606f22f.title: RBI starts 3 surveys to capture inflation expectations, consumer confidence
6660dd9e7606f22f.summary: Reserve Bank on Tuesday announced three key surveys to capture inflation expectations of households and gauge consumer confidence in the country- the studies that provide input for bi-monthly monetary policy. The central bank has announced the launch of the November 2026 round of the Inflation Expectations Survey of Households (IESH). "The November 2026 round of the survey is being launched. The survey aims at capturing subjective assessments on price movements and inflation, based on their individual consumption baskets," it said. The study will be conducted across 19 cities -- Ahmedabad, Bengaluru, Bhopal, Bhubaneswar, Chandigarh, Chennai, Delhi, Guwahati, Hyderabad, Jaipur, Jammu, Kolkata, Lucknow, Mumbai, Nagpur, Patna, Raipur, Ranchi and Thiruvananthapuram. In another statement, the RBI said the Urban Consumer Confidence Survey seeks qualitative responses from households regarding their sentiments on the general economic situation, employment scenario, price level, households'

Velu for the party’s Northern Zone Youth Wing Conference held on December 14, 2025. cb6a087f49e6adf0.summary: The changes form part of the Foreign Exchange Management (Export and Import of Goods and Services) which came into effect from October 1, 2026. Under the amended regulations, a resident individual exporting services will be deemed to have submitted the Export Declaration Form, or EDF, once the individual provides the authorised dealer bank with the information required to credit the payment to the exporter's account. No transaction-value threshold has been prescribed for resident individuals.

b076dd70c49e380d.title: In Tehran, a search for the future of West Asian security
b076dd70c49e380d.summary: Updated - November 04, 2026 01:26 am IST ‘Saudi Arabia, Türkiye and Pakistan travelling to Iran for this exchange came as a surprise to many given that Tehran had struck several Arab countries in response to American and Israeli aggression’ | Photo Credit: AP More than eight months after the United States and Israel launched strikes on Iran , West Asia remains on tenterhooks, as the United States, Israel, and Iran continue to flirt with a resumption of military hostilities. Elections in Israel as well as the U.S. midterm polls offered an interesting pause, even as war rhetoric remained high. Amid these tensions, an alliance of Saudi Arabia, Türkiye and Pakistan, known as the “Mecca Agreement”, arrived in Iran’s capital in October to discuss regional security. A large part of Iran’s response since the U.S. and Israel began bombing the country in February 2026 has been to target American interests, including data centres, and military installations across the Gulf states. This forms part of Tehran’s strategy of asymmetric warfare, shaped by its view of the conflict as an existential threat to the Islamic Republic, particularly following the killing of Supreme Leader Ayatollah Ali Khamenei in an airstrike. 0341b26a696066b0.title: On the Arunachal frontier, silence is not a strategy
0341b26a696066b0.summary: Updated - November 04, 2026 01:18 am IST ‘Candour will strengthen New Delhi’s hand in dealing with Beijing’ | Photo Credit: THE HINDU/RITU RAJ KONWAR For some time, reports have circulated of transgressions by China’s People’s Liberation Army (PLA) in the Asaphila, Taksing and Longju areas of Arunachal Pradesh. The facts are neither clear nor officially acknowledged. Yet, there are signals that something out of the ordinary is happening along this stretch of the border. The matter warrants close attention. The clearest signal came on October 22, 2026. Speaking at an Indo-Tibetan Border Police (ITBP) function, Director General Shatrujeet Singh Kapoor said: “In the past few days, a situation arose where face-off happened at several locations in Arunachal and it still continues.” This was the first official confirmation of the scale of the problem. This daily reported, citing “government sources”, that the two sides had been in a stand-off at Asaphila, near Taksing, since late July. These changes aim to reduce conflicts of interest associated with higher commission payments in regular plans.

fd0d1593764da810.title: Coming of age: On the Binance hack
fd0d1593764da810.summary: Updated - November 04, 2026 12:58 am IST The recent hack at Binance, the biggest theft ever at the world’s largest cryptocurrency exchange, has lessons for India. But Indian policymakers must be careful to learn the right ones. First, it must be understood that the hack is not an indictment of the crypto space itself . Being a crypto exchange did not make Binance more vulnerable than if it were, say, a bank. Hacking is now a daily occurrence across sectors and even small pharmaceutical companies often have to fend off millions of attacks a month. Of course, Binance must look into how it was hacked and prevent a recurrence, but the cat-and-mouse game between hackers and security software developers is a perpetual one. For every million, or even billion, attacks that are stopped, one will inevitably get through. The lesson for Indian policymakers is not that crypto is unsafe in itself; this incident does not prove that. Rather, it is about how Binance prepared for and reacted to the attack. Back in 2018, Binance had set up an emergency fund called the Secure Asset Fund for Users (SAFU) to protect user assets in the event of a security breach or platform-level incident. The fund was created for exactly this kind of incident, and was financed through trading fees that Binance collects from users. Since the $6.3 billion worth of assets stolen exceeded the SAFU’s resources, Binance dipped into its own resources to restore about 95% of users’ assets within four days of the hack. So, Binance used a stable source of revenue to finance an emergency fund, which it deployed when an emergency occurred. The system worked perfectly, also showing how maturely and responsibly the crypto space can be run. The Indian government and the Reserve Bank of India still view the private crypto space as the Wild West of techno-finance. This is no longer the case. Large crypto companies are employing prudential practices, safeguarding customers, and cooperating with law enforcement agencies. I

ea8eeda99dc14955.title: Business, unusual: On engaging with the Myanmar junta
ea8eeda99dc14955.summary: Updated - November 04, 2026 12:54 am IST Months after a sham election that installed junta chief Min Aung Hlaing as Myanmar’s civilian President, the military continues to wage war on its own people even as the world has largely looked away. More than a lakh people are estimated to have died since the 2021 coup, many in fighting between the junta and the anti-coup People’s Defence Forces and ethnic armed organisations. The junta has also killed thousands of civilians in air strikes on villages in rebel-held areas to terrorise communities into giving up their resistance. With wars affecting Ukraine, Gaza, Sudan and Yemen, and Iran, the world has grown numb to such violence. The junta has exploited that indifference and a shifting geopolitical situation to act with impunity. Russia and China, its principal arms suppliers, have stood by it with the former supplying jets that were used to bomb civilians. Beijing, which tacitly allowed three ethnic armed organisations to launch an offensive in Shan and Rakhine States in late 2023, has since pressured two of them into ceasefires and returning seized territory. It also backed the January election. Since being sworn in, Min Aung Hlaing has visited India , Thailand, Vietnam and three other ASEAN member-states. ASEAN still swears by its Five-Point Consensus, which calls for an end to violence and dialogue. Yet, its members seem more than eager to do business with a regime that has flouted every point. Meanwhile, U.S. officials reportedly held secret talks with the junta in Tokyo in June and October, and a senior delegation met Min Aung Hlaing in Naypyidaw in September. Japan is reportedly pressing the Financial Action Task Force to take Myanmar off its blacklist. The motives are not hard to understand. China wants an outlet to the Indian Ocean and security for its oil and gas pipelines. The police, along with Delhi Fire Services officials, are inspecting the proposed premises, verifying applicants’ credentials and checking ownership or tenancy documents. Malik said Fire Department officials would assess whether the premises were accessible to firefighting vehicles and complied with fire safety requirements. “Temporary sheds must be made of non-flammable material, with at least three metres between sheds and 50 metres from protected works (such as residential buildings, educational institutions, hospitals, places of worship, markets and other public spaces). Balakrishna lashed out at senior Congress leader and MLA K.N. Rajanna on Tuesday, saying he was free to quit the party if he so wished, and accusing him of “betraying the party while being part of it.” This comes against the backdrop of Mr. Rajanna’s son and MLC R. Rajendra recently meeting JD(S) leader and Union Minister H.D. Kumaraswamy. Speaking to reporters in Chitradurga, he said, “If Mr. Rajanna wants to leave the party and join another party, he is free to do so. If the Congress party does not pay attention to such issues, it may have to face serious problems in the future. Mr. Rajanna is betraying the party while remaining in it. Ragesh People who visited the Kozhikode Corporation office or those who strolled through the nearby beach on Tuesday morning were perhaps amused by the songs emerging from a ‘pandal’ outside the gate. 3d972eaddd00d5f1.title: Man undergoing de-addiction treatment dies at private clinic in Kodungaiyur
3d972eaddd00d5f1.summary: Published - November 04, 2026 12:36 am IST - CHENNAI A 28-year-old man undergoing treatment for alcohol addiction at a private clinic in Kodungaiyur died on Monday. His family members alleged that medical negligence at the clinic led to his death. A senior police officer said, “We have registered a case of unnatural death. Further action will be taken only after receiving the post-mortem and viscera examination reports.” The deceased was identified as Lokesh, 28, Lokesh was assisting his father in real estate business. He had recently developed an addiction to alcohol. His family admitted him to a private de-addiction clinic in Moolakadai last week within the jurisidiction of Kodungaiyur police. A staff member at the clinic administered him an injection after his health condition deteriorated. As his condition worsened, his family members rushed him to another private hospital in Madhavaram, where doctors declared him brought dead. His body was subsequently brought back to the clinic in Moolakadai. Following this, his relatives and family members staged a protest outside the clinic, accusing its staff of negligence. Police personnel intervened and pacified them after receiving a complaint. The body was sent to Government Stanley Hospital for post-mortem examination. e971873e9869d8c6.title: Bengaluru: South corporation shuts 63 commercial establishments in residential layouts
e971873e9869d8c6.summary: Published - November 04, 2026 12:42 am IST - Bengaluru The Corporation sealed the highest number of establishments in the BTM Layout Assembly constituency, where 30 shops were shut. | Photo Credit: Image for representational purpose The Bengaluru South City Corporation has sealed 63 commercial establishments operating “illegally” in residential areas across its jurisdiction during a special enforcement drive conducted by officials. The Corporation sealed the highest number of establishments in the BTM Layout Assembly constituency, where 30 shops were shut. This was followed by 10 in the Bengaluru South constituency, nine in Bommanahalli, eight in Padmanabhanagar, four in Jayanagar, and two within the limits of the Anekal Assembly constituency (part of which falls under the South City Corporation). According to Corporation officials, the action targeted commercial establishments operating in residential areas in violation of regulations. Officials said they were causing inconvenience to residents and obstructing vehicular movement. Bakeries, eateries, condiment stores, salons, beauty parlours, fruit and vegetable outlets, hardware stores, and other commercial establishments were among those sealed. The Corporation said commercial establishments operating on roads narrower than 40 feet in residential areas were prohibited. However, several establishments had continued operations without valid trade licences despite being issued notices and instructions to vacate. The drive was conducted simultaneously across several wards in Kumaraswamy Layout, J.P. Nagar, Madiwala, Koramangala, Ejipura, Jakkasandra, Begur, Singasandra, Yelachenahalli, Uttarahalli, Gottigere, Bilekahalli and Arakere, among others. Commissioner K.N. Ramesh warned of strict legal action against establishments operating illegally or without the necessary licences. 2fec4d1b944ad2de.title: SRMIST to open SRMJEE applications from November 4
2fec4d1b944ad2de.summary: Published - November 04, 2026 05:30 am IST - Chennai SRM Institute of Science and Technology (SRMIST) will open applications for SRM Joint Entrance Examination (SRMJEE) for all courses on November 4. Applications will be available from 2 p.m. on the website www.srmist.edu.in for Engineering and Technology, Architecture, Management, Liberal Arts and Business Studies, Law, Medicine and Health Sciences, Hotel Management, and Agricultural Sciences programmes. The SRMJEE for undergraduate and postgraduate courses in engineering will be held in over 160 centres across the country. The first phase for the B.Tech, M.Tech, and M.Tech (integrated) engineering programmes will be held on April 17 and 18, 2027, and the last date to apply is April 2, 2027. The second phase will be held on June 19 and 20, 2027, and the last date to apply is June 4, 2027. SRM Law Entrance Test will be held between January 5, 2027 and June 30, 2027 through on-demand centre-based tests. The last date for applying is June 25, 2027. Students appearing for SRMJEE for Management can take the test online between January 11, 2027 and June 30, 2027 for which the last date for applying is June 25, 2027. Similarly, students appearing for SRMJEE for undergraduate and postgraduate courses in Health Sciences can take the test online in two phases. The first phase will be held on April 9 and 10, 2027, and the last date for application is April 4, 2027. The second phase will be held on June 11 and 12, 2027, and the last date to apply is June 6, 2027. For post-PG programmes, the exam will be held on April 9 and 10, 2027, and the last date for applying is April 4, 2027. SRMJEE toppers will receive Founder’s Scholarship that entails a 100% waiver of tuition and hostel fees. Besides, students will also be offered merit scholarships of 25% to 100% tuition fee waivers based on ranks across phases, subjects, and campus-specific criteria, according to a press release. c3ef18c2e0ed82e2.summary: Published - November 04, 2026 01:10 am IST - Bengaluru A candidate in Haveri, who was flagged for poor academic record and emerging as a topper in VAO exam, has now been found to have used a mobile phone during the exam. | Photo Credit: K. MURALI KUMAR Taking into account the irregularities reported at the Shiggaon examination centre of Haveri district in the Village Administrative Officer (VAO) recruitment examination recently, the Karnataka Examination Authority (KEA) has decided to introduce several additional security measures. A candidate in Haveri, who was flagged for poor academic record and emerging as a topper in VAO exam, has now been found to have used a mobile phone during the exam. Haveri police are probing the case now. To prevent such instances, from now on, two invigilators will be appointed for every examination hall. One invigilator will stand at the rear of the hall to monitor candidates, while the other will remain at the front. They will also be responsible for ensuring that the mobile signal jammer in the examination centre is functioning properly. Although candidates are required to undergo thorough frisking before entering the examination centre, it was found that this rule had not been implemented seriously. Therefore, KEA has decided to conduct a second round of checking inside the examination hall as well. All candidates must reach the examination centre at least 30 minutes before the examination begins. Candidates arriving at the last minute will not be permitted to enter, H. Prasanna, Executive Director, KEA said. “Instructions have already been issued to establish district-level monitoring systems to oversee examination centres through webcasting. Going forward, KEA has also decided to appoint a separate invigilator at each examination centre to monitor CCTV footage,” he added. f678e794988cf1e5.title: Security guard dies in fire at Peravallur warehouse
f678e794988cf1e5.summary: Published - November 04, 2026 12:38 am IST - CHENNAI A 54-year-old security guard died of suffocation after a fire broke out at an e-commerce warehouse on SRP Koil Road in Peravallur on Tuesday morning. The warehouse, located on the first floor of a building, had been rented by an online delivery company to store goods ordered by customers. It had been functioning for the past two years. The fire broke out around 6.30 a.m. when the warehouse was closed. Ramamoorthy, 54, a security guard on duty, noticed thick smoke billowing out and entered the premises to locate the source of the fire. However, the blaze spread rapidly, trapping him inside. He collapsed due to suffocation. Fire and Rescue Services personnel from Kolathur and Sembium rushed to the spot and put out the fire. They rescued Ramamoorthy and took him to Periyar Nagar Government Hospital, where doctors declared him dead. Peravallur police have registered a case and are investigating the cause of the fire. An electrical short circuit is suspected to have triggered the blaze. ff01b48fc3db8bdb.title: RPF head constable saves passenger from being dragged by train at Perambur railway station
ff01b48fc3db8bdb.summary: Published - November 04, 2026 12:33 am IST - CHENNAI A Railway Protection Force (RPF) head constable saved a 23-year-old passenger from being dragged along by a moving train at the Perambur railway station on Tuesday. The incident occurred when Train No. 12672 Nilgiri Superfast Express was departing from Platform 1. Mohammed Kajim Alam, who realised that he had boarded the wrong train, attempted to alight while it was moving. He lost his balance, clung to the grab rails near the coach doorway, and was dragged on the platform. Noticing the danger, RPF head constable Bhagchand Meena came to his rescue and pulled him away from the moving train, averting a possible tragedy. The passenger’s brother subsequently pulled the alarm chain, bringing the train to a halt. Prime Minister Shah is likely to visit India in the last week of November, his first bilateral trip after assuming office in March, according to Foreign Ministry sources here. The dates of the visit are yet to be announced officially. Foreign Secretary Misri is paying an official visit to Nepal from November 4-5 at the invitation of Nepal's Foreign Secretary Amrit Bahadur Rai, the Foreign Ministry here said in a statement. During the visit, the foreign secretary will hold bilateral discussions with his Indian counterpart, it said. The two sides will review the full range of Nepal-India relations and exchange views on matters of mutual interest, with a view to further strengthening the long-standing close and friendly ties between the two countries, the ministry said. Misri will also pay courtesy

e1174ed557d93b84.title: 7,000 kg of unhygienic, foul-smelling khoya seized, destroyed: Delhi CMO
e1174ed557d93b84.summary: Published - November 04, 2026 03:49 am IST - New Delhi Chief Minister Rekha Gupta said the government would not compromise on public health. File photo: X/@gupta_rekha via ANI. The Food Safety Department of the Delhi government carried out an inspection at Mori Gate Khoya Market on Tuesday (November 3, 2026) and seized and destroyed about 7,000 kg of unhygienic and foul-smelling khoya, taking the total quantity of khoya destroyed by the department so far to 10,660 kg, the Chief Minister’s Office (CMO) said. Chief Minister Rekha Gupta said the government would not compromise on public health, and ensuring that people have access to safe and quality food during the festive season is one of the government’s foremost responsibilities. “Those involved in food adulteration, regardless of how influential they may be, will be brought within the ambit of the law and face strict action,” she said. Also, 35 of 44 samples of khoya failed preliminary tests at the ‘Food Safety on Wheels’ mobile testing facility. Two additional samples were also collected and sent to a laboratory for detailed examination. “The preliminary tests conducted at the site also brought to light information relating to milk powder, vanaspati and substances used for binding in the suspected material. Samples have been sent to the laboratory for further investigation into these ingredients,” an official statement said. The Food Safety Department has been conducting sustained drives against food adulteration in view of the festive season. As part of the action taken so far, the department destroyed 2,830 kg of khoya on September 4, 610 kg on September 8 and 520 kg on October 23, as per the CMO. flags: Anachronism: The 2024 US midterm elections occurred in November 2024, but Donald Trump was not the incumbent president facing a 'verdict' in that election; he was a former president and the Republican nominee for the 2024 presidential election (which took place in November 2024, not midterms). Midterms are held in even years not divisible by 4 (e.g., 2022, 2026).

Factual Error: The 2022 midterm elections were seen as a verdict on President Biden, not Trump. The 2018 midterms were a verdict on Trump, but the context of 'Iran war' and 'rising fuel costs' does not align with the primary narratives of 2018 (which focused on healthcare, trade, and Trump's first term).

Contextual Mismatch: There was no active 'Iran war' during the 2022 or 2018 US midterm election cycles. While tensions existed, a full-scale war was not a defining feature of those specific midterm contests.

Source Mismatch: Business Standard is an Indian news outlet. While they cover US news, the phrasing and specific combination of issues suggest a potential fabrication or a misdated/misattributed article.

74e5df1dfed40c77.title: Kasi, food for soul
74e5df1dfed40c77.summary: Published - November 04, 2026 04:49 am IST Kasi is often called Anna Kshetra since Goddess Annapoorani, an incarnation of Parvati, resides there permanently. Coming down to earth to undertake a penance for a playful sport with Siva leading to consequences, She chose Kasi at a time when the town was reeling under severe famine. Armed with a ladle and a pot, She brought back prosperity and stayed on, heeding the local king’s request, and continued to bless devotees, said P. Swaminathan. The sacred town attracted saints, sages and ordinary devotees as well, especially around Deepavali. Long ago, Narayana Dikshitar, a staunch devotee who resided there, often invited holy men to his home and fed them humbly. On one occasion, after inviting a group of sadhus for a meal, he reached home only to find his wife bedridden. The guests were due in a couple of hours and a harassed Dikshitar went out seeking a solution. Just outside his house he spotted a woman walking past. Richly adorned, she had a talisman around her neck and a diamond nose ring. She looked at him kindly and the man blurted out his predicament. With a smile, she offered to help prepare the meal for the sadhus. The meal was a stupendous success and all the holy men blessed him. The woman had left the place after her duties and only then did Dikshitar realise that he had not even offered a meal to the woman who came to his aid. He went to bed with that thought and had a dream wherein he apologised to her and asked to see her; the woman declared that she was Annapoorani. She affirmed that She would always remain with those who have a good heart and a supplicatory mind. Informing him that She had left a green turban on the eastern wall of the house, She instructed Dikshitar to install her idol there. “I will remain here forever,” said Annapoorani. Visiting Kasi around Deepavali is considered highly efficacious. Published - November 04, 2026 04:49 am IST Terms & conditions | Institutional Subscriber Comments have to

1bceed40d8213fab.summary: Citing a World Bank report, Prime Minister Narendra Modi on Tuesday said around 50 crore people had been lifted out of extreme poverty in India over the last 10 to 12 years, noting that the fight against poverty was limited to "slogans" in the past. Modi doubled down on the development agenda; underlined "transformation" in urban transport infrastructure over the past 12 years, and maintained that empowering the poor and delivering good governance were hallmarks of his government. After inaugurating Pune Metro Line 3 (Pink Line) via video conferencing, Modi said India's operational metro network, which covered 248 km before 2014, now covers 1,200 km, and stressed that better urban infrastructure would accelerate the country's economic growth. The 23-km-long Pink Line, built at a cost of over Rs 8,300 crore, will connect the Hinjewadi IT hub to the District Court Metro station. It is expected to improve daily commutes for thousands of IT professionals, ease traffic congestion, and .

04fb5c818d6ed465.title: Fifty years ago | Carter elected President of U.S. in close contest
04fb5c818d6ed465.summary: Published - November 04, 2026 02:54 am IST Washington, November 3: Mr. Jimmy Carter, the peanut farmer from Georgia, who was a political unknown until early this year was elected the 39th President of the United States after he defeated the White House incumbent, Mr. Gerald Ford, in a closely fought election held yesterday. It was a remarkable achievement for a “rank outsider” who had started his quest for the Presidency two years ago, without much money, without a real political base and without going through the traditional corridors of power. To the loser, Mr. Ford, who was unexpectedly and accidentally elevated to the highest place in the land after Mr. Richard Nixon resigned 28 months ago, it was the end of a long but unspectacular career in politics. The quarterly profit included a deferred-tax credit of approximately Rs 244 crore, according to the company's audited financials seen by PTI. PRISM's revenue from operations increased 35 per cent to Rs 2,814 crore in the first quarter of FY2026-27, compared with Rs 2,078 crore in the corresponding quarter last year, the audited financials showed. The company's Gross Booking Value grew 30 per cent to nearly Rs 9,600 crore in the same period. Growth was broad-based across its hotels and vacation homes businesses. PRISM's hotel segment bookings grew 30 per cent year-on-year, while the vacation homes business recorded 28 per cent growth in bookings. According to Forbes' Real-Time Billionaires list, Ambani's wealth increased by 7.85 per cent, or USD 6.3 billion, making him the biggest gainer globally in the latest update to the ranking on November 2. The gain was substantially ahead of the second-biggest wealth accretion on the list, with Spanish retail billionaire Amancio Ortega adding USD 1.7 billion, followed by China's Zhong Shanshan at USD 1.5 billion. The gains pushed Ambani to No.23 spot on the world billionaire list, making him the richest Indian ahead of Gautam Adani, who was ranked at No.26 with a wealth of USD 79.12 billion, according to the Forbes listing. bf5ea52deba87aaa.title: IPO fundraising rises 30% to record ₹84,400 crore in H1FY27: Report
bf5ea52deba87aaa.summary: India's mainboard IPO market witnessed a record fund mobilisation at Rs 84,400 crore in the first half of FY27, registering a 30 per cent rise over the year-ago period, with nearly 94 per cent of the funds raised during the July-September period, according to a report by Grant Thornton Bharat. As many as 71 companies made their stock market debut during April-September 2026, compared with 55 in the corresponding period a year ago. According to the report, the funds raised increased from Rs 64,900 crore in H1 FY26 to Rs 84,400 crore in H1 FY27. The average listing-day gains improved to 18 per cent from 10 per cent a year ago, while average retail oversubscription increased to 28 times from 25 times, the report titled 'India IPO Market: H1 FY27 and Q2 FY27 Review' said. Notably, September was the busiest month, with 32 IPOs collectively raising Rs 40,400 crore. In terms of sectoral contribution, financial services accounted for 43 per cent of the total capital mobilised during H1 FY

As of 3 a.m., the inner spiral band in the northern sector has touched land, and the wall cloud region is also entering land, according to the official bulletin from the India Meteorological Department. The Leader of the Opposition in the Lok Sabha, Rahul Gandhi, on Monday (November 2, 2026) challenged Prime Minister Narendra Modi to an open debate , alleging that it was with “foreign help” that Mr. Modi became Prime Minister and continues to occupy the position. The Congress leader’s challenge came after the Prime Minister had accused the Opposition of taking foreign help to destabilise the country. Foreign social and home care workers, who arrived in the U.K. before May 2025, will be able to normally settle (become permanent residents) in five years , rather than in 15 years, as was first proposed in the British government’s ‘earned settlement’ scheme announced in November 2025. Those earning more than £50,271 per annum, doctors, nurses and teachers will be able to settle in five years, while those earning more than £1,25,140 per annum could settle in three years, as was proposed in the November 2025 draft rules. The Union government plans to establish Foreigners Regional Registration Offices (FRROs) in all State capitals by 2027, the Ministry of Home Affairs said on Monday (November 2, 2026). 92e91ead481f85e3.title: Amit Shah backs SIR, alleges 3 crore ‘illegal infiltrators’ identified in 13 crore deleted voters
92e91ead481f85e3.summary: Updated - November 03, 2026 01:48 am IST - HYDERABAD Union Home Minister Amit Shah addresses a public meeting during the ‘Save Democracy, Remove Anarchy’ campaign in Hyderabad on Monday (November 2). | Photo Credit: RAMAKRISHNA G Union Home Minister Amit Shah on Monday alleged that the Election Commission of India’s (ECI) Special Intensive Revision (SIR) exercise had identified around three crore ‘unaccounted voters’, whom he described as ‘illegal infiltrators from Bangladesh’, among the 13 crore names removed from electoral rolls. He asserted that all such infiltrators would be expelled from the country. Addressing a public meeting at MJ Market in Hyderabad’s Old City after a ‘Save democracy-Remove anarchy’ foot march , Mr. Shah claimed that of the nearly 13 crore names deleted from voter lists during the SIR process, 4.25 crore voters were registered in two different locations, three crore were deceased, and another one crore were duplicate entries. He questioned if such names should continue to remain on the electoral rolls. “Do we need to remove infiltrators from the country’s voter lists or not?” he asked. The Home Minister accused Congress leader Rahul Gandhi of defending the alleged three crore ‘unaccounted’ voters. “No matter how hard Rahul Gandhi or Chief Minister A. Revanth Reddy may try, the BJP is committed to driving every infiltrator out of the country,” he said. Mr. Shah alleged that the Congress and other Opposition parties were opposing the SIR exercise to protect ‘infiltrators from Bangladesh’, whom he described as their ‘vote bank’ and maintained that only genuine Indian citizens should be included in electoral rolls. Ridiculing Sunday’s joint rally of Opposition parties in New Delhi, Mr. Shah described it as a ‘Save Infiltrators’ rally and urged BJP workers to counter what he termed ‘fear-mongering’ by the former on the SIR exercise through a door-to-door campaign. The Congress was determined to halt SIR while the BJP would continue to support it

b850f1e5733062c8.title: Petronet LNG reports 52.3% growth in net profits, in talks for availing undelivered cargoes
b850f1e5733062c8.summary: Published - November 03, 2026 05:43 am IST Petronet LNG declared a dividend of ₹7 per equity share. | Photo Credit: The Hindu State-owned Petronet LNG reported 53.2% growth in net profits in the September-end quarter, driven by improved operational efficiency, although cargoes from its most prominent supplier, Qatar, continued to be affected because of the reignited conflict in West Asia. The company also declared a dividend of ₹7 per equity share. The country’s largest LNG importer’s net profit stood at ₹1,235 crore in the reported quarter against ₹806 crore in the same period last year. Revenue from operations although declined about 35% during the period to ₹7,200.35 crore. The company processed 231 trillion British Thermal Units (TBTU) during the period, higher than 228 TBTU it processed in the same period last year. Overall capacity utilisation in the reported quarter narrowed to 64% against 78% in the same period last year. Capacity utilisation at their Dahej terminal stood at 73% against 92% in the comparable period last year. Speaking to the press, Akshay Kumar Singh, Chairman and Managing Director (CMD) informed that the company was also in talks with QatarEnergy to secure delivery of the cargoes that could not be delivered because of the force majeure. “On the sidelines, we also discuss if they would be able to give more cargoes before the contractual date. If there is a requirement in the country, we will take that as well,” he said. The supplier has declared forced majeure until December-end. Mr. Singh told reporters that the contractual terms have provisions to recoup the lost cargoes for one year after the expiry of the current contract period, that is, May 2028. He stated that Petronet LNG lost an average 9-10 cargoes each month in the last eight months, thus, about 75-80 cargoes whilst it has received 6 cargoes from the supplier. The united outcry of protest by the Opposition, led by the Leader of Opposition Rahul Gandhi , is a strong signal of public opinion for the ruling party and India’s institutions, including the ECI, that appear complicit in a scheme that threatens the foundations of Indian democracy. What remains unexplained by the ECI and Mr. Kumar are malpractices in the Special Intensive Revision that could have the effect of subverting the popular will. Protestors on Sunday had arrived from all parts of India, and included people directly affected by the SIR across the country. The protest reinforced Mr. Gandhi’s central role as the key challenger of Prime Minister Narendra Modi. Mr. Gandhi, for all his faults, has been an uncompromising champion of constitutional values and pluralism in India. The BJP caricatured him, and even non-BJP voices had bought into the idea of Mr. Gandhi being a privileged dynast out of touch with the commoner. While his ancestry is a matter of fact, so is his tenacity. All Opposition parties mobilised for the protest, but the centrality of the Congress party was unmistakable. Mr. Gandhi has a special focus on subaltern classes to be included in positions of responsibility in the party. The Sunday protest was clearly the largest show of strength in recent memory. 478c19867d6818b6.title: Cyclonic storm Murasu to make landfall close to Ongole
478c19867d6818b6.summary: Updated - November 03, 2026 02:42 am IST - VIJAYAWADA A satellite image of Cyclone Murasu over the Bay of Bengal on Sunday. IMD | Photo Credit: Special Arrangement As the cyclonic storm, Cyclone Murasu , moves towards the A.P. coast, the State has deployed six National Disaster Response Force (NDRF) teams and seven State Disaster Response Force (SDRF) teams in districts likely to be affected by the cyclone. According to information from the A.P. State Disaster Management Authority (APSDMA), the landfall point is likely to be Ongole and in this connection, two teams each have been stationed in the districts of Krishna, Bapatla, Guntur, Nellore and Prakasam, while one team each has been deployed in Markapuram, Palnadu and Tirupati districts. Additional teams are also available for deployment if required. Murasu is the second cyclonic storm to hit A.P. in less than a week. According to the 9 p.m. bulletin from the India Meteorological Department (IMD), the cyclonic storm centred over Southwest and adjoining Westcentral Bay of Bengal at 5.30 p.m. It was located about 420 km east-southeast of Chennai, 490 km east-southeast of Nellore, 500 km southeast of Machilipatnam, 510 east-southeast of Kavali, 530 km southeast of Ongole and 560 km south-southeast of Vishakhapatnam. The IMD said the system may intensify further into a Severe Cyclonic Storm over Westcentral Bay of Bengal in the early hours of November 2. The landfall will be close to the Ongole coast, with a wind speed of 100 to 120 kmph, in the early hours of November 3. Isolated extremely heavy rainfall is expected at one or two locations in the districts of Krishna, Guntur, Bapatla, Prakasam, Markapuram and Nellore on Monday. NTR and Guntur districts have announced holidays for all government and private schools, junior colleges and degree colleges on Monday (November 2, 2026). 9c21bc940db95f10.summary: A federal judge on Monday dismissed a lawsuit against Harvard University over its alleged failure to provide admissions records that the Justice Department had demanded to ensure the Ivy League school stopped using affirmative action in admissions. The Justice Department said Harvard had "thwarted" efforts to investigate potential discrimination. It accused Harvard of refusing to comply with a federal investigation and asked a judge to order the university to turn over the records. But US District Judge Myong Joun concluded that the Justice Department didn't take the necessary procedural steps to obtain the data before filing the lawsuit. "Before taking enforcement action under the statutory framework, the agency must advise the recipient of its failure to comply and determine that compliance cannot be secured by voluntary means," Joun wrote. 69f62dc9701a46b5.title: Craft Council of A.P. receives praise for providing platform for weavers, artisans
69f62dc9701a46b5.summary: Updated - November 03, 2026 12:36 am IST - VIJAYAWADA Heritage Foods executive director Nara Brahmani examines a saree at a stall after inaugurating ‘Vasantam’ crafts and textiles exhibition in Vijayawada on Monday. | Photo Credit: K.V.S. Giri The Craft Council of Andhra Pradesh (CCAP) inaugurated ‘Vasantham’, an exhibition showcasing the rich heritage of handlooms, handicrafts and traditional crafts of India, in Vijayawada on Monday. Heritage Foods executive director Nara Brahmani visited the exhibition and interacted with the weavers and artisans, and appreciated the efforts of the Craft Council of A.P. in organising the exhibition. She also commended the initiative for providing a valuable platform to weavers and artisans to showcase their products, reach customers and promote their traditional crafts. She said that such exhibitions were extremely beneficial in supporting the weaving community and encouraging the preservation of our rich craft heritage. The two-day exhibition will conclude on November 3 (Tuesday). It remains open from 10 a.m. to 8 p.m. at Sesha Sai Kalyana Mandapam, Vedika in the city. e9958b1c4de528c6.title: Police foil bid to snatch smuggled gold from woman at Karipur
e9958b1c4de528c6.summary: Updated - November 03, 2026 08:23 am IST File photo for representational purpose only. The police foiled an attempt to abduct a woman carrying 817 gm gold worth over ₹1.10 crore at Calicut International Airport, Karipur, on Monday. They also arrested two members of the alleged robbery gang. According to the police, the incident took place around 3 a.m. A police team noticed a group behaving suspiciously in the arrival area and kept them under watch. The group followed Abhirami, 27, a native of Vandanmedu in Idukki, after she arrived from abroad. When Abhirami reached the parking area with a man who had come to receive her, the gang blocked their way and grabbed her trolley bag. The police team intervened when the gang tried to overpower the man accompanying her. During the struggle, the accused attacked the police and bit home guard Murali Krishna. They also tried to run over a member of the police team with a car while escaping. The officer narrowly escaped from being hit. The police arrested Sayanth, 28, and Babilesh, 40, both from Kallachi, Nadapuram. Abhirami and Harshal, 40, a native of Kochi who had arrived to collect the gold, were also taken into custody. The police said the gold had been sent with Abhirami by Swalih, a native of Thamarassery. Around 10 people had reached the airport in two cars to seize the gold and abduct her. A search of Abhirami’s baggage led to the recovery of 14 gold plates concealed inside an emergency lamp. The gold weighed 817 gm after cleaning and is estimated to be worth more than ₹1.10 crore. The gold, along with ₹67,000 allegedly kept to pay Abhirami for carrying it, a car and the two people detained in connection with the gold, were handed over to the Customs Department for further action. The police said the arrested men had been involved in several similar cases. One of them had lost a hand in a blast. b7ebb6640bbe2a16.title: US Supreme Court rejects Trump admin's push to set aside California ballots
b7ebb6640bbe2a16.summary: The Supreme Court on Monday rejected a push for California to set aside thousands of mail ballots from people President Donald Trump's administration claims are noncitizens, a decision that comes on the eve of the pivotal midterm elections. The high court refused to intervene in a case involving 20,000 people the Republican administration flagged as likely noncitizens on the largely Democratic state's voter rolls. It was the latest in a flurry of election-related litigation the day before the midterm elections, which will decide control of Congress for the last two years of Trump's second term. In California, the Trump administration had asked the high court to set aside the challenged ballots until the voters' citizenship status could be verified. But officials there said that the list appeared to be filled with errors and that setting the ballots aside could effectively disenfranchise legal voters. The high court did not detail its reasoning, as is common in emergency decisions.

ec05d0c73acf6bca.title: Netanyahu presses Trump for fresh Iran strikes after US midterm elections
ec05d0c73acf6bca.summary: Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu is pushing for another wave of strikes on Iran after Tuesday's midterm elections in the United States, according to two regional officials and a third person familiar with the matter. A return to full-scale war with Iran could help Netanyahu to form an emergency government after he and his far-right allies lost their parliamentary majority in last week's elections. US President Donald Trump has alternated between threatening major strikes while pushing for a deal with Iran. The two officials said diplomatic efforts have made progress, with Qatari mediators holding two rounds of talks last week with Iranian officials. The two officials said the mediators are trying to advance a framework for Iran to cease its attacks in the Strait of Hormuz in return for the US lifting its blockade on Iran's ports. They said more talks are planned for this week. The two officials spoke on condition of anonymity because they were discussing classified briefing

f5c1503860f7f7db.title: Cascading effect: On dams and land rights
f5c1503860f7f7db.summary: Published - November 03, 2026 12:56 am IST The bureaucratic impetus for the 11.2-GW Siang Upper Multipurpose Project (SUMP) in Arunachal Pradesh purportedly comes from China’s aggressive development of a 60-GW mega-dam in Tibet , stoking anxieties among Indian authorities over ‘weaponised’ transboundary waters. Beijing may be able to divert flows in the Yarlung Tsangpo river, which becomes the Brahmaputra in India, to cause drought downstream or release water en masse to trigger catastrophic floods in Arunachal Pradesh and Assam. New Delhi thus imagines SUMP as a strategic buffer, but in so doing faces a dilemma it should not attempt to resolve with force. Its extant top-down approach, exemplified by deploying security forces to guard survey teams and imposing the State Unlawful Activities (Prevention) Act against activists, only validates fears among locals that the state will grab their land. The region also hosts sustained protests against the Subansiri Upper Hydroelectric Project , expanding the indictment to Arunachal Pradesh’s model of hydroelectric power development. The eastern Himalayas are among the most tectonically active and erosion-prone landscapes in the world. The mega-dam in Tibet will comprise five cascading power stations over the river’s roughly 2,000-metre fall over 50 km. Beijing has maintained the dam will not harm countries downstream but has declined to share crucial engineering details. This is why diplomacy will be an essential part of operating SUMP, in addition to Beijing’s disputed claims on Arunachal Pradesh. The Brahmaputra basin in Assam and Bangladesh receives most of its water from monsoon rains and tributaries downstream of the Tibetan Plateau, so China cannot straightforwardly control the river’s total flow through India. Yet since Chinese interventions would have greater consequences closer to the border, SUMP will need information about both the mega-dam’s operations and downstream inflows to plan its own operations, and Beijin

"The landfall process commenced at 0100 hours IST on November 3. The forward sector of the wall cloud is entering the coast, while the wall cloud region is very close to the coast," the IMD's official press release said. Under the influence of the cyclone, heavy rain struck several places in the southern state. The cyclone was centred over the west-central Bay of Bengal, close to the South Andhra Pradesh coast, about 40 km southeast of Ongole, 60 km northeast of Kavali and 70 km south of Bapatla, as of 0130 hours. 6fe4e482fbc13805.title: A hundred years ago | Tutankh-Amen’s Tomb: Contents of the Second Chamber
6fe4e482fbc13805.summary: Published - November 03, 2026 03:57 am IST CAIRO, Nov. 2.: The newspaper Siasash learns from a trustworthy source that the contents of the third chamber of Tutankh-Amen’s tomb have recently been opened and while they are not so rich and fine as those of the other two chambers they are of great historical importance, because they represent everything used for the funeral ceremony. Thirty small boats of two kinds were found, one sort being that used for funerals for journeying from Luxor across the Nile to the tombs and the other sort intended to transport the body from the earth to heaven. A very interesting box of small statuettes has also been found having Tutankh-Amen’s head but the body of a bird or animal, giving the Egyptian conception after life and two chariots have been found unornamented. They were supposed to have been used during hunting. These are the first of their kind ever discovered. 729df165de669f2f.title: Mangala sloka for Rama
729df165de669f2f.summary: Published - November 03, 2026 04:50 am IST When Valmiki saw a hunter kill one of a pair of krauncha birds, he cursed the hunter through a sloka. But the sloka can also be interpreted differently, in a positive sense, said M.A. Venkatakrishnan in a discourse. Valmiki’s sloka begins with the word manishadah . If you split this as ma and nishada , then it is Valmiki addressing the hunter ( nishada ). Valmiki curses the hunter, “Oh hunter! You killed one of two birds which were making love ( kaamamohitam ). Because of that, you will never have any peace.” But if the word manishadah is not split, then it means the One who is never separated from ma , that is Mahalakshmi. So, this can be taken as a reference to Rama Himself. While the words shasvathi samah pratistham tvam agamah have a negative meaning when we take them as referring to the hunter, they also can mean ‘May you live long.’ Kaamamohitam can be seen as a reference to Ravana, who was caught in kama (lust) for Sita. So, the entire sloka can be seen as a mangala sloka for Rama, the One who is never separated from Sita and the One who killed the lustful asura. While Valmiki’s intention was to curse the hunter, it so happened that he presented the Ramayana story in a nutshell through that sloka. There are certain rules to be followed while writing a kavya . A mahakavya must have thousands of verses, and Valmiki’s Ramayana has 24,000 verses. Although many versions of the Ramayana came up later, Valmiki’s is the authentic account, because he was witness to everything that happened in Rama’s life, thanks to the divine vision which Brahma gave him. When Lord Narayana decided to take the Rama avatara, Veda Purusha decided to take an avatara as Valmiki Ramayana. So, the Ramayana is the embodiment of Vedic tenets. It has many tattvas which need deep study and analysis. Published - November 03, 2026 04:50 am IST Terms & conditions | Institutional Subscriber Comments have to be in English, and in full sentences. 0056552907126bc0.title: Bajaj Auto's total sales during October rise 14% to 591,876 units
0056552907126bc0.summary: Bajaj Auto on Monday posted a 14 per cent year-on-year growth in its total sales during October, with double-digit growth across two-wheelers and commercial vehicles. The automaker's total wholesales stood at 5,91,876 units, against 5,18,170 units in the year-ago period, according to an exchange filing. Domestic sales rose 12 per cent to 3,51,148 units, while exports grew 18 per cent to 2,40,728 units. Total two-wheeler sales increased by 13 per cent to 5,01,194 units from 4,42,316 in the year-ago period. Total commercial vehicle sales were higher by 20 per cent to 90,682 units, compared to 75,854 units. Bajaj Auto's total sales during the April-October period rose 22 per cent to 35,79,011 units. Two-wheeler sales rose 22 per cent to 30,07,707 units, while commercial vehicle sales were higher by 23 per cent at 5,71,304 units.

13f1db64f5be6e0c.summary: Commercial vehicle major Ashok Leyland on Monday reported a 23 per cent year-on-year growth in its total sales during October. The Chennai-based automaker's total sales, including exports, stood at 21,888 units, up from 17,820 units a year ago, according to an exchange filing. Sales in the Medium and Heavy Commercial Vehicle (M&HCV) segment grew 28 per cent to 13,927 units from 10,865 units, while the Light Commercial Vehicle (LCV) segment registered a 14 per cent rise to 7,961 units. Total domestic sales rose 24 per cent to 20,224 units from 16,314 units a year ago, with 32 per cent growth in the M&HCV segment to 12,646 units. The Chennai-based automaker's total sales, including exports, stood at 21,888 units, up from 17,820 units a year ago, according to an exchange filing. Sales in the Medium and Heavy Commercial Vehicle (M&HCV) segment grew 28 per cent to 13,927 units from 10,865 units, while the Light Commercial Vehicle (LCV) segment registered a 14 per cent rise to 7,961 units. Total domestic sales rose 24 per cent to 20,224 units from 16,314 units a year ago, with 32 per cent growth in the M&HCV segment to 12,646 units. Domestic LCV sales increased 13 per cent to 7,578 units.

6ce0c0e80e6eb1d2.summary: Don't travel by air, the Supreme Court told a petitioner on Monday while refusing urgent listing of a plea alleging nearly 700 per cent increase in airfares. An advocate mentioned the matter for urgent listing before a bench comprising Justices Vikram Nath, Sandeep Mehta and Aparesh Kumar Singh. "The aviation fare has increased by 700 per cent," the advocate said. "Don't travel by air," the bench observed. The advocate then said air travel is an essential service. "It's a violation of Article 14." Article 14 of the Constitution deals with equality before law. 114481a9559f90ba.title: US consortium pushes for $4.4 billion LNG project in Pakistan: Report
114481a9559f90ba.summary: A consortium of American companies, backed by US President Donald Trump's administration, is seeking up to USD 4.4 billion in investment for an integrated liquefied natural gas (LNG) project in Pakistan, according to a media report on Monday. The proposed project will cover imports, storage, regasification, gas transmission and sales to large consumers on a merchant basis, the Dawn newspaper reported. LNG is natural gas that has been cooled to around minus 162 degrees Celsius, turning it into a liquid and reducing its volume by about 600 times. This makes it easier to store and transport by specialised ships. At its destination, the LNG is converted back into gas through a process called regasification and supplied to consumers. It is used to generate electricity, fuel industrial processes, produce fertilisers and provide energy for heating and cooking. It is also used as a fuel in some vehicles and ships. bd9e4166ce611995.summary: Published - November 02, 2026 07:55 pm IST - Chennai AIADMK General Secretary Edappadi K Palaniswami. | Photo Credit: R SENTHILKUMAR The AIADMK general secretary Edappadi K. Palaniswami on Monday expressed concern over the previous month’s reported three per cent growth in the Goods and Services Tax (GST) collections in Tamil Nadu, which was much below the national average. In a post on his social media handle, Mr. Palaniswami referred to the State’s level of inflation which was higher than that of the all-India figure and “diversion” of industrial projects to other States, similar to what was shown in a feature film of Chief Minister C. Joseph Vijay. “How would the GST collections go up unless industry achieved progress, which would, in turn, generate jobs; enable higher growth in Gross Domestic Production and rise in per capita income?” Mr. Palaniswami wondered. Recalling that the Guidance Tamil Nadu, the nodal agency for investment promotion and single-window facilitation, was established when Jayalalithaa was Chief Minister, the AIADMK leader accused the present TVK-led government of having “ruined” it.
