e21b19eda890a1b1.title: Telangana plans AI-enabled transactions in agri. market yards
e21b19eda890a1b1.summary: Published - November 02, 2026 07:51 pm IST - HYDERABAD Minister for Agriculture Tummala Nageswara Rao holding a meeting with marketing officials in Hyderabad on Monday. | Photo Credit: By Arrangement The Telangana government is planning to make the agricultural markets in the State AI (artificial intelligence)-enabled for the first time in the country and also make them model markets, Minister for Agriculture Tummala Nageswara Rao said. At a meeting with the agricultural marketing and agriculture departments here on Monday, he said the AI technology would check for irregularities in transactions in market yards. Tenders for introduction of AI technology in the market yards’ transactions would be called within a week. He suggested them to bring into a single digital system all transactions related to farmers — from the farmer entering the market with his/her produce, its sale, payments and others till he/she leaves the market yard. Listing of farmers’ details, allocation of identity number to every lot/crop, assessing crop quality, fixing price, digital bidding/tender details, online auction, farmer’s consent, weighing, sale bills, market charges, payments to farmers, recording of gate exit, e-receipts and e-permits issuance should be done on a single platform. The management information system should also have details of commission agents, traders, price patterns, auction details and others so that they can be cross-checked in future too. The Minister told the officials to study the digital marketing systems being implemented elsewhere in the country. Even the attendance of marketing department officials, including biometric attendance registering, be also made part of the new digital system. The market yards should also have closed-circuit camera systems to monitor maintenance of godowns and daily activities. 88523712e648304f.title: Joint survey to resolve Revenue-Forest land disputes: Ponguleti
88523712e648304f.summary: Published - November 02, 2026 07:43 pm IST - HYDERABAD Revenue Minister Ponguleti Srinivasa Reddy at a review meeting with Revenue, Forest and Survey and Settlement officials at the Secretariat on Monday. The Telangana government has decided to undertake joint surveys by the Revenue and Forest departments to find a permanent solution to long-pending disputes over land boundaries, particularly those involving forest, revenue and patta lands. Revenue Minister Ponguleti Srinivasa Reddy directed officials of both departments to work in close coordination and ensure that ordinary people and farmers do not suffer because of inter-departmental boundary disputes. At a review meeting with Revenue, Forest and Survey and Settlement officials at the Secretariat, the Minister said the government, under the leadership of Chief Minister A. Revanth Reddy, was committed to resolving land-related issues that had remained unsettled for decades. Pointing out that the erstwhile Khammam, Warangal and Adilabad districts had substantial forest areas, Mr. Ponguleti said boundary disputes between the Revenue and Forest departments had persisted for several decades. He called for scientific and technology-based joint surveys to establish clear boundaries and prevent such disputes from recurring. Officials should examine the actual ground position and comprehensively reconcile land records, maps and survey details before arriving at conclusions. Issues that could be settled at the field level should be resolved locally, while matters requiring higher-level intervention should be referred to the State government without delay, he said. Observing that prolonged disputes had caused considerable hardship to farmers and landowners, he said he would personally monitor the joint survey exercise and periodically review its progress. ecee93d69cbdb6d7.title: One held in Keralam for securing job in panchayat with fake mark list
ecee93d69cbdb6d7.summary: Published - November 02, 2026 07:39 pm IST - PALAKKAD Representational image. | Photo Credit: Getty Images A former Democratic Youth Federation of India (DYFI) unit secretary was arrested for allegedly securing a contractual job at Puthukkode grama panchayat here by submitting a fake BCom mark list. The arrested person, K.V. Ganapathy, a native of Puthukkode Kizhakke Gramam, worked as an accountant-cum-IT assistant in the panchayat’s employment guarantee scheme section. The Vadakkenchery police arrested him in connection with the case on Monday. Mr. Ganapathy joined the panchayat on a contractual basis in July 2021, when the Left Democratic Front (LDF) was in power. He continued in the post until July 2026. He had submitted a BCom mark list purportedly issued by the University of Calicut as proof of his educational qualification. After the United Democratic Front (UDF) came to power in the last local body elections, the panchayat committee refused to extend his contract. Mr. Ganapathy then approached the High Court and obtained an order allowing him to continue in the post until September 2026. The alleged fraud came to light during the verification process for his reinstatement. The new panchayat administration became suspicious because Mr. Ganapathy had submitted only a mark list, rather than an original or provisional degree certificate, to prove his qualification. Growing suspicious, the panchayat authorities sent the mark list to the University of Calicut for verification. The university informed them that the document was fake and that Mr. Ganapathy had not passed the BCom degree. 33f9968d0690c99e.title: Hair donation drive to support cancer patients held at Sri Ramachandra Institute of Higher Education and Research
33f9968d0690c99e.summary: Updated - November 02, 2026 07:41 pm IST - Chennai Film producer and director Soundarya Rajinikanth inaugurating the hair donation driver held at SRIHER on Monday. | Photo Credit: Special arrangement A hair donation drive was organised on Monday at Sri Ramachandra Institute of Higher Education and Research (SRIHER) to support cancer patients who lose their hair during treatment. The National Service Scheme unit of SRIHER, in association with Ladies Circle India, Hair for Hope India, and the Adyar Cancer Institute, organised the event, aiming to collect hair from 800 donors in an attempt to set a world record. Film producer and director Soundarya Rajinikanth inaugurated the drive. She urged the media to raise awareness on the challenges faced by cancer patients and the impact of hair loss on their confidence. 53c883e3af2a990d.title: A.P. set for counting of votes in 92 ULBs on November 3
53c883e3af2a990d.summary: Published - November 02, 2026 07:39 pm IST - VIJAYAWADA The State Election Commission (SEC) has made arrangements for the counting of votes in 92 urban local bodies (13 Municipal Corporations and 79 Municipalities and Nagar Panchayats) from 8 a.m. on November 3 (Tuesday). SEC Commissioner Anil Chandra Punetha, in a press release, said that counting was being conducted for a total of 3,186 wards, including 804 in Municipal Corporations (MCs) and 2,382 in Municipalities and Nagar Panchayats (M&NPs). The total number of counting centres is 138 — 22 in Municipal Corporations and the remaining in Municipalities and Nagar Panchayats. The counting process will be undertaken by 47,817 supervisors, assistants and staff (28,182 in MCs and 19,635 in M&NPs). A total of 1,372 CCTVs have been installed at strong rooms and counting centres (98 in MCs and 126 in M&NPs). Meanwhile, the SEC reported that the final voting percentage in the 92 urban local bodies that went to polls on November 1 stood at 62.16, with 60,22,411 of the 96,89,061 voters exercising their franchise. 1e06532f2305d2f6.title: TG-Redco for speeding up implementation of renewable energy schemes
1e06532f2305d2f6.summary: Published - November 02, 2026 07:33 pm IST - HYDERABAD Vice-chairman and MD of TG-Redco Jithesh V. Patil holding a virtual meeting with district managers from Hyderabad on Monday. | Photo Credit: Arrangement Vice-chairman and managing director of the Telangana State Renewable Energy Development Corporation (TG-Redco) Jithesh V. Patil has asked officials to accelerate the implementation of renewable energy schemes across the State and achieve planned targets within stipulated timelines. In a virtual meeting held on Monday with the district managers of the Redco, he stressed the need to identify field-level challenges and resolve them promptly through coordination with the departments concerned. He reviewed the Model Solar Village Programme, installation of rooftop solar power plants, solarisation of agricultural pump sets, PM-KUSUM scheme, energy conservation activities and development of electric vehicle (EV) charging infrastructure. He sought details from the officials on the work completed so far, current status and pending issues. Mr. Patil told the district managers to create awareness among eligible consumers about the benefits of rooftop solar under the Gruha Jyothi scheme. He called for district-level action plans to achieve the targets under agricultural pump set solarisation and the PM-KUSUM scheme. On pending approvals and inspections, he instructed officials to speed up the process of obtaining necessary approvals from various departments and complete pending inspections without delay. Venkatesan. Daisy Asha Moraes, a fourth-year student at the South Ural State Medical University in Russia, had planned to return to India on leave for medical reasons. With her visa set to expire on October 20, she booked a flight via Moscow and arrived at the airport on October 18. However, ongoing drone attacks linked to the Russia-Ukraine conflict forced the cancellation of domestic flights, grounding her scheduled journey. When alternative flights failed to materialise immediately, Russian authorities detained her under the classification of overstaying her expired visa, initiating detention proceedings on October 20. Although a local court granted a 10-day grace period, her family faced mounting anxiety that she could be held in detention for up to 90 days. After exhausting other avenues, the student’s father, Arul Moraes, sought the assistance of Mr. Venkatesan. Operating through parliamentary offices in Madurai and New Delhi, Mr. Venkatesan’s team coordinated directly with the External Affairs Minister, senior ministry officials, and the Indian Embassy in Russia. Compiling documentation regarding her medical condition and the war-related flight disruptions, officials presented the case to Russian authorities on October 27, establishing that the student bore no fault in the travel disruption. Originally informed that the student could not leave until November 15, the intervention successfully expedited her departure. Medical assistance and travel arrangements were secured, and Moraes boarded a flight to India on November 1, arriving safely in Madurai. e3eb50752922ec13.title: IRC summit to showcase Telangana’s growth, investment potential: Komatireddy
e3eb50752922ec13.summary: Published - November 02, 2026 07:36 pm IST - HYDERABAD Roads and Buildings Minister Komatireddy Venkat Reddy at a review meeting with senior officials at the Secretariat on Monday. The 85th Indian Roads Congress (IRC) summit, scheduled to be held in Hyderabad from November 19 to 22, should be transformed into a global platform to showcase Telangana’s development, culture and investment potential, Roads and Buildings Minister Komatireddy Venkat Reddy said. At a review meeting with senior officials at the Secretariat on Monday, the Minister directed them to make the event a precursor to the ‘Invest Telangana’ Global Summit scheduled to be held in December at Bharat Future City. He said the IRC summit should not remain confined to technical discussions on roads and infrastructure but should also help attract investments, industries and employment opportunities to the State. Officials should prepare a special action plan to connect with potential investors and encourage them to participate in the December global investment summit. Union Minister for Road Transport and Highways Nitin Gadkari and Chief Minister A. Revanth Reddy would jointly inaugurate the four-day summit at HITEX on November 19. Union Ministers, Ministers from various States, senior bureaucrats, international delegates and experts from the engineering and infrastructure sectors are expected to participate. 3ce124ce86c16ef5.title: Chittoor, Annamayya districts brace for Cyclone Murasu
3ce124ce86c16ef5.summary: Published - November 02, 2026 07:34 pm IST - CHITTOOR/MADANAPALLE The officials are prepared for any emergency following a high alert for Severe Cyclonic Storm Murasu across South Andhra Pradesh, projected to impact Chittoor and Annamayya districts over the next 48 hours. While the core system is projected to make landfall between Nellore and Narsapur, the sprawling outer bands of the cyclone are expected to reach the interior Rayalaseema region. Officials have issued an orange alert for Chittoor district, warning of heavy to very heavy rainfall through Monday and Tuesday. Neighbouring Annamayya district, which began the week under a yellow warning, is bracing for an escalation to an orange alert on Tuesday, with expectations of downpours in isolated areas. Officials said that the sudden rain could trigger severe waterlogging in low-lying tracts, spill over swollen streams, and trigger localised flooding in vulnerable rural pockets. Farmers across the Nagari, Chittoor, and Palamaner revenue divisions in Chittoor district and the eastern parts of Annamayya district initiated measures to protect standing paddy, horticultural orchards, and vegetable plots from gusty winds and floodwaters. Officials of the APSPDCL and civic officials were instructed to be prepared in the event of potential snapping of power lines and major roadblocks caused by uprooted trees. Annamayya district Collector Nishant Kumar said that with the crucial 48-hour window under way, the district machinery has swung into action at all vulnerable areas. “Revenue, police, municipal, and disaster response teams remain stationed on high alert in flood-prone zones,” he said. Chittoor Collector Sumit Kumar said that the district administration has issued strict advisories urging residents to stay alert to official weather bulletins. “Above all, the public should be cautious about fast-flowing streams and causeways,” he said. a14467189d646d17.title: Telangana Civil Supplies officials uncover rice sale violations, hoarding in Hyderabad
a14467189d646d17.summary: Published - November 02, 2026 07:35 pm IST - HYDERABAD Diversion of rice meant for Public Distribution System (PDS) was one of the violation detected by Telangana Civil Supplies teams during checks between October 29 and 31. The image is used for representative purposes only. | Photo Credit: BY ARRANGEMENT Telangana Civil Supplies Department officials uncovered violations in sale of rice at a few outlets in Hyderabad and Rangareddy districts. The violations include weight manipulations by traders by affixing 26-kilogram labels onto bags having only 25 kilograms of rice , and exorbitant prices pasted over the rates printed by manufacturers. The department’s teams lodged complaints at Saroornagar, Jeedimetla, and Alwal police stations, based on which action was initiated, as per official information. This follows surprise checks by the Enforcement Task Force (ETF) along with the Legal Metrology Department across Hyderabad and Ranga Reddy districts between October 29 to 31. The other violations detected include diversion and hoarding of Public Distribution System (PDS) rice, traders operating without mandatory trade, GST, Labour, or FSSAI licenses. The teams have documented the offences on-site by taking videos and photos. The department stated that the vigilance will continue. The State government on Saturday (October 31, 2026) announced a ceiling on maximum retail price (MRP) on three varieties of fine rice in the urban limits , which are most consumed by people. As per the orders, price of a kg of BPT/KNM variety was fixed at ₹66; RNR/Telangana Sona at ₹74 and HMT/JSR variety at ₹79, in Hyderabad and Medchal. d4535bfeee0e14e6.title: Pawan Kalyan directs high alert as Cyclone Murasu nears Nellore coast
d4535bfeee0e14e6.summary: Updated - November 02, 2026 07:38 pm IST - VIJAYAWADA Deputy Chief Minister K. Pawan Kalyan | Photo Credit: File photo Deputy Chief Minister K. Pawan Kalyan has directed officials to remain on high alert as cyclone Murasu approaches the coast, even as the State is yet to recover from the damage caused by cyclone Arnab. At a review meeting with senior officials of the Panchayat Raj and Rural Development and Rural Water Supply Departments on Monday, Mr. Kalyan said the India Meteorological Department (IMD) had warned of extremely heavy rain in Nellore, Prakasam, Markapuram, Bapatla and Krishna districts. In view of the forecast of intense rainfall, he stressed the need to evacuate people living in low-lying areas to safer locations, ensure proper coordination among departments, minimise hardship and prevent loss of life. Officials informed the Deputy Chief Minister that the cyclone was initially forecast to cross the coast between Bapatla and Machilipatnam. However, it had changed course and was now expected to make landfall near Nellore. Heavy rain was already lashing Nellore, Prakasam, Bapatla, Tirupati and Markapuram districts under the influence of the cyclone. Six National Disaster Response Force (NDRF) and seven State Disaster Response Force (SDRF) teams had been kept on standby, officials said. They added that other necessary precautionary measures were being taken. 8d7756523fa00748.title: Residents seek closure of Tasmac outlet, illegal recreation club in Keela Arasadi panchayat
8d7756523fa00748.summary: Published - November 02, 2026 07:43 pm IST - THOOTHUKUDI: Residents of Thuppaspatti and Ayyanarpuram at the Collectorate in Thoothukudi on Monday. | Photo Credit: N. RAJESH Residents of Thuppaspatti and Ayyanarpuram in the district on Monday submitted a petition to the Collector, seeking closure of a newly opened Tasmac outlet and an ‘llegal’ recreation club nearby. The petition was submitted at the weekly grievance redressal meeting chaired by Collector Vishu Mahajan. In their petition, the villagers said the Tasmac outlet and the club in Thuppaspatti-Ayyanarpuram area under Keela Arasadi panchayat were causing several problems. Also, while staging continuous protests demanding the closure of both outlets, anti-social elements were issuing death threats to the protesters. The petitioners said that drunken people made it a regular practice to engage in quarrels in nearby thickets, break and throw liquor bottles and lie around in an intoxicated state. This raised serious safety concerns among women, who left for work at the salt pans early in the morning, and school students passing through the area. The residents urged the authorities to permanently shut down the Tasmac outlet and the recreation club, which were causing inconvenience to the public, and take stringent action against those threatening and intimidating the villagers. In a separate petition, Sudalai of Meelavittan and other villagers said that 70 goats died after allegedly consuming wastewater discharged from a fertilizer godown owned by a private company at Veeranayakkanthattu near Thoothukudi. The animals had been grazing in the area. They sought criminal action against the godown management and adequate compensation for the loss of goats. 668d07ff7e0eaaea.title: Ranji Trophy: Urvil and Vishal boost Gujarat
668d07ff7e0eaaea.summary: Published - November 02, 2026 07:37 pm IST - Ahmedabad Opener Aarya hit six fours and three maximums in his 95. | Photo Credit: VIJAY SONEJI A frustratingly familiar script unfolded again for Kerala at the Narendra Modi stadium here on Monday. For the third time this season, Kerala allowed the opposition’s lower-order to fight back and wrest away the hard-earned advantage. An unbeaten, counterattacking 111-run partnership for the sixth wicket between Urvil Patel (63 batting, 67b, 7x4, 1x6) and Vishal Jayswal (50 batting, 83b, 3x4, 2x6) was the latest to hurt Kerala as Gujarat ended the opening day of the Ranji Trophy Elite Group C match at 300 for five. Soon after tea, Kerala had Gujarat in a spot of bother at 189 for five when Jaymeet Patel (one) was stumped by Mohammed Azharuddeen off Aditya Sarvate. But the visiting side let Gujarat off the hook when it failed to grab the chances and wilted under the calculated assault by Urvil and Vishal. Rohan Kunnummal showed poor judgement while running back and failed to reach a skier from Vishal off Vaisakh Chandran when the batter was on 33. Azharuddeen fumbled when Urvil, on 32, stepped out to attack Sarvate. Urvil and Vishal capitalised on these errors to take their side to a position of strength in the final session. Earlier, Kerala had crawled back into the contest in the post-lunch session, picking up four wickets to reduce the host to 182 for four. The strikes included that of top-scorer Aarya Desai (95, 132b, 6x4, 3x6), who in a hurry to reach his hundred top-edged a wild slog and was caught by Vishnu Vinod off Vaisakh. In the morning, openers Aarya and Abhishek Desai played fluently against the Kerala bowlers who found little help from the track. However, a better disciplined show with the ball in the second session choked the flow runs which forced the Gujarat batters to take the risks, which ultimately led to their downfall. The scores: Gujarat — 1st innings: Abhishek Desai c Rohan b Nidheesh 42, Aarya Desai c Vi

The National Highways Authority of India (NHAI) has proposed a 70-km inter-corridor highway connecting NH 81 in Tiruppur district to NH 544 near Sankari in Salem district. The project cost is estimated at ₹ 2,000 crore and the four-way lane is expected to pass through about 19 km in Namakkal district. Farmers have raised opposition, stating that the project would severely affect farmlands, schools, spinning mills, and houses. P. The project envisions laying 150-ft road for 19 km in Namakkal district. This would affect around 200 acres of farmland, schools at Padaiveedu, Uppupalayam, spinning mills, and over 100 houses. Likewise, 18 village roads will have to be destroyed for the project. Two weeks ago, farmers from seven villages submitted a petition against the project at the divisional-level farmers’ grievances meet at the Pallipalayam panchayat union office. 783e08fb334bc57d.title: PWD employees stage black badge protest over delayed October salary
783e08fb334bc57d.summary: Updated - November 02, 2026 07:52 pm IST - MADURAI Employees of the Tamil Nadu Government Public Works Department Accounts and Administrative Staff Association staged a State-wide protest on Monday, wearing black badges to condemn the non-disbursement of October salary to over a thousand employees across the Public Works Department (PWD) and the Water Resources Department. The salary delay, affecting personnel from chief engineers down to office assistants, has severely impacted livelihoods as the Deepavali festival approaches, said Abdul Najimudeen, general secretary of the association. Association representatives revealed that the delay stemmed from files pending in the Finance Department and the salary item being disabled in the IFHRMS portal, leaving employees unable to receive timely pay even with government intervention. They noted that pay authorisation bottlenecks—with delays recurring every three to six months—and unapproved temporary posts have created major administrative hurdles, echoing a similar crisis last July when salaries were delayed past the 15th of the month. The association has put forward an eight-point charter of demands, urging the State government to disburse salaries immediately on a war footing and find a permanent solution to departmental issues rather than handling staff livelihoods casually. Key demands include issuing requested transfers pending for the last five months, promoting over 450 junior assistants and typists, regularising temporary workers who have served for over a decade, revoking Government Order No. 69, converting divisional accountant posts into a State service, and filling all vacant positions. Warning that this year’s festival risks becoming a ‘black Deepavali’ for PWD staff, the union announced escalated protests if their grievances are ignored. A zonal-level dharna is scheduled for November 17, followed by a massive hunger strike at the Chennai PWD campus on December 8. Published - November 02, 2026 07:23 pm IST Te

e32d6b6853bbb527.title: Facial recognition attendance system introduced as pilot project in SCCL’s Kothagudem Area
e32d6b6853bbb527.summary: Published - November 02, 2026 07:39 pm IST - BHADRADRI KOTHAGUDEM A facial recognition-based attendance system was introduced on a trial basis in the Kothagudem Area of the Singareni Collieries Company Limited (SCCL) on Monday. The initiative is part of the SCCL’s efforts to adopt technology in its employee attendance system to enhance transparency. Biometric attendance systems are already in use at some General Managers’ offices in SCCL. However, this is the first time the system is being implemented across the coal mines and departments of an entire area. The initiative is aimed at promoting discipline and punctuality among employees and is expected to improve transparency and productivity, according to an SCCL press release. SCCL has around 40,000 employees, of whom approximately 1,600 work in the Kothagudem Area. The trial run began in the Kothagudem Area as a pilot project on Monday. The system is expected to be extended to mines and departments in other areas in a phased manner. 8568b14a98d223eb.title: Karnataka deploys 500 linemen, equipment to restore power supply in cyclone-hit Andhra Pradesh
8568b14a98d223eb.summary: Published - November 02, 2026 07:49 pm IST - Bengaluru The State government is providing contingency funds to meet travel, accommodation and other emergency expenses of the deployed personnel. | Photo Credit: File Photo Karnataka has deployed 500 trained power utility workers and specialised equipment to Andhra Pradesh to help restore electricity infrastructure damaged by Cyclone Arnab. The deployment follows a request from the Andhra Pradesh government for manpower and equipment to carry out restoration work in cyclone-affected areas. The Karnataka government has mobilised the teams under the supervision of Energy Minister K.J. George as part of inter-State cooperation. Chief Minister D.K. Shivakumar spoke to his Andhra Pradesh counterpart N. Chandrababu Naidu over the phone and assured him of Karnataka’s support. “Electricity is an essential service, and restoring it immediately is necessary for the well-being of people affected by the disaster. Karnataka stands firmly with the people of Andhra Pradesh during this difficult time,” the Chief Minister said. Mr. George said Karnataka’s teams would work closely with Andhra Pradesh officials to restore power supply at the earliest through field-level coordination and the deployment of specialised equipment. The State has sent 500 trained linemen, 15 Palfinger trucks equipped with cranes and earth augers, and 25 tractor-mounted drilling machines. The teams were mobilised on an emergency basis and left for Andhra Pradesh on Monday afternoon, reaching the State by midnight. For effective deployment and coordination, each electricity supply company (ESCOM) has appointed a single-point contact officer to liaise with the concerned Andhra Pradesh officials. The linemen have been divided into teams of 10, each led by a junior or assistant engineer. 87ebc376380a8fdf.title: Tight security arrangements for ULB vote counting in Chittoor, Annamayya, Sri Sathya Sai districts
87ebc376380a8fdf.summary: Updated - November 02, 2026 07:36 pm IST - CHITTOOR Elaborate arrangements are in place for counting votes in the urban local body elections across Chittoor, Annamayya, and Sri Sathya Sai districts on Tuesday (November 3, 2026), with officials intensifying security to ensure a tension-free and transparent declaration of results. Annamayya district Collector Nishant Kumar inspected the strong rooms and counting centres in Madanapalle, while Chittoor Collector Sumit Kumar reviewed the arrangements in Chittoor on Monday (November 2). In Sri Sathya Sai district, SP S. Satish Kumar inspected the strong rooms in Dharmavaram and reviewed security arrangements. “Heavy police bandobast has been deployed at counting centres, with special focus on preventing unauthorised entry, maintaining law and order and avoiding clashes between political groups. Strong rooms housing ballot boxes are under round-the-clock security,” said Sumit Kumar. “CCTV surveillance and strict entry regulations will be enforced at counting venues. Candidates and their authorised counting agents only will be allowed inside after verification,” Sri Sathya Sai district Collector A. Shyam Prasad said. Minister of Endowments Anam Ramanarayana Reddy campaigned in Sangam mandal, which falls under his Atmakur constituency. Similarly, the YSRCP leaders also campaigned for their candidates. Despite the rain, the party workers continued campaigning in Jarugumalli village, which falls under Kothapalem MPTC segment in Kota mandal. Under the guidance of YSRCP leader Nedurumalli Harish Chandra Reddy, the party cadre conducted an extensive campaign throughout the village for MPTC candidate Gali Praveenamma. a02bb588eee39523.title: Six fishermen safe as fishing boat runs aground at Rushikonda beach in Visakhapatnam
a02bb588eee39523.summary: Published - November 02, 2026 07:37 pm IST - VISAKHAPATNAM Rescued crew members of the fishing vessel that drifted ashore at Rushikonda beach in Visakhapatnam on Monday. | Photo Credit: BY ARRANGEMENT A major maritime mishap was averted when a mechanised fishing boat drifted ashore near Rushikonda Beach on Monday, after its engine failed and ran out of fuel in rough seas. All six fishermen aboard the vessel were unharmed as the boat grounded near the shoreline. According to the fisheries officials and coastal police, the fishing boat, bearing registration number IND.AP.V5.MM.255 and owned by Korangi Narsinga Rao, had set out on a routine fishing expedition off the Visakhapatnam coast a few days ago. Trouble began at mid-sea when the vessel’s engine developed a technical snag and subsequently ran out of fuel. The crew dropped anchor in an attempt to stabilise the drifting vessel. However, strong tidal surges and turbulent waves caused by the adverse weather conditions along the coast caused the anchor line to snap. Unable to manoeuver the vessel in the swelling waters, the boat along with the crew was carried westward by high-energy waves before the boat ran aground near Rushikonda beach. Recounting the incident one of the crew members said: “We lost power after running out of fuel, and before we could secure the boat, the anchor broke under heavy wave pressure. Fortunately, the ocean tides pushed us towards the shore rather than towards the deep sea.” Beach lifeguards, local fishermen, and Coastal Security Police quickly rushed to the spot on seeing the grounded vessel. Officials confirmed that all six crew members managed to disembark safely without sustaining injuries. Marine police authorities and fisheries department staff arrived at Rushikonda to inspect the vessel for structural damage and made arrangements to tow it once sea conditions improve. 90c3264d8212701c.title: All Souls Day observed in Madurai
90c3264d8212701c.summary: Published - November 02, 2026 07:45 pm IST - MADURAI Family members on All Souls Day performing rituals at a cemetery in Madurai on Monday. | Photo Credit: G. MOORTHY Hundreds of Catholic families gathered at various city cemeteries on Monday to offer prayers for departed souls in observance of All Souls Day. The solemn occasion is observed with the belief that prayers assist souls in purgatory on their path to Heaven. As a gesture of remembrance, believers cleaned burial sites before lighting candles and placing flowers and wreaths upon the graves of their loved ones. Special masses were also held across local churches. Devotional gatherings and prayers took place at cemeteries in Mahaboobpalayam, Kalavasal, Karpaga Nagar, Thuvariman, and surrounding areas. 00d12a7aa8bf2173.title: Tasmac workers shut shops in Namakkal, Salem
00d12a7aa8bf2173.summary: Published - November 02, 2026 07:49 pm IST - Salem A total of 155 Tasmac outlets in Namakkal and many outlets in Salem downed shutters on Monday, in protest against the implementation of new Environmental and Social Welfare Cess. Meanwhile, on Sunday evening, three customers went to an outlet at Pillur near Paramathi Velur, returned the empty liquor bottles and demanded money. Due to server issues, the bottles could not be scanned and it resulted in a quarrel between the customers and the salesman, Purusothaman (46). During the quarrel, the three men hit Purusothaman with a bottle and he sustained injuries. He was admitted to Paramathi Velur Government Hospital. Similarly, customers attacked another salesman, Marimuthu, at Nallar outlet and damaged his two-wheeler. In Salem district, acting on complaints that Tasmac workers were collecting excess money for bottles, the officials checked an outlet at Venkatappa Chetty Street at Pal Market on Sunday evening. They found the allegations to be true. Following this, the outlet salesmen Senthil, Pachaperumal, and supervisor Govindan were placed under suspension. c051082588990188.title: Villagers stage protest at Collectorate demanding mobile ration shop
c051082588990188.summary: Published - November 02, 2026 07:35 pm IST - RAMANATHAPURAM Keelakarai villagers staged a demonstration outside the Ramanathapuram Collectorate demanding the setting up of a mobile ration shop. The Collector assured that action will be taken. More than a hundred villagers and members of the women’s self-help group from Velanoor (South) village in Keelakarai taluk, Ramanathapuram district, besieged the Collectorate, demanding the establishment of a mobile ration shop in their village. They then stated that they intended to submit their family cards along with a petition to Collector M. Sivaguru Prabhakaran at the public grievance redressal meeting. After the Collector assured them that appropriate action would be taken, the villagers returned with their family cards. The villagers stated, “There are 210 family cards in our village. We all purchase essential goods from the ration shop operating in Velanoor North Street, which is located one km away. As Scheduled Caste community people, we face various hardships when we go there to buy goods from a ration shop located in an area where people of another community reside. So, we have submitted petitions multiple times to the District Supply Officer to set up a mobile ration shop in our village once a month. On July 7th, we staged a siege protest at the Keelakarai Tahsildar’s office. During the talks held under the chairmanship of the Tahsildar that day, an assurance was given to set up a mobile ration shop. However, no ration shop has been set up to date. Hence, we came to surrender our family cards to the District Collector. The Collector has assured us that action will be taken.” Published - November 02, 2026 07:35 pm IST Terms & conditions | Institutional Subscriber Comments have to be in English, and in full sentences. 998ff12a26ed57ad.title: Three rebel AAP MLAs from Punjab join BJP ahead of Assembly polls
998ff12a26ed57ad.summary: In a setback to the Aam Aadmi Party ahead of the Punjab assembly polls, three of its leaders from the state, including Kunwar Vijay Pratap Singh and two other legislators, joined the BJP on Monday. Earlier in the day, suspended AAP MLA and former IPS officer Kunwar Vijay Pratap Singh said he resigned as a legislator of the Punjab Vidhan Sabha. In a post on Facebook, Singh -- the MLA from Amritsar North seat -- said he has sent his resignation to Speaker Kultar Singh Sandhwan. Singh, along with Punjab MLAs Chetan Singh Jouramajra and Harmeet Singh Pathanmajra, joined the BJP in the presence of senior leaders at its headquarters here. His resignation from the Punjab Assembly came on the heels of two other AAP legislators -- Chetan Singh Jouramajra from Samana and Harmeet Singh Pathanmajra from Sanour in Patiala district -- resigning from the party on Sunday.

af8f3d0c3943d793.title: Jagan accuses SEC of complicity in civic poll malpractices, says YSRCP will go to court
af8f3d0c3943d793.summary: Updated - November 02, 2026 03:32 pm IST - VIJAYAWADA YSRCP president Y.S. Jagan Mohan Reddy staging a protest outside the office of the Returning Officer in Pulivendula on Sunday. | Photo Credit: Special Arrangement YSR Congress Party (YSRCP) president and former Chief Minister Y.S. Jagan Mohan Reddy has accused the State Election Commission (SEC) of being complicit in the electoral malpractices that took place during the urban local body elections on November 1. Instead of protecting democracy, the SEC acted as per the whims of the coalition government, he said. In an X post on Monday, Mr. Jagan Mohan Reddy said the shocking incidents during the municipal elections, particularly those in Pulivendula, exposed how the SEC stood firmly behind the malpractices. The State Election Commission (SEC), which is meant to protect democracy, has become subservient to @ncbn. The shocking incidents during yesterday's municipal polling across the state, including in Pulivendula, show how the SEC is enabling election irregularities. Yesterday in Pulivendula, YSRCP agents were kept out of 70 of the 80 polling booths. TDP goons brought in from other areas went on a rampage with the support of election officials and the police. They attacked our party agents to stop them from entering polling booths. In some places, they dragged our agents out of the polling stations. These incidents took place with the police's support. Voter slips were snatched from people, polling booths were captured, and votes were rigged and cast repeatedly. The video evidence of these incidents is clear. Agents from all 70 booths came to me personally, showed their agent forms to the officials, lodged complaints and protested. The entire state witnessed what happened. Yet the SEC's response was shocking. Irregularities took place in 70 of the 80 booths, and our agents were attacked and forced out. In these circumstances, how was it fair for the SEC to order repolling in only four booths and then wash its hand

35d271bddf5e0566.title: Cyclone Murasu: List of flights cancelled to and from Chennai, Visakhapatnam, Vijayawada
35d271bddf5e0566.summary: Updated - November 02, 2026 04:16 pm IST Representational Image | Photo Credit: Velankanni Raj Cyclone Murasu, which has intensified into a ‘Severe Cyclonic Storm’ over the West Central and Southwest Bay of Bengal, has led to flight cancellations on November 2, 2026, owing to adverse weather conditions. Flight services to and from Chennai, Vijayawada and Visakhapatnam have been impacted. Chennai International Airport, in a post on social media platform X, said eleven flights have been cancelled to and from Chennai owing to the Cyclone. IndiGo has also confirmed in a post on X that “flight operations to and from Rajahmundry, Vijayawada and Tirupati are impacted.” Cancelled departures from Chennai #FlightUpdate | In view of the adverse weather conditions due to #CycloneMurasu, the following flights have been cancelled. Passengers are requested to contact the concerned airline for further information and assistance. #ChennaiAirport #Cyclone #Murasu #MurasuCyclone #CycloneUpdate #CycloneMurasuUpdate #FlightCancellations #Chennai #Airport #AAIAirports @MoCA_GoI | @AAI_Official | @IndiGo6E | @Pib_MoCA | @PIBChennai Also Read: Cyclone Murasu: 12 flight services cancelled at Vijayawada; Visakhapatnam flights hit IndiGo, in its X post, has said that “We are notifying affected customers on the mobile number provided at the time of booking. Customers are advised to check their flight status before proceeding to the airport.We remain in close coordination with the relevant authorities and continue to closely monitor the situation. The safety and well-being of our customers and crew remain our highest priority.” Chennai Airport has requested passengers to contact the airline for more information and assistance. Travel Advisory Due to adverse weather conditions associated with Tropical Cyclone Murasu, flight operations to and from Rajahmundry, Vijayawada and Tirupati are impacted. 9ef1ec07f605ba03.title: Delhi traders claim ₹10,000-₹11,000 crore loss from INDIA bloc's rally
9ef1ec07f605ba03.summary: Delhi's trading sector suffered an estimated loss of Rs 10,000-11,000 crore due to disruptions caused by the INDIA bloc rally at Ramlila Maidan, Chamber of Trade & Industry (CTI) Chairman Brijesh Goyal claimed on Sunday.Goyal said around 20 to 25 major markets in the vicinity of the rally venue were affected, with approximately 2.5 lakh shops remaining closed out of the nearly three lakh shops in these markets.Speaking about the impact on traders, Goyal said the closures were largely due to panic over the expected arrival of a large number of people and vehicles for the rally."Due to the rally held at Ramlila Maidan today, about 20 to 25 major markets in the vicinity were affected. These historic markets house approximately 3,00,000 shops. Based on data we received this evening from various WhatsApp groups-comprising traders from different markets under the CTA (Confederation of All India Traders)-about 80% of these shops-roughly 2,50,000 out of 3,00,000-remained closed today," .

4576f06676c06a16.title: Suspended Punjab AAP leader Kunwar Vijay Pratap quits as MLA ahead of polls
4576f06676c06a16.summary: Amritsar North MLA Kunwar Vijay Pratap Singh announced his resignation, citing a push for clean politics and transparent administration | File Image: X@Kvijaypratap In a major political development ahead of the 2027 Punjab Assembly elections, Amritsar North MLA Kunwar Vijay Pratap Singh announced his resignation from the Punjab Legislative Assembly on Monday. Kunwar Vijay Pratap Singh was suspended from the Aam Aadmi Party (AAP) on June 29, 2025. In a X post addressed to the people of Amritsar, Singh said he would remain indebted to them "until my last breath" for their love and respect. He called for a collective effort to rise above "the politics of lanes and ribbon-cutting" and to bring Punjab, which he described as "trapped by drugs, extortion, gangsterism and corruption", back to being a progressive state. ਬਹੁਤ ਹੀ ਸਤਿਕਾਰਯੋਗ ਅੰਮ੍ਰਿਤਸਰ ਦੇ ਮੇਰੇ ਭੈਣ-ਭਰਾਵੋਂ, ਪੰਜਾਬ ਵਿਧਾਨ ਸਭਾ ਦੀ ਮੈਂਬਰਸ਼ਿਪ ਤੋਂ ਮੈਂ ਇਸਤੀਫ਼ਾ ਦੇ ਦਿੱਤਾ ਹੈ। ਮੈਂ ਤੁਹਾਡੇ ਵੱਲੋਂ ਮਿਲੇ ਪਿਆਰ ਅਤੇ ਸਤਿਕਾਰ ਵਾਸਤੇ ਆਖ਼ਿਰੀ ਸਾਹ ਤੱਕ ਰਿਣੀ ਰਹਾਂਗਾ। >ਤੁਹਾਡੇ ਸਹਿਯੋਗ ਅਤੇ ਪਰਮਾਤਮਾ ਦੇ ਆਸ਼ੀਰਵਾਦ ਨਾਲ ਗਲੀ-ਨਾਲੀ ਅਤੇ ਰਿਬਨ-ਕਟਿੰਗ ਦੀ ਰਾਜਨੀਤੀ ਤੋਂ ਉੱਪਰ ਉੱਠ ਕੇ ਨਸ਼ਾ, ਫਿਰੌਤੀ, ਗੈਂਗਸਟਰਵਾਦ ਅਤੇ ਭ੍ਰਿਸ਼ਟਾਚਾਰ ਤੋਂ ਜਕੜੇ ਪੰਜਾਬ ਨੂੰ ਮੁੜ ਉੱਨਤਸ਼ੀਲ ਅਤੇ ਮੋਹਰੀ ਸੂਬਾ ਬਣਾਉਣ ਲਈ ਅਸੀਂ ਸਾਰਿਆਂ ਨੇ ਮਿਲ਼ ਕੇ ਇਕਜੁਟ ਪ੍ਰਯਾਸ ਕਰਨਾ ਹੈ। >ਵੈਸੇ ਤੁਸੀਂ ਸਾਰੇ ਜਾਣਦੇ ਹੋ ਕਿ ਮੈਂ ਬਤੌਰ ਵਿਧਾਇਕ ਆਪਣਾ 90 ਪਰਸੈਂਟ ਟਾਰਗੇਟ ਪੂਰਾ ਕਰ ਲਿਆ ਹੈ; ਜੋ ਕੰਮ ਇੱਕ ਵਿਧਾਇਕ ਨੇ ਕਰਨਾ ਹੁੰਦਾ ਹੈ। ਕੌਂਸਲਰ, ਮੇਅਰ ਅਤੇ ਸਾਂਸਦ ਦੇ ਕੰਮ ਇਸਤੋਂ ਇਲਾਵਾ ਹਨ। >ਮੈਂ ਇਲਾਕਾ ਵਾਰ ਆਪਣੇ ਵੱਲੋਂ ਕਰਾਏ ਕੰਮਾਂ ਦਾ ਵੇਰਵਾ ਵੀ ਦਿੱਤਾ ਹੈ ਜੋ ਅਖ਼ਬਾਰ ਅਤੇ ਮੇਰੇ ਫੇਸਬੁੱਕ ਪੇਜ ਤੇ ਮੌਜੂਦ ਹੈ। >ਮੇਰੀ ਸੱਭ ਤੋਂ ਵੱਡੀ ਪ੍ਰਾਪਤੀ ਹੈ ਕਿ ਮੈਂ ਰਾਜਨੀਤੀ ਤੋਂ ਮਾਈ-ਬਾਪ ਕਲਚਰ ਨੂੰ ਖਤਮ ਕੀਤਾ ਅਤੇ ਇੱਕ ਜਨਤਾ ਨੂੰ ਆਪਣਾ ਪ੍ਰੇਰਣਾ-ਸਰੋਤ ਸਮਝ ਕੇ ਕੰਮ ਕੀਤਾ। >ਪੰਜਾਬ ਵਿਧਾਨ ਸਭਾ ਦੇ ਵਿੱਚ ਮੈਂ ਹਮੇਸ਼ਾ ਅੰਬਰਸਰੀਆਂ ਦੀ ਆਵਾਜ ਬੁਲੰਦ ਕੀਤੀ ਅਤੇ ਪਾਣੀ ਸੀਵਰੇਜ ਤੋਂ ਲੈ ਕੇ ਸਰਕਟ ਹਾਊਸ, ਕੰਪਨੀ ਬਾਗ, ਗੰਦਾ ਨਾਲਾ, ਗੁਰੂ ਨਾਨਕ ਦੇਵ ਯੂਨੀਵਰਸਿਟੀ, ਸਰਕਾਰੀ ਮੈਡੀਕਲ ਕਾਲਜ, ਸਰੂਪ ਰਾਣੀ ਕਾਲਜ ਅਤੇ ਬਰਗਾੜੀ ਬੇਅਦਬੀ ਦੇ ਮੁੱਦੇ ਬੇਬਾਕੀ ਨਾਲ ਰੱਖੇ। ਇਹ ਪਹਿਲੀ ਵਾਰ ਹੋਇਆ ਕਿ ਪੰਜਾਬ ਦੀ ਵਿਧਾਨ ਸਭਾ ਦੇ ਵਿੱਚ ਗਲੀ ਅਤੇ ਮੁਹੱਲਾ ਦਾ ਨਾਂ ਲੈ ਕੇ ਇਲਾਕੇ ਵਾਰ ਮੁੱਦੇ ਮੇਰੇ ਵਲੋਂ ਉਠਾਏ ਗਏ। >ਤੁਹਾਡੇ ਨਾਲ ਮਿਲਕੇ ਅੱਗੇ ਦੀ ਸਟ੍

836fbbd76fe0e28f.title: Andhra goes ahead with Kotia local body polls despite Odisha’s plea in Supreme Court
836fbbd76fe0e28f.summary: Updated - November 02, 2026 03:39 pm IST - PARVATIPURAM A resident of Madkar village in the Kotia gram panchayat shows voter cards issued by both the Andhra Pradesh and Odisha governments. Andhra Pradesh is going ahead with local body polls in the disputed villages on November 5. File | Photo Credit: Biswaranjan Rout The Andhra Pradesh government and the State Election Commission are making all arrangements to conduct local body elections in the Kotia group of villages on the Andhra Pradesh-Odisha border, despite strong objections from Odisha. The neighbouring State has approached the Supreme Court to stop the election process in the disputed region. Both the States have been at odds over the jurisdiction of the Kotia group of villages for about seven decades. Both have also been holding local body elections there for many decades. Odisha has objected before: it filed contempt petitions when Andhra Pradesh held polls in the villages in 2021. This time, it filed a fresh contempt petition last month, alleging that the poll notification violates the Supreme Court’s 2006 order directing both States to maintain the status quo. The villages are located 35 km from Salur town of Parvathipuram Manyam district. Since the court has not passed any order on Odisha’s petition, the Parvathipuram Manyam district administration is making all arrangements to hold elections in places like Ganjai Bhadra, Pagalu Chennuru, Pattu Chennuru, Kurukutti, Sarika, Kotia and other villages on November 5, 2026. The YSR Congress Party (YSRCP), which won the Salur Zilla Parishad Territorial Constituency and all four Mandal Parishad Territorial Constituencies in 2021, is keen to win them again with its spirited campaign in all Kotia villages. 7ac472482663b212.title: Cyclone Murasu: Red alert in two Telangana districts, orange in three more on November 3
7ac472482663b212.summary: Updated - November 02, 2026 04:21 pm IST - HYDERABAD Nagarkurnool and Nalgonda districts in Telangana were placed under red alert on Tuesday (November 3, 2026) | Photo Credit: BY ARRANGEMENT With Cyclone Murasu likely to make landfall at Andhra Pradesh coast between evening of Monday (November 2, 2026) and early morning of Tuesday (November 3, 2026), the India Meteorological Department (IMD) has issued a red alert for two Telangana districts and an orange alert in three districts for Tuesday (November 3, 2026). According to the IMDs latest bulletin, a red alert — meaning, heavy to very heavy rain with isolated extremely heavy rainfall — was issued for Nalgonda and Nagarkurnool districts. An orange alert — meaning heavy to very heavy rainfall — was issued for Suryapet, Mahabubnagar and Wanaparthy districts. Additionally, a yellow alert — indicating heavy rainfall with thunderstorms accompanied with lightning and gusty winds — was issued for Mulugu, Bhadradri Kothagudem, Khammam, Mahabubabad, Warangal, Hanumakonda, Jangaon, Yadadri Bhuvanagiri, Rangareddy, Vikarabad, Narayanpet and Jogulamba Gadwal districts. Hyderabad city for the next 24 hours will see a generally cloudy sky. “Moderate to heavy rain or thundershowers by lightning accompanied with gusty winds are very likely to occur in parts of the city towards evening or night. The maximum and minimum temperatures are likely to be 33 C and 23 C respectively’,” as per the bulletin. f0f2e9e125ddf598.title: Shock and regret: scientists react to AI roiling life’s work
f0f2e9e125ddf598.summary: Updated - November 02, 2026 03:42 pm IST For decades, three computer scientists built their careers around an idea about the limits of what computers can do. Artificial intelligence may now have shown it to be wrong: OpenAI and Anthropic each said last week that one of their AI models had disproved the exponential time hypothesis (ETH). The hypothesis holds that some problems are so hard that computers can solve them only by trying nearly every possible answer. Hundreds of studies in computer science and biology rely on it. The claim is the latest in a string of AI results that have shaken academia, setting off soul-searching, most notably among mathematicians, over the value of human expertise and the future of their profession. Russell Impagliazzo and Ramamohan Paturi of the University of California San Diego first proposed the hypothesis around 25 years ago. Ryan Williams of MIT, a leading researcher in the field, had long publicly doubted it. The three are now helping organise an independent review of the claims from the AI companies. Q: How did you feel when you learned that a machine may have overturned this hypothesis? Ryan Williams: I did not fully believe the hypothesis, and I’m on the record as a prominent sceptic. So I felt vindicated. Russell Impagliazzo: I’m afraid I am less cheerful about this than the others. I would have much preferred it to be discovered by a human who could explain their thought process. And I’d like to have shaken the (actual) hand of the person who disproved ETH. Q: What is left for human researchers facing the machine? What would you tell a student? Paturi: These breakthroughs extend the frontier of research, but I believe shaping that frontier and moving it forward remain within human capacity and creativity. I would encourage young students to join. They should learn to use these tools while developing their own judgment. 97c137308f83a282.title: Vasan urges Centre to secure release of T.N. fishermen detained by Sri Lankan Navy
97c137308f83a282.summary: Published - November 02, 2026 04:35 pm IST - CHENNAI G.K. Vasan. File | Photo Credit: M. Govarthan Tamil Maanila Congress (Moopanar) president G.K. Vasan on Monday (November 2, 2026) urged the Central government to take immediate steps to secure the release of seven Tamil Nadu fishermen recently detained by the Sri Lankan Navy . In a statement, the former Union Minister said the fishermen, who had ventured into the sea for fishing, were arrested by the Sri Lankan Navy and their boats confiscated on Sunday (November 1) morning. He expressed concern over the repeated incidents of arrests, harassment and attacks against Tamil Nadu fishermen by the Sri Lankan authorities. Mr. Vasan called upon the Central government to intervene diplomatically with Sri Lanka, ensure the immediate release of the detained fishermen and secure the return of their boats. c987aed75b01f9ef.title: 37% of pre-SIR Form-6 applications rejected due to absence of declaration form
c987aed75b01f9ef.summary: Updated - November 02, 2026 04:35 pm IST - HYDERABAD A large number of applications for fresh voter registration, submitted through Form-6 before the start of Special Intensive Revision, got rejected because they were not accompanied by a declaration form mandated as a prerequisite for enrolment. The image is used for representative purposes only. Shifting goal posts by the Election Commission of India (ECI) with regard to the ongoing Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of the Electoral Rolls have resulted in rejection of tens of thousands of application forms for new voter enrolments in Telangana. A large number of applications for fresh voter registration, submitted through Form-6 before the start of the SIR process, got rejected because they were not accompanied by a declaration form mandated as a prerequisite for enrolment. The declaration form, which was an attachment to the Form-6 exclusively for the SIR process, sought details of the voter or the voter’s parents/relatives from 2002 SIR. In the absence of such details, the applicants were required to submit any of the listed 12 documents as proof of their citizenship. The ECI recently announced that the declaration was not required for submission of Form-6 in States where SIR is not on . It was too late for Telangana, where a large number of voters who had submitted Form-6 before the start of SIR were rejected for lack of the declaration form. As per data obtained from the office of the Telangana Chief Electoral Officer, a total of 5,20,331 applications were received for new enrolments during the pre-SIR period between January 1, 2026 and June 14, 2026. They were not accompanied by the declaration form which was made mandatory only during the SIR process. As per the Registration of Electors Rules, 196, such claims should be exhibited at the office of the Electoral Registration Officer, and disposed of in a week’s time. This was not adhered to, and the forms submitted up to June 14, 2026 are now being processed al

fa68ea5f3342fcdf.title: Cyclone Murasu: Seven fishermen caught in rough seas rescued in Nellore
fa68ea5f3342fcdf.summary: Updated - November 02, 2026 04:10 pm IST - Nellore Fisheries Department officials rescue seven fishermen whose boat was caught in rough seas near Juvvaladinne village in SPSR Nellore district on Monday. | Photo Credit: Special Arrangement SPSR Nellore district officials have rescued seven fishermen who ventured into the sea near Juvvaladinne village in Kavali constituency on Monday (November 2, 2026) morning. They were brought safely to shore after their boat’s engine broke down at sea. Fishermen had been advised not to venture into the sea in view of Cyclone Murasu. Speaking to the media, District Collector Himanshu Shukla said, “Seven fishermen who had set out for a fishing trip from Juvvaladinne Fishing Harbour noticed changes in the sea conditions while off the coast of Nellore and attempted to return to the harbour. However, their boat’s engine broke down en route, leaving them stranded at sea. Surveillance personnel on duty at the harbour spotted this and immediately alerted the relevant authorities.” Officials and local fishermen pull a boat ashore at Patakadapalem in SPSR Nellore district on Monday after its engine failed in seas made rough by Cyclone Murasu. All seven fishermen on board were rescued. Special Arrangement https://t.co/FbNW0z6qGQ The boat’s anchor snapped, and because of the strong waves, the vessel drifted towards Patakadapalem village in Bogole mandal of the district. The officials of the Fisheries Department and the Marine Police responded immediately. With the assistance of local fishermen, they initiated rescue efforts. Initially, reaching the boat proved difficult because of the high waves. Ultimately, they managed to bring the boat to the shore at Patakadapalem and ensured that all fishermen were safe. The District Collector commended the Fisheries Department officials, Marine Police, surveillance personnel and local fishermen for their presence of mind and efforts in saving the lives of the fishermen. 494bf2da99576b8e.title: Cyclone Murasu: CM directs officials to brace for flood into Bapatla district
494bf2da99576b8e.summary: Updated - November 02, 2026 04:47 pm IST - BAPATLA Andhra Pradesh Chief Minister N. Chandrababu Naidu reviews preparations for Cyclone Murasu with district officials through a video conference on Monday. Bapatla district is likely to bear the brunt of the storm. | Photo Credit: Special Arrangement Andhra Pradesh Chief Minister N. Chandrababu Naidu directed officials to take all precautionary measures to prevent loss of life and property in Bapatla district in view of Cyclone Murasu , which has intensified into a severe cyclonic storm. He reviewed the preparedness of district administrations through a video conference on Monday (November 2, 2026), attended by Bapatla Collector Vinod Kumar V. The Chief Minister warned that Bapatla was likely to bear the brunt of the cyclone, since heavy inflows of floodwater were expected through irrigation canals from upstream districts, including Guntur, Palnadu, Prakasam and Markapuram. He asked officials to inspect canal bunds, remain alert for four days of heavy inflows, evacuate people from low-lying areas and establish rehabilitation centres. He also said a special officer would be appointed for Bapatla district. In a review meeting on cyclone preparedness, Mr. Naidu said the District Collectors should be alert to meet any contingency keeping in view the likelihood of heavy rains and gales. 5daf79f1d4fa17b2.title: EVMs vs paper ballots: What makes MLC polls different? | Explained
5daf79f1d4fa17b2.summary: Why are paper ballots still used in MLC elections when India uses Electronic Voting Machines (EVMs) for Lok Sabha and Assembly polls? The BJP-led NDA’s victory in the recent Legislative Council elections has renewed the political debate over EVMs and paper ballots. Ternus, ⁠who took the reins from Tim Cook in September, has overseen the introduction of Apple’s first foldable phone, smart home hub and Apple’s first touch-screen laptops. All of those products began shipping during the company’s current fiscal first quarter, amid ‌what Cook had called a “100-year flood” of rising memory costs. Apple will face scrutiny over three key issues: its crucial holiday-quarter outlook, Ternus’ remarks on AI and the revamped Siri, and ‌rising memory-chip costs that analysts expect to drag quarterly profit growth to its weakest in six ‌quarters. Apple ⁠has been trying to position its AI offerings differently than rivals such as Meta ⁠Platforms’ Muse agent, which took App Store rankings by storm in recent weeks. Rivals such as OpenAI, which Apple is suing over alleged trade-secret theft, are also developing devices aimed at displacing the iPhone as the central device in people’s lives. Apple is marketing Apple’s AI systems toward “everyday people” rather than Silicon Valley insiders, who ​are big users of frontier AI models from the likes of OpenAI. Morgan added that investors want to know

08c48fb1267ea4bf.title: New logo, new inaugural venue: Stage set for iconic Kolkata International Film Festival
08c48fb1267ea4bf.summary: Updated - November 02, 2026 03:00 pm IST - Kolkata New logo of 32nd Kolkata Internation Film Festival was designed by Satyajit Ray’s son filmmaker Sandip Ray, and was unveiled on November 1, 2026. With a new logo in black and saffron and a new venue at Victoria Memorial for the inaugural ceremony, the 32 nd Kolkata International Film Festival (KIFF) is all set to lay the carpet for cine-lovers from across the world from December 16 to December 23 this year. The new logo, which was unveiled on Sunday (November 1, 2026) at Nandan by the festival authority, was redesigned by the son of Satyajit Ray, filmmaker Sandip Ray. The latest logo replaces the previous blue-and-white artwork, which was launched in 2015. The first KIFF under the new Bharatiya Janata Party government in West Bengal is witnessing a complete overhaul, with superstar Tollywood Prosenjit Chatterjee as the KIFF chairperson and veteran actor Mithun Chakraborty as the Chief Advisor. Some other prominent faces of the Bengal film industry, including actor Jeet, Hiran Chatterjee, actor-cum-politician Rudranil Ghosh, and Nandan CEO and KIFF Director Sharmistha Banerjee, were also present at Sunday’s (November 1) event. Addressing the event, Mr. Chatterjee said that the inaugural ceremony of the festival will also take place at Victoria Memorial for the first time. The venues that have earlier been used by the previous Trinamool Congress government since 2011 include Netaji Indoor Stadium and Dhono Dhanyo Auditorium while the festival was also organised at Nandan during the COVID-19 pandemic. Nandan was also the traditional venue for the festival in its initial years. According to the officials, superstars Rajinikanth, Akshay Kumar, and Prabhas may make their maiden appearances at KIFF this year, along with a star-studded lineup from the film industries across the country. The guest list for the inaugural ceremony of the festival may also include Sanjay Dutt, Paresh Rawal, Anupam Kher, Johnny Lever, Kangana Ra

911b88855c3e65da.title: Rain begins in north Andhra ahead of Cyclone Murasu
911b88855c3e65da.summary: Updated - November 02, 2026 02:06 pm IST - VIJAYAWADA Rough waves lash the Palepalem coast near Kothapatnam in Prakasam district on Monday, ahead of Cyclone Murasu’s expected landfall near Ongole. | Photo Credit: Kommuri Srinivas The first rain from Cyclone Murasu has fallen in north coastal Andhra Pradesh, far from where the storm is headed. The central and south coastal districts, which are on red alert, were yet to see any major rainfall on Monday (November 2, 2026). Kakinada (Rural) mandal recorded the most rain between 8.30 a.m. and noon, 51.75 mm at the MRO office gauge, according to real-time data from the Andhra Pradesh Directorate of Economics and Statistics (APDES). Most of the rain fell in Kakinada, Vizianagaram and Srikakulam districts. Visakhapatnam’s highest reading was 12.5 mm at Gambheeram in Anandapuram mandal. Ongole in Prakasam district, where the landfall is likely to happen, had not recorded any rain as of 10 a.m. The Rayalaseema districts stayed dry. 06beca9cee78fcfc.title: ‘Cyclone Murasu’: Palnadu District Collector declares November 2 holiday for schools, colleges
06beca9cee78fcfc.summary: Updated - November 02, 2026 03:00 pm IST - NARASARAOPET (PALNADU DISTRICT) Palnadu District Collector Kritika Shukla. Photo: Special Arranagement Palnadu District Collector Kritika Shukla has announced holiday for all government and private schools, colleges and Anganwadi centres on Tuesday (November 2) in view of Cyclone Murasu. The Collector, in a press release here on Sunday, informed that the district administration has made all necessary arrangements to effectively deal with Cyclone Murasu. Cyclone Murasu LIVE updates: November 02, 2026 A special control room has been set up at the Collectorate to ensure that people do not face any inconvenience due to the cyclone and to facilitate immediate relief measures. The control room will function round-the-clock. Staff have been deployed to provide necessary information to the public and coordinate relief operations. People can contact the control room for emergency assistance or information on the number 08647 252999 In view of the cyclone warnings, the District Collector urged people to remain alert and avoid going outdoors unless absolutely necessary. 51b6d65215f5069a.title: SRN Mehta School-Kalaburagi student selected for national-level chess championship
51b6d65215f5069a.summary: Published - November 02, 2026 12:15 pm IST - KALABURAGI Anish P. More of SRN Mehta State School in Kalaburagi with representatives of the school’s management and teachers after securing fifth place in the State-level under-14 chess championship and qualifying for the national-level competition. | Photo Credit: ARUN KULKARNI Anish P. More, a student of SRN Mehta School in Kalaburagi, has been selected to participate in the national-level chess championship to be held in Madhya Pradesh after securing fifth place in the State-level under-14 chess competition. The tournament was organised by the Department of Public Instruction at Gangavati in Koppal district of Karnataka from October 15 to 17 as part of the 2026-27 academic year’s sports competitions. Anish’s achievement has brought recognition to his school and Kalaburagi district. The school management’s trustee Chakore Mehta, Principal Preeti Mehta, Head of the Physical Education Department Basavaraj Talakeri, chess coach Pramod More, and other teachers congratulated the student on his achievement and expressed happiness over his selection for the national-level competition. 1eff5fc8eac5c5a4.title: Coast Guard evacuates fisherman in distress 100 km off Mangaluru coast
1eff5fc8eac5c5a4.summary: Updated - November 02, 2026 01:24 pm IST - MANGALURU Indian Coast Guard Ship C-448 reaches Indian fishing boat Shiv Sagar, about 100 km off the Mangaluru coast, to rescue a fisherman in urgent need of medical attention on the night of November 1, 2026. | Photo Credit: SPECIAL ARRANGEMENT Indian Coast Guard (ICG), District Headquarter 3, Mangaluru, safely evacuated a fisherman in urgent need of medical attention from a fishing vessel sailing about 100 km off Mangaluru coast on November 1 night. The headquarters received a distress call over VHF from Indian Fishing Boat (IFB) Shiv Sagar, operating approximately 54 NM (100 km) off Mangaluru on November 1. They were told that a fisherman had fallen overboard while hauling fishing nets. He was rescued, but required urgent medical attention, and shifting to a hospital. The ICG deployed Indian Coast Guard Ship C-448, which located the fishing boat amid the darkness of the night. The disoriented fisherman, identified as Komara Ramu, was safely evacuated, provided immediate first aid, and transferred to New Mangalore Port Authority jetty. He was subsequently shifted to the nearest hospital for further medical management. IFB Shiv Sagar had sailed out of Old Mangaluru Port three days ago, ICG informed. a00438c594b93c32.title: KBN Hospital hosts workshop on hysterectomy and advanced laparoscopy in Kalaburagi
a00438c594b93c32.summary: Updated - November 02, 2026 12:18 pm IST - KALABURAGI Dignitaries inaugurate the advanced live laparoscopy workshop organised by Khaja Banda Nawaz University and the Karnataka State Obstetrics and Gynaecology Association at KBNTGH in Kalaburagi on October 30, 2026. | Photo Credit: ARUN KULKARNI A workshop on ‘Hysterectomy: Different Approaches and Advanced Laparoscopy’ was conducted at Khaja Banda Nawaz Teaching and General Hospital (KBNTGH) in Kalaburagi on October 30 as part of the conference of the Karnataka State Obstetrics and Gynaecology Association (KSOGA), in collaboration with Khaja Banda Nawaz University. The workshop provided a platform for gynaecologists and medical professionals to interact with experts and gain insights into the latest technologies, techniques and developments in the field. Around 150 delegates from different parts of Karnataka had registered for the programme. Ten surgical procedures performed in the operation theatre were telecast live to the seminar hall, enabling participants to observe the procedures, and interact with experts during the sessions. Highlighting the importance of the workshop, Professor Syed Ashfaq Ahmed said it could bring positive changes to the lives of many women by promoting awareness and knowledge of modern treatment options. He said participants had benefited from direct interaction with specialists and gained valuable information about recent advances in medical technology. He reiterated the hospital’s commitment to providing quality healthcare to all sections of society, particularly the poor and needy. He said the hospital was upgrading its departments with advanced technology to emerge as a leading, well-equipped medical centre in the region. It was also organising free medical screening and treatment camps regularly to protect public health, he added. edcf897aced216ff.title: Indian Bank targets ₹100 crore lending under EV charging scheme in FY27: MD
edcf897aced216ff.summary: Indian Bank has set a lending target of Rs 100 crore for the current fiscal year under its dedicated financing scheme for electric vehicle (EV) charging infrastructure, as the public sector lender seeks to tap business opportunities in the fast-growing green mobility segment. The bank has launched 'IND Green Charge', a financing scheme for public, captive and fleet charging stations under both standalone and franchise models. The bank will offer loans of up to Rs 10 crore for a maximum tenure of 8 years, Indian Bank MD and CEO Binod Kumar told PTI. "We have set lending targets of Rs 100 crore for the remaining five months of the ongoing financial year and Rs 250 crore for the coming financial year under this scheme," he said. The initiative aims to promote entrepreneurship among micro, small and medium enterprises (MSMEs), generate employment and support India's transition towards sustainable mobility, he added. According to reports, EV sales grew 29.7 per cent to 26.59 lakh units

351ef5661d84b3fb.title: Hyundai Motor India sales hit record 82,299 units in October, up 17.7%
351ef5661d84b3fb.summary: Hyundai Motor India Limited (HMIL) on Sunday reported its highest-ever total monthly sales, including exports, of 82,299 units in October, a 17.7 per cent year-on-year rise. The milestone was driven by record domestic sales of 62,799 units, a 16.7 per cent rise, and exports grew 21.1 per cent to 19,500 units, the automaker said. Tarun Garg, MD & CEO - HMIL, said, "Strong festive demand, coupled with healthy momentum in both domestic and export markets, helped us set this new sales record. Going forward, the newly launched Hyundai BAYON - our Intelligent Utility Vehicle, will provide further impetus to our growth in India as well as across 50+ export markets, reinforcing India's role as a strategic manufacturing and export hub for Hyundai".

7751d2870f6a8c29.title: Escorts Kubota reports 10% decline in October sales to 16,921 units
7751d2870f6a8c29.summary: Escorts Kubota Ltd on Sunday reported a 10 per cent year-on-year decline in total tractor sales to 16,921 tractors in October from 18,798 a year earlier. Its domestic tractor sales fell 10.9 per cent to 16,412 tractors compared to 18,423 units in the year-ago period. However, the company's exports rose 35.7 per cent to 509 units in October against 375 units in the year-ago period. The industry witnessed some moderation in October 2026, impacted by a high base, shift in festive timing and monsoon-related disruptions. Elevated input costs due to geopolitical developments and consequent pricing actions may moderate demand in the near term, the company said in a release.

eff9335dce1a201a.title: Sebi extends digital accessibility compliance deadline to January 31
eff9335dce1a201a.summary: Sebi has extended the deadline for regulated entities to complete key digital accessibility compliance requirements to January 31 next year, following requests from market participants. In a circular dated October 30, Sebi said the extension covers the appointment of an International Association of Accessibility Professionals (IAAP) auditor, conducting accessibility audits of digital platforms and remediation of findings arising from the audits. The requirements are part of Sebi's earlier circulars on mandatory compliance with the Rights of Persons with Disabilities Act, 2016, and the rules framed thereunder by all regulated entities. In July-September, the company's total income reduced by 5.7 per cent to Rs 1,505 crore from Rs 1,596 crore a year ago. In Q2 FY2, the company's EBITDA also fell 2.7 per cent year-on-year to Rs 564 crore from Rs 580 crore in July-September of FY26. However, in April-September, its PAT grew 4.5 per cent to Rs 799 crore from Rs 764 crore in the year-ago period. Sarda Energy & Minerals Limited (SEML) is an integrated energy and minerals company with interests spanning power generation, mining, steel and ferro alloys.

eb1eeb2f5d1fe4a5.title: Gross GST collections rise 23% to ₹2.31 trillion in October on strong sales
eb1eeb2f5d1fe4a5.summary: Gross GST collections increased 23 per cent to over Rs 2.31 lakh crore in October, driven by strong mop-up from domestic activities and imports, according to government data released on Sunday. Gross GST collections from domestic sales rose 16 per cent to over Rs 1.59 lakh crore, and revenues from imports climbed 42 per cent to Rs 72,246 crore. The Rs 2.31 lakh crore collection includes Central GST mop-up of 42,935 crore, State GST of Rs 51,340 crore and Integrated GST of over Rs 1.37 lakh crore, data showed. Goods and Services Tax (GST) refunds increased 6.5 per cent year-on-year to Rs 27,934 crore in October. After adjusting for refunds, net GST collections rose 26 per cent to over Rs 2.03 lakh crore in October. During April-October, gross GST collection grew 13.2 per cent to over Rs 14.77 lakh crore. Net collections rose 13 per cent to over Rs 12.69 lakh crore.

4af26c97f834c2fc.summary: The Securities and Exchange Board of India (SEBI) is working towards removing companies with no economic activity from the stock exchanges, as their continued presence in the listed space poses a potential risk to investors, a top official said. There are a number of listed companies with no economic activity, SEBI chairman Tuhin Kanta Pandey said. "They pose a potential danger to investors, and therefore, it is necessary to remove them from the listed space. We are making efforts towards their delisting," Pandey said here on Saturday during a programme. From the perspective of market integrity, it is important to address the presence of such companies, as their continued listing could expose an increasing number of investors to potential risks through social media groups, he said. Mr. Carney said on the social ‌media site X that ‌their ⁠exchange “builds on recent constructive ⁠discussions on the outlines of a mutually beneficial trade deal” that would create ​jobs, improve affordability, ‌and fully respect Canada’s languages, culture, and sovereignty. “Our teams will now be working in the ‌coming weeks to deliver that ​outcome,” Mr. Carney said. 77959aa04b44f5f2.title: I was offered ₹5 crore to make someone Iyal Isai Nataka Mandram president: Rajmohan
77959aa04b44f5f2.summary: Published - November 02, 2026 12:26 am IST - Chennai School Education Minister Rajmohan. | Photo Credit: R. RAGU Tamil Nadu Minister for Information and Publicity Rajmohan on Sunday alleged that he was offered ₹5 crore as bribe to appoint someone as the president of the Iyal Isai Nataka Mandram. Participating at the Tamil Nadu Day event celebrations at Egmore in Chennai, the Minister said: “I have not revealed this before. [Tamil Nadu Textbook Corporation chief] Layola Mani knows this. A person said, ‘If I am given the post of president of the Iyal Isai Nataka Mandram, I will offer ₹5 crore to Minister Rajmohan’. I smiled and told Layola Mani, even if someone offers ₹500 crore as bribe, I will not give the post to someone who is not suited for it. Without even getting a single rupee from anyone, Pushpavanam Kuppusamy, who is the most suited for the role, was appointed as the president of the association.” According to him, for the first time in Tamil Nadu, every Minister [in the C Joseph Vijay cabinet] hates bribery and corruption. Meanwhile, AIADMK leader D. Jayakumar questioned the identity of the person who allegedly offered to bribe Mr. Rajmohan and said the person should be prosecuted. Speaking to reporters, he said: “There is no doubt that Pushpavanam Kuppusamy is the right person for that post. But, who was the one who came forward through [Chairman of the Tamil Nadu Textbook and Educational Services Corporation] Layola Mani to offer ₹5 crore? Should that person not be brought before the law?” Mr. Jayakumar added: “If Chief Minister C. Joseph Vijay was honest, he should name the person and prosecute him.” Published - November 02, 2026 12:26 am IST Terms & conditions | Institutional Subscriber Comments have to be in English, and in full sentences. 5b5aaf3e99e3b146.title: Slow recovery: On the ISRO’s GSLV-F18 mission
5b5aaf3e99e3b146.summary: Published - November 02, 2026 12:53 am IST With the successful launch of the GSLV-F18 mission and the NVS-03 satellite’s healthy status , the Indian Space Research Organisation (ISRO) is on course to heave a sigh of relief. Its last 18 months have been constrained by the consequences of two launch failures involving PSLV rockets , which share some of their design aspects with GSLV, to the extent that the F18 mission was only the second successful launch of 2026. If the NVS-03 satellite is successfully manoeuvred into its final intended orbital slot and commissioned, ISRO will also have pulled off a rescue mission for the ‘Navigation with Indian Constellation’ (NavIC) programme , which has been at least one functional satellite short for the last six months and thus unable to meet its primary purpose of providing standalone positioning services over the Indian subcontinent. The three second-generation NVS satellites thus far are distinguished by having at least one indigenously made atomic clock onboard, in line with the recommendations of the Parliamentary Standing Committee (PSC) on Science and Technology and India’s investments in quantum timekeeping, and away from the imported clocks onboard the first-generation IRNSS satellites. The PSC had also flagged procurement bottlenecks across ISRO’s programmes, including difficulties with obtaining specialised components and ensuring vendor readiness on the timelines that NavIC needs. The ISRO Space Applications Centre’s ‘request for proposals’ in 2025 also specified a large lead time of nearly two years between a contract’s start and the first two flight models. The Electronics Component Manufacturing Scheme and the programme to modernise the Semiconductor Laboratory can be tweaked to serve these needs, with the Electronics Ministry also setting aside dedicated funds for developing specialised components and their qualification tests in a five- to seven-year programme. 5853f885cfa5693d.title: Alcaraz beats De Minaur to win Vienna Open without dropping a set to clinch fourth title this year
5853f885cfa5693d.summary: Published - November 02, 2026 05:14 am IST - Vienna Spain's Carlos Alcaraz poses with the trophy after winning the men's singles final against Australia's Alex de Minaur during the Vienna Open ATP tennis tournament in Vienna, Austria, on November 1, 2026. | Photo Credit: AP Seven-time Grand Slam winner Carlos Alcaraz beat Alex de Minaur 6-1, 6-4 to win the Vienna Open on Sunday (November 1, 2026) and defeat his opponent for the seventh time in as many meetings. Alcaraz has beaten the Australian on grass and clay as well as on indoor and outdoor hard courts. He sealed his latest victory with trademark panache. Alcaraz drew his opponent to the net with a sliced backhand drop shot. De Minaur retrieved it but Alcaraz lobbed him with a backhand and, after the Australian volleyed that shot back near the net, clipped a cross-court forehand that landed just in. The second-seeded Spaniard looked jubilant and cracked a broad smile after clinching his fourth title this year — including the Australian Open for a career Grand Slam — and his 28th overall. The fifth-seeded De Minaur was looking for his second title of the year. He advanced to the final of the ATP 500 event with a semifinal win against Alexander Zverev, who will top the rankings on Monday (November 2, 2026). Alcaraz beat Daniil Medvedev in the other semi.
