0b6e9aeb65c95fdd.title: Dwindling support: On the U.S. and the Cuban embargo
0b6e9aeb65c95fdd.summary: Updated - November 02, 2026 12:46 am IST Nearly every year since 1992, the United Nations General Assembly has passed a resolution calling on the U.S. to end its decades-old economic embargo on Cuba . As a result, the outcome at the UNGA resolution titled the ‘Necessity of ending the economic, commercial and financial embargo imposed by the United States of America against Cuba’ passed on October 30, was expected. Surprisingly, the support for the resolution this year was dramatically lower than previous years. For the preceding decade, more than 180 countries of the 193-member UNGA had expressed their support for ending the embargo, but the numbers dropped to 165 in favour in 2025; this year’s tally dropped sharply lower, with 130 in favour, 25 abstaining and 17 countries voting against the resolution. The trend clearly points to efforts by the Trump administration to use its pressure on countries to change their votes, and many appear to have succumbed to those threats. Among those were several Latin American countries, that have more recently grown closer to the U.S., particularly after the operation in Venezuela in January 2026 , where U.S. marines abducted President Maduro and brought him to the U.S. for a trial. Countries in the region such as Costa Rica, Ecuador, Argentina, and Colombia that have downgraded ties with Havana, switched votes on the resolution. In addition, U.S. diplomats argued that Havana-Moscow ties emboldened Russia’s war in Ukraine , which led to several western countries switching their vote. Diplomats from Ukraine and Poland, for example, referred to Cuba’s ties with Russia while explaining their vote, and Germany and Italy switched for the first time in many years to abstaining on the resolution. While it is clear that the bulk of the Group of 77 and non-aligned states including India maintained their support on the resolution for Cuba, the vote by the others demonstrates a disquieting turn. Amidst these turns, New Delhi must be credited

6c515e1ea67140f6.title: 25 Cattle rescued while being transported to Keralam for slaughter
6c515e1ea67140f6.summary: Published - November 02, 2026 12:18 am IST - CHENNAI The cattle were found crammed inside the container, with little space to stand. | Photo Credit: Special Arrangement Twenty-five heads of cattle allegedly being transported from Andhra Pradesh to Kerala for slaughter were rescued by the police near Pazhavali, near Maraimalai Nagar, on Saturday evening.. The complaint was filed by Sai Vignesh, president of Almighty Animal Care Trust, who said that he noticed cow dung and urine leaking from a container truck near Maraimalai Nagar, and alerted the police through an emergency helpline. The police intercepted the vehicle near Pazhavali after a chase. The cattle were found crammed inside the container, with little space to stand. Their nose ropes had been tied to bars on the roof, and several animals had sustained injuries. The vehicle allegedly lacked adequate ventilation and provisions for food and drinking water. Following the intervention, all 25 cattle were handed over to Gosamrakshana Gaushala for medical treatment and care. Mr. Vignesh also lodged a formal complaint with the police seeking action against those responsible. 810a887f6caf2122.title: Lifter Usha tops her 61kg group, Nirupama finishes disappointing 4th in Group C at World Championships
810a887f6caf2122.summary: Published - November 02, 2026 05:46 am IST - Ningbo (China) Indian weightlifter Usha topped Group D, while compatriot Nirupama Devi endured a disappointing outing to finish fourth in Group C of the women's 61kg competition at the IWF World Championships in Ningbo on Sunday (November 1, 2026). The 23-year-old Usha lifted a total of 212kg — 93kg in snatch and 119kg in clean and jerk — to finish ahead of all the lifters in her group and several competitors in the higher Group C as well. Nirupama, who has moved down from the 63kg weight class, managed a total of 211kg (91kg+120kg), one kilogram short of Usha's effort despite being placed in Group C owing to her higher entry total. Following the completion of Groups C and D, Usha was placed third overall while Nirupama was fifth. Their final standings will be updated after the completion of Group A. Usha started with a successful 90kg snatch before failing to lift 93kg in her next attempt, but the Indian regained her composure to clear the same weight in her third and final snatch attempt. In the clean and jerk as well, Usha managed to complete two of her three attempts. After successfully lifting 115kg and 119kg, she faltered in her final attempt of 121kg. On the other hand, Nirupama just managed to register a total after completing the minimum two successful lifts. She started with a failed attempt at 91kg in snatch but managed to lift the weight in her second attempt before failing to clear 93kg in her third. In the clean and jerk, she lifted 120kg before failing in both attempts to heave 124kg. At the World Championships, Group A comprises lifters with the highest declared entry totals — the combined weight they intend to lift in the snatch and clean and jerk — while Groups B, C and D feature athletes with progressively lower entry totals. The World Championships is one of six events in the first period of the Olympic qualification system for the 2028 Los Angeles Games. Published - November 02, 2026 05:46 am IST Term

b1ed1a0c8ea58afc.title: GVMC polls record 51% turnout with Bheemunipatnam leading at 65%
b1ed1a0c8ea58afc.summary: Published - November 02, 2026 12:09 am IST - VISAKHAPATNAM Voters wait in a queue to exercise their franchise at a polling booth in Peda Jalaripeta, in the East Assembly Constituency during the Greater Visakhapatnam Municipal Corporation elections in Visakhapatnam on Sunday. | Photo Credit: V RAJU Barring a few alleged irregularities and violations of the Model Code of Conduct (MCC), the Greater Visakhapatnam Municipal Corporation (GVMC) election elections passed off peacefully on Sunday. The city registered a voter turnout of 51.47%, according to preliminary figures released by the election authorities at 9:30 p.m. The final polling percentage is yet to be released. The turnout this time was considerably lower than the 59.41% recorded in the previous GVMC elections held in 2021. Of the 18.37 lakh registered voters across the city, 9,45,915 exercised their franchise. They included 4.55 lakh men and 4.90 lakh are women. Nearly 8.91 lakh voters stayed away from casting their votes, according to the preliminary report. Ward No. 105 in Aganampudi recorded the lowest turnout of 28%, while Ward No. 5 in the Bheemunipatnam Zone registered the highest at 74.69%. Among the zones, Bheemunipatnam topped the list with a turnout of 65.90%, followed by Anakapalli at 65.54%. Gajuwaka, which has the highest voter population of around 2.98 lakh, recorded a turnout of 54.10%, while Aganampudi registered 53.46%. The South Zone, which includes One Town recorded a turnout of 51.24%, followed by the West Zone with Gopalapatnam, Simhachalam, and Malkapuram registering 51.21%, and Madhurawada with 50.81%. The East Zone registered 50.55%, while Pendurthi recorded 48.93%. The North Zone, which includes prominent residential localities such as Seethammadhara and Balayya Sastry Layout, witnessed the lowest turnout among these zones at 44.24%. Polling began on a sluggish note, particularly in the densely populated urban areas. The first two hours, between 7 a.m. and 9 a.m., witnessed a turnout

2aff8262e3f0b1de.title: Asian Champions Trophy: Harmanpreet’s hat-trick helps India down Malaysia
2aff8262e3f0b1de.summary: Updated - November 02, 2026 12:09 am IST - Jalandhar Harmanpreet, centre, converted two penalty corners and a penalty stroke. | Photo Credit: X@TheHockeyIndia It was expected to be India’s toughest test of the tournament and the match between the two highest ranked sides in the competition lived up to its billing. Malaysia tested the host before India prevailed 4-2 to remain the only unbeaten side at the Asian Champions Trophy here on Sunday. The penultimate day of the league competition at the Olympian Surjeet Stadium also confirmed the semifinalists with Japan and Korea completing the line-up. The rematch between the Asian Games finalists was a much closer affair but it was also more tactical as well. A lot of play was confined to the midfield with neither team being in complete control but neither willing to pull back either. India took an early lead when Harmanpreet Singh converted the team’s first penalty corner in the third minute but then missed a couple of chances up front. With both teams well matched in every department, it was more a battle of attrition than one of skills. Compared to the final in Nagoya, Malaysia was more compact and read the Indian team better, anticipating the overlapping and passes and using short passes to try and break the flow. On the other hand, India found its own way around, pressing harder off the ball and being inventive with the passing. Both coach Craig Fulton and captain Harmanpreet admitted that the finishing needed to be clinical. “We created chances, it is up to us to make use of them,” Fulton agreed. Harmanpreet got a hat-trick, converting another PC in the 33rd and a penalty stroke in the 58th. Malaysia equalised through Akhimullah Anuar to be level at half time, then Shello Silverius pulled one back in the final seconds. But the Tamil Nadu Tennis Association had promised Dipakbhai Kanabar that Shrivalli’s wild card will be reallocated to Jensi, his 14-year-old daughter and India’s second-best female junior, provided they were onsite and a few withdrawals led to Shrivalli entering the draw based on her ranking. Dipakbhai and Jensi took a leap of faith. They made the 10-hour journey from Junagadh, a city in western Gujarat, to Chennai. “We thought that if we got in, fine. Otherwise, we will visit some temples in Rameswaram and Madurai before heading back,” said Dipakbhai. Coached by Dipakbhai, a schoolteacher by profession, Jensi is already amongst the world’s top-50 juniors. She has also played two women’s ITFs but Tour-level tennis is a different ball game. Jensi was up against Polish World No. 287 Weronika Falkowska, a player 12 years older and 13cm taller than her. Falkowska won 6-2, 5-7, 6-3 but the teenager made her sweat for more than two hours under the floodlights on Saturday evening. The Pole initially overpowered Jensi, but in the second set the Indian could read Falkowska’s serve. Falkowska tried surprising Jensi with drop shots and the Indian responded with impressive court coverage. The Pole attempted closing the net but on multiple occasions, ended up watching gorgeous passing forehands from Jensi. Facing a left-handed player, quite uncommon in the sport, added to the tension Falkowska was feeling. “In the second set, Falkowska was unable to handle the shots hit into her body,” said Jensi. The Pole, however, gathered her composure and edged the teenager in the decider. 60b87fabad4ffcec.title: Marquez wins in Malaysia to stand on brink of MotoGP world title
60b87fabad4ffcec.summary: Published - November 02, 2026 05:32 am IST - Sepang, Malaysia Ducati Lenovo Team's Marc Marquez celebrates after winning the MotoGP race of the Malaysian Grand Prix at Sepang International Circuit, Sepang, Malaysia on November 1, 2026. | Photo Credit: Reuters Marc Marquez moved to the brink of an eighth world title with an imperious victory at the Malaysian MotoGP on Sunday (November 1, 2026). The Ducati star romped to a dominant win in 40min 14.236sec, finishing 4.172sec ahead of Red Bull’s Pedro Acosta as his younger brother Alex Marquez came third, almost six seconds adrift. Marquez, who is now 44 points ahead of his closest rival Jorge Martin, has seven victories to his name this season. It was also his third triumph in Malaysia in the MotoGP class, having last won in Sepang back in 2018. With Aprilia’s Martin missing the Sepang weekend with a broken wrist, his fellow Spaniard Marquez can seal the championship next weekend in Qatar. Marquez wasted no time in snatching the lead from his brother as the riders came into Turn 1 from the start, and the siblings briefly traded places before the older Marquez just edged ahead in scorching conditions. Saturday’s sprint race winner Acosta tailed both the Marquez brothers closely in third, with Italian Marco Bezzecchi in fourth and Japan’s Ai Ogura in fifth. Championship leader Marquez, 33, began to pull away from the chasing pack to develop a 1.7 sec advantage over his brother, who was valiantly defending his second spot against Acosta. Acosta would be rewarded for his persistence as the Red Rull rider snatched second place from Alex Marquez in Lap 10. At the front Marquez coasted to victory unchallenged to continue his purple streak in the second half of the 2026 season. After Qatar there are just two weekends left in the campaign. 6fdc3913b4479f9d.title: 800 houses in Division 59 of Kochi Corporation to get sewerage connection by December
6fdc3913b4479f9d.summary: Published - November 02, 2026 07:00 am IST - KOCHI The Kerala Water Authority's sewage treatment plant at Elamkulam in Kochi. STPs had been proposed in three divisions, including Edakochi North. | Photo Credit: file photo Around 800 houses in Division 59 (Edakochi South) will be connected to the sewerage network linked to the 1.1-MLD sewage treatment plant (STP) in the first phase of the project by December. With the project nearing completion, half of the houses in the division will be connected to the new STP, which is expected to cover around 1,800 households. “The construction work on the STP has been completed. The installation of electro-mechanical components remains, and the work is progressing,” said a KWA source. The sewage pipeline to be laid within the division will have a total length of 18 km. “Of this, only 200 m of the pipeline remains to be laid. Pipelines have been laid in front of all the houses, and interceptor tanks have been installed within their compounds. The only work remaining is to connect these tanks to the kitchens. This work has been completed in over 150 houses,” said an official. The decentralised sewerage system is being implemented under the Atal Mission for Rejuvenation and Urban Transformation (AMRUT) STP project. The STP is being set up on land owned by the Kochi Corporation near Ambedkar Colony in Edakochi. If the plant proves successful, similar decentralised plants can be set up in other divisions of the city, the official said. K.J. Baisil, councillor of Division 58 (Edakochi North), said decentralised STPs help manage sewage more effectively than centralised plants. “Earlier, STPs were proposed in three divisions, including Edakochi North. There was opposition to setting up a plant in the division, largely due to misconceptions among residents. Eventually, however, the inability to find suitable land in the division proved to be a hindrance,” said Mr. Baisil. Published - November 02, 2026 07:00 am IST Terms & conditions | In

56be8f59dd04b474.title: Science Snapshots: November 1, 2026
56be8f59dd04b474.summary: Published - November 02, 2026 07:00 am IST A view of the Rub al-Khali quarter of the desert in Saudi Arabia in 2007. | Photo Credit: Javierblas (CC BY-SA) Even in a desert, early humans sought more than water More than water alone guided humans in the ancient Arabian Peninsula. Scientists earlier believed human populations expanded across ‘Green Arabia’ wherever lakes formed. But after surveying a 1,500-km stretch in the Rub’ al Khali desert, researchers found evidence of 55 extinct lakes but no stone tools or signs of life. Since early humans relied on stone tools for survival, the team concluded human migration was guided by the availability of both water and toolmaking stones. 12a9b6d4922e2a92.title: ‘Murasu’ strengthens into Severe Cyclonic Storm
12a9b6d4922e2a92.summary: Updated - November 02, 2026 07:01 am IST - VIJAYAWADA Cyclonic Storm ‘Murasu’ intensified into a Severe Cyclonic Storm over the West Central and Southwest Bay of Bengal. A scene at Marina Beach on November 1 | Photo Credit: Velankanni Raj B Cyclonic Storm ‘Murasu’ intensified into a Severe Cyclonic Storm over the West Central and Southwest Bay of Bengal in the early hours on Monday (November 2). As per observations made by the IMD at 2.30 a.m., the storm lay centered over the same region, which is about 260 km east-northeast of Chennai, 290 km east-southeast of Nellore, 320 km south-southeast of Machilipatnam, 310 km east-southeast of Kavali, 330 km southeast of Ongole and 470 km south of Vishakhapatnam. The system may continue to move northwestwards and cross south Andhra Pradesh coast, near Ongole, as a Severe Cyclonic Storm with wind speed of 100 to 110 kmph gusting 120 kmph. The rainfall activity has begun in parts of the State as of 6 a.m. Extremely heavy rainfall alert has been issued for the five districts of Eluru, Krishna, Guntur, Bapatla and SPSR Nellore, and very heavy rainfall is likely in the districts of NTR, Eluru, East and West Godavari, Palnadu, Chittoor and Tirupati for Monday, November 1. Ashok unveiling the ‘HMT Kannadiga’ wristwatches, in Bengaluru on Sunday. | Photo Credit: ALLEN EGENUSE J. Union Minister for Heavy Industries and Steel H.D. Kumaraswamy on Sunday unveiled a new collection of watches by Hindustan Machine Tools (HMT), named “HMT Kannadiga”, to mark the 71st Karnataka Rajyotsava. The watches will soon be available at the HMT stores in the city. Hundreds of people thronged the HMT grounds in north Bengaluru. However, much to their disappointment, the watches were not yet available for purchase. The new collection comprises four different variants, although the design remains the same. The watches come with different strap and chain options. To emphasise the essence of the language, the dials feature Kannada numericals. A Gandabherunda emblem highlights Kannada pride, while the yellow-and-red Kannada flag and the series name, “HMT Kannadiga”, underscore regional identity. The watches are estimated to be priced at ₹3,500 and ₹3,600, placing them in the HMT’s premium segment. Meanwhile, pictures of the watches released on Saturday have been widely shared on social media and among groups of watch aficionados. According to officials, the watches will feature modern technology and a radium glow. The strap variants will be fitted with genuine Italian leather straps. Ashok unveiling the ‘HMT Kannadiga’ wristwatches, in Bengaluru on Sunday. | Photo Credit: ALLEN EGENUSE J. Union Minister for Heavy Industries and Steel H.D. Kumaraswamy on Sunday unveiled a new collection of watches by Hindustan Machine Tools (HMT), named “HMT Kannadiga”, to mark the 71st Karnataka Rajyotsava. The watches will soon be available at the HMT stores in the city. Hundreds of people thronged the HMT grounds in north Bengaluru. However, much to their disappointment, the watches were not yet available for purchase. The new collection comprises four different variants, although the design remains the same. The watches come with different strap and chain options. To emphasise the essence of the language, the dials feature Kannada numericals. A Gandabherunda emblem highlights Kannada pride, while the yellow-and-red Kannada flag and the series name, “HMT Kannadiga”, underscore regional identity. The watches are estimated to be priced at ₹3,500 and ₹3,600, placing them in the HMT’s premium segment. Meanwhile, pictures of the watches released on Saturday have been widely shared on social media and among groups of watch aficionados. According to officials, the watches will feature modern technology and a radium glow. The strap variants will be fitted with genuine Italian leather straps. 4c42c293f417f8e6.title: Two dead in Gokarna beach, one goes missing
4c42c293f417f8e6.summary: Published - November 01, 2026 11:53 pm IST - Belagavi Two IT professionals from Bengaluru drowned in a beach near Gokarna in Uttara Kannada on Sunday, while another one has gone missing. A team of 16 employees from Alorica Ecospace had come on a holiday to Koje resort near Dubbanshashi beach near Gokarna. They entered the sea waters in the morning but were caught in the strong waves. Twentytwo-year-old Shobha Das of Jamshedpur and Mohammad Akram from Bengaluru drowned. Fishermen and locals brought them to the shore and shifted them to a hospital in Gokarna. Shobha Das died in the hospital, while Akram died on the way to a hospital in Manipal. Twentyfour-year-old Vishwa A.K., who has gone missing, is yet to be traced. 967d6c8c641288c5.title: GST decriminalisation decisions mark shift to trust-based governance: CII
967d6c8c641288c5.summary: Industry body CII on Sunday described the GST Council's decisions to decriminalise certain offences and rationalise enforcement powers as a significant institutional reform, saying the move marks a shift towards trust-based economic governance and offers a model for India's next generation of economic reforms. On the decisions taken at the GST Council's October 8 meeting, CII said the consensus-driven approach showed how the Centre and states could work together on difficult reforms to improve the relationship between the government and businesses. CII Director General Chandrajit Banerjee said, "The GST Council's decisions deserve special recognition as a landmark institutional reform. We deeply appreciate the leadership of Prime Minister Narendra Modi and Finance Minister Nirmala Sitharaman in advancing this transformation, and the constructive role of state governments in achieving consensus on an issue involving sensitive questions of enforcement, revenue protection and taxpayer .

ad386963cafc689e.title: ‘Cyclone Murasu’: Palnadu District Collector declares November 2 holiday for schools, colleges over
ad386963cafc689e.summary: Updated - November 02, 2026 12:06 am IST - NARASARAOPET (PALNADU DISTRICT) Palnadu District Collector Kritika Shukla has announced holiday for all government and private schools, colleges and Anganwadi centres on Tuesday (November 2) in view of Cyclone Murasu. The Collector, in a press release here on Sunday, informed that the district administration has made all necessary arrangements to effectively deal with Cyclone Murasu. A special control room has been set up at the Collectorate to ensure that people do not face any inconvenience due to the cyclone and to facilitate immediate relief measures. The control room will function round-the-clock. Staff have been deployed to provide necessary information to the public and coordinate relief operations. People can contact the control room for emergency assistance or information on the number 08647 252999 In view of the cyclone warnings, the District Collector urged people to remain alert and avoid going outdoors unless absolutely necessary. 5105340bf45a0333.title: Solex Energy eyeing US market for international debut, says chairman
5105340bf45a0333.summary: Eyeing a footprint in the global renewable energy market, homegrown Solex Energy plans to establish solar module and cell manufacturing capacities in the US as part of its USD 1.5 billion investment roadmap through 2030. In an interaction, the company's Chairman Chetan Shah said that while the US remains the largest global solar market, steep anti-dumping duties on Chinese imports leave India as the sole viable supplier of low-cost alternatives. When asked whether Solex Energy is exploring expansion in the US, he replied in the affirmative. Sharing the rationale behind the move, he said Solex Energy is targeting the US market for expansion primarily to capitalise on the massive global demand for clean energy components while positioning itself as a reliable, cost-effective alternative to Chinese suppliers. "The US is a high-potential market. While many Indian corporates are already present there, a healthy number of business houses, including us, are also looking to invest there,"

76859e4a55e99067.title: A.P. seeks assistance from Tamil Nadu, Karnataka for cyclone power restoration
76859e4a55e99067.summary: Published - November 01, 2026 11:56 pm IST - VIJAYAWADA Chief Minister N. Chandrababu Naidu has sought assistance from Tamil Nadu and Karnataka to mobilise personnel and machinery for restoring electricity infrastructure in Andhra Pradesh in anticipation of damage from Cyclone Murasu. Mr. Naidu spoke to Tamil Nadu Chief Minister C. Joseph Vijay and Karnataka Chief Minister D.K. Shivakumar on Sunday and requested them to extend support by deploying the necessary manpower and equipment for restoration works in cyclone-hit areas. Both Chief Ministers responded positively and assured him of all possible assistance. Mr. Naidu said officials of Andhra Pradesh would coordinate with their counterparts in the two States to facilitate the deployment of personnel and machinery. Meanwhile, electricity department personnel from Telangana are already engaged in restoring infrastructure damaged by Cyclone Arnab. The State government has also kept teams that completed restoration works in the Arnab-affected areas on standby for deployment in regions likely to be affected by Murasu. The move is aimed at ensuring the availability of additional manpower and equipment to tackle possible damage to power infrastructure, particularly the uprooting of electricity poles. f71560495f0d02ac.title: Coal India's October coal output rises 19.3% to 67.2 million tonnes
f71560495f0d02ac.summary: Coal India Ltd (CIL) on Sunday said its coal production rose 19.3 per cent year-on-year to 67.2 million tonnes (MT) in October. The state-owned miner had produced 56.4 MT in the same month last year, according to provisional data filed with the stock exchanges. Offtake in October stood at 70.3 MT, up 18.7 per cent from 59.2 MT a year ago. For the April-October period of 2026-27, CIL's production inched up 0.7 per cent to 388.2 MT from 385.5 MT in the year-ago period. Offtake during the seven months grew 9.2 per cent to 454.6 MT from 416.2 MT. Among the subsidiaries, Mahanadi Coalfields Ltd (MCL) recorded the highest production in October at 20.8 MT, up 25.3 per cent. South Eastern Coalfields Ltd (SECL) produced 14.3 MT, a rise of 17.4 per cent. Western Coalfields Ltd (WCL) posted the sharpest growth, with output rising 64.7 per cent to 5.9 MT. Eastern Coalfields Ltd (ECL) produced 4.6 MT, up 27.9 per cent, while Central Coalfields Ltd (CCL) output rose 26.1 per cent to 7.3 MT. Bh

The automaker sold 6.50 lakh units in October 2025. Domestic sales grew 11 per cent to 6.64 lakh units from 5.98 lakh units, while exports increased 35 per cent to 69,735 units from 51,644 units. The Japanese automaker's total sales in April-October this year grew 15 per cent to 41.74 lakh units from 36.44 lakh units in the year-ago period. Domestic sales increased 13 per cent to 37.08 lakh units, and exports climbed 28 per cent to 4.65 lakh units.

33b7076f3b21ffe3.title: Sebi bars EKI Energy, MD Dabkara, others from market; imposes penalty
33b7076f3b21ffe3.summary: Markets regulator Sebi has barred EKI Energy Services Ltd and its Managing Director Manish Kumar Dabkara from the securities market for two months and 12 months, respectively, for misrepresenting financial statements of the carbon credits trading firm and diverting funds. Also, the regulator has restrained the company's former Chief Financial Officer (CFO) Mohit Kumar Agarwal from the securities market for eight months, while whole-time directors Naveen Sharma and Sonali Sheikh have been prohibited for five months and one month, respectively. Besides, Sebi has imposed monetary penalties totalling Rs 88 lakh on the company and other individuals for various violations of securities market regulations. 14e8bffd818c6f8d.title: Govt to meet liquor firms as bulk Scotch tariff row threatens UK trade pact
14e8bffd818c6f8d.summary: Representative image from file. India's government will hold talks with liquor companies on Monday after domestic firms joined Diageo and Pernod in expressing alarm about a federal investigation into bulk Scotch ​imports, according to four sources and an industry letter. In the first major dispute ​linked to a historic India-UK trade pact implemented in July, New Delhi has told major companies ‌that bulk Scotch imports are not eligible for the tariff reduction to 75 per cent from 150 per cent agreed in the deal. The International Spirits & Wines Association of India, a group representing Pernod and Diageo, has privately warned New Delhi that the move to exclude bulk Scotch imports could undermine the pact. The Confederation of Indian Alcoholic Beverage Companies (CIABC) has now joined the protest by flagging a hit to domestic manufacturing, according to an October 27 confidential letter to the government that Reuters is reporting for the first time. Around 80 per cent of Scotch whisky imports from Britain by volume arrive in bulk to be used to make popular brands, and India's $65 billion alcohol industry had hoped the cut in tariffs would bolster business. Top Indian commerce ministry officials will on Monday ‌hold closed-door talks with several senior executives of foreign and domestic liquor companies to discuss the issue, said the four people who have direct knowledge of the meeting. The ministry did not immediately respond to a request for comment outside regular business hours on Saturday. Britain has said it is working with India on the issue, and Scottish government has raised the treatment of bulk Scotch with New Delhi, Reuters has reported. India has not commented on the matter. Whisky tariffs were a sticking point during years of protracted negotiations on a UK-India free trade deal, though ​India, a whisky-loving nation, ultimately agreed to halve taxes on certain Scotch imports. d8b69d301d1d9e4d.summary: The Odisha government launched a search operation for 12 people who went missing after a rain-triggered landslide struck a village bordering Ganjam and Kandhamal districts a day ago, officials said on Saturday. Special Relief Commissioner Rajesh P Patil said altogether, 170 personnel of the National Disaster Response Force, Odisha Disaster Rapid Action Force and Special Operation Group have been engaged in the operation to locate the missing people. "A hilltop village was home to 26 people. Thirteen of them managed to escape from the landslide, while 13 others went missing. One of the missing people has been traced, and others are still untraceable. The search operation has been going on since Friday night," Patil told reporters here on Saturday. The landslide at Gidipabali village under the Baibali panchayat in Ganjam's Bhanjanagar block was among the 10 such incidents that occurred during incessant rain triggered by cyclone Arnab. a6153da1392c8551.summary: Simplified GST registration for small sellers on e-commerce platforms, unified documentation for GST registration, faster refunds, and a Rs 10,000 threshold for issuing GST notices are some of the Goods and Services Tax process reforms that are likely to be rolled out from November 1, an official said on Thursday. The 57th GST Council meeting on October 8 approved a host of reforms in GST processes, primarily covering registration, returns, refund and adjudication. Officials said some of the changes approved by the Council that can be implemented through administrative processes will be brought into effect in phases from November 1, 2026. The changes which require an amendment to the GST law would be implemented from April 1, 2027. The notifications and circulars on the relevant process reforms have already been approved by the legal department and are likely to be issued on Friday, an official said. c8cc1631dbc97c8a.title: Low-pressure set to intensify into depression, reach Andhra coast by Nov 2
c8cc1631dbc97c8a.summary: A low-pressure weather system near the Andaman and Nicobar Islands became a "well-marked" system on Saturday and was likely to intensify into a "depression" before reaching the Andhra Pradesh coast around November 2 evening, the weather department said. In its morning bulletin on Saturday, the India Meteorological Department (IMD) said the low-pressure area has concentrated into a "well-marked" low-pressure area. "The system is moving in a west-north-westward direction. It is expected to intensify into a depression over the same region during the next 12 hours," said Manorama Mohanty, the director of the meteorological centre in Bhubaneswar. Mohanty said the IMD was yet to provide any clear information on the possible impact of the system on Odisha. "We are monitoring the system's progress and will issue further updates as it evolves," she said. f3b18465c001da4f.title: How were the States formed and how has the Indian map changed since 1947?
f3b18465c001da4f.summary: Updated - November 01, 2026 12:38 pm IST File photo of a 1955 conference of Chief Ministers to discuss the recommendations of the States Reorganisation Commission. THE HINDU PHOTO ARCHIVES The story so far: On the “appointed day”, as Independence Day was referred to in the Indian Independence Act, 1947, British paramountcy lapsed in India, leading to the formation of two independent dominions- India and Pakistan. Pre-independence India consisted of state units, provinces and more than 550 scattered princely states. Nearly 114 of these, through the Instrument of Accession, had already joined India before August 15. The rest had the choice of joining either India or Pakistan, with most deciding to accede to the former. From then to now, as India completes 79 years of independence and has 28 States and eight Union Territories, the internal boundaries of the country have undergone several changes with States being reorganised in multiple phases, with different factors behind the redrawing of the map. 7764aadbd610fe2b.title: Depression intensifies into deep depression over Bay of Bengal
7764aadbd610fe2b.summary: Published - November 01, 2026 12:09 pm IST - VIJAYAWADA Fishing boats berthed at the Visakhapatnam fishing harbour following a weather warning advising fishermen not to venture into the sea due to a Depression over the Bay of Bengal around November 2. | Photo Credit: V. Raju The depression over the southeast Bay of Bengal intensified into a deep depression in the early hours of Sunday (November 1, 2026). According to observations recorded by the India Meteorological Department (IMD) at 5.30 a.m., the system was centred about 700 km east-southeast of Chennai, 770 km south-southeast of Visakhapatnam, 770 km southeast of Machilipatnam and 810 km east-southeast of Ongole. The system is expected to move west-northwestwards and intensify into a cyclonic storm over the southwest and adjoining westcentral Bay of Bengal during the next six hours. It is likely to further intensify into a severe cyclonic storm over the westcentral Bay of Bengal on November 2. The development comes days after severe cyclonic storm Arnab hit Andhra Pradesh and Odisha on October 28. So far, the State, where polling for the municipal elections is under way in 92 urban local bodies, has not reported any significant rainfall. b5a5d1d8c6202dec.title: Commercial LPG prices hiked ₹10/cylinder; ATF hiked ₹1.37/litre
b5a5d1d8c6202dec.summary: Updated - November 01, 2026 11:41 am IST - Delhi Image used for representative purposes only. | Photo Credit: PTI In the run-up to the festive season, oil-marketing companies increased prices of the commercial variant of the liquefied petroleum gas (LPG) cylinders by nearly about ₹10 per cylinder across the country on Sunday (November 1, 2026). Further, prices of the 5 kg free-trade LPG (FTL) refill – primarily catering to migrant workers – increased by nearly ₹2.5 per cylinder. Prices of the domestic variant remained unchanged. Other than the bottled hydrocarbon gas, Sunday also had the prices of aviation turbine fuel (ATF) for domestic carriers surging by ₹1.37 per litre to ₹138.5 for every litre. This was the fourth such hike in jet fuel prices since it was last slashed in July. The latest hike has made the 19-kg cylinder in Delhi ₹10 more expensive and would now be sold at ₹2,820. The 5-kg FTL now costs ₹782 per refill in the national capital. Mumbai also woke up to a nearly similar hike. Prices of the 19 kg cylinder were hiked ₹10.5 for every cylinder to ₹2,775. Kolkata had the steepest upward revision. The cylinder became ₹17 more expensive and is now priced at ₹2,971. While in Chennai, prices increased ₹11.5 per cylinder to ₹2,994.5. Though Sunday’s standalone hike is marginal, it is the third consecutive hike since July and August, when prices of the 19 kg cylinder were cumulatively slashed by ₹380 per cylinder. Prices of the commercial variant have cumulatively increased by about ₹85 per cylinder refill across the three tranches since then, which includes the latest hike. Prior to the reduction in July and August, prices had cumulatively increased ₹1,345 for each cylinder across four tranches since March 7. The hike comes amidst a rise in projected under-recoveries for LPG in November and December. 01fce450362ae0c4.title: Seven Rameswaram fishermen detained by Sri Lankan Navy near Katchatheevu islet
01fce450362ae0c4.summary: Published - November 01, 2026 10:33 am IST - RAMESWARAM This image is used for representational purpose only. | Photo Credit: L. Balachandar In a fresh incident, seven fishermen from Rameswaram and Thangachimadam in the Ramanathapuram district were arrested on charges of poaching in international waters by Sri Lankan Navy personnel in the early hours of Sunday (November 1, 2026). According to Tamil Nadu Fisheries Department officials, Sri Lankan Navy personnel apprehended seven fishermen who were fishing between the Katchatheevu islet and Mannar North at around 1 a.m. on Sunday (November 1, 2026). They were taken, along with the trawler, to a naval port in the island nation. Fisheries Department officials issued 398 tokens on Saturday (October 31, 2026), and the fishermen were scheduled to return to the shores on Sunday evening (November 1, 2026). Seven of them were detained. Officials gave the names of the seven fishermen as Placius (41), Alagu Pandi (22), Antony Pitchai (33), Rabin (21), Nelson (58), Arulananda Xavier (65) and Sahaya Anand (34). Fishermen leaders have condemned the incident and urged the governments to get them released at the earliest. “We will convene a meeting of all fishermen associations in the coastal district and decide the next course of action,” the fishermen leader said, adding that with the Deepavali festival around, such an incident has come as a rude shock. Fisheries Department officials issued 398 tokens on Saturday (October 31, 2026), and the fishermen were scheduled to return to the shores on Sunday evening (November 1, 2026). Seven of them were detained. Officials gave the names of the seven fishermen as Placius (41), Alagu Pandi (22), Antony Pitchai (33), Rabin (21), Nelson (58), Arulananda Xavier (65) and Sahaya Anand (34). Fishermen leaders have condemned the incident and urged the governments to get them released at the earliest. “We will convene a meeting of all fishermen associations in the coastal district and decide the next course of action,” the fishermen leader said, adding that with the Deepavali festival around, such an incident has come as a rude shock. 50bb05ef00ed760e.title: Tamil Nadu to set up 26 POCSO Act courts and four NDPS courts
50bb05ef00ed760e.summary: Published - November 01, 2026 12:34 pm IST - Chennai File photo of Tamil Nadu Chief Minister C. Joseph Vijay. | Photo Credit: The Hindu Tamil Nadu Chief Minister C. Joseph Vijay has ordered the establishment of 26 courts under the Protection of Children from Sexual Offences (POCSO) Act, 2012, and four courts under the Narcotic Drugs and Psychotropic Substances (NDPS) Act, 1985, to expedite the trial of cases registered under these laws. A State government press release issued on Sunday (November 1, 2026) said during a review meeting on cases registered under the POCSO Act, the Chief Minister had stressed the need to ensure justice for victims by speeding up trials. He had also sought details on the need for additional courts. Accordingly, the government had decided to establish more courts. Already, 22 courts dealing with POCSO Act cases and four special courts will start functioning soon. The government said the Chief Minister had ordered the establishment of 12 special courts and 14 additional courts at a cost of ₹46.59 crore, taking into account the volume of cases registered under the Act. With the addition of these courts, there will be 52 special courts across 47 police districts. They are expected to expedite the delivery of justice and help prevent the recurrence of sexual offences against children, the government said. The release said, 11 special courts were already functioning to deal with cases registered under the NDPS Act. Four more courts will be established, one each in Kancheepuram, Tiruvallur and Vellore, and an additional court in Chennai. According to officials, the operation was part of the STF’s ongoing crackdown on narcotics syndicates. On Saturday (October 31), an STF team intercepted a vehicle on National Highway 12 near Madhughat in Kaliachak and recovered 2.688 kg of morphine, estimated to be worth around ₹3 crore. Earlier, on October 21, an STF team raided a location in Baishnabnagar in Malda district and seized 505 g of morphine. A 26-year-old man, Sahinur Ali, a resident of Kaliachak, was arrested. 60972eae64070a92.title: US judge dismisses Trump's multibillion-dollar defamation suit against WSJ
60972eae64070a92.summary: A federal judge has thrown out President Donald Trump's multibillion-dollar lawsuit against The Wall Street Journal and media mogul Rupert Murdoch over a story reporting on his ties to wealthy financier Jeffrey Epstein. US District Judge Darrin Gayles in Miami dismissed the suit with prejudice on Saturday, ruling that the president did not prove the defendants made defamatory statements with actual malice. The ruling said the lawsuit was "grasping at straws" as it attempted to "manufacture" flaws in the Journal's investigative reporting. When a case is thrown out "with prejudice," it cannot be refiled again and the dismissal is permanent and incontrovertible. The lawsuit was over a story the Journal published last year describing a sexually suggestive letter that the paper said bore Trump's name and was included in a 2003 album compiled for Epstein's 50th birthday. ce81647b4c51ec68.title: Mysuru City Corporation collects ₹210 crore in property tax so far this year: Yathindra Siddaramaiah
ce81647b4c51ec68.summary: Published - November 01, 2026 01:43 pm IST - Mysuru Mysuru City Corporation. File | Photo Credit: M.A. Sriram Minister in charge of Mysuru district Yathindra Siddaramaiah said the Mysuru City Corporation (MCC) has collected ₹210 crore in property tax so far during the current financial year. He was delivering his Rajyothsava Day address in Mysuru on Sunday (November 1, 2026). It may be mentioned here that the MCC had set a target of collecting ₹286.72 crore in property tax during 2026-27. During his address, Mr. Yathindra said a special ‘Prajaseva’ e-Khata campaign by charging a nominal fee of just ₹175 had been organised by MCC recently. During the campaign, over 590 property owners had been distributed e-khata documents within 72 hours of submitting their applications. So far, around 78,000 ‘A’ and ‘B’ Khatas have been issued in MCC, he added. GRAMANUBHAVA: Mr. Yathindra also launched the ‘Gramanubhava’ or Village Experience programme, an initiative by the State Government’s Department of School Education and Literacy aimed at creating awareness among urban students about rural life, agricultural culture, and their connection to the soil. AWARDS: Meanwhile, a total of 92 persons were given away district level Rajyothsava awards on the occasion. Also, SSLC and PUC students who studied in the Kannada medium at Government schools and secured the high marks were felicitated. Narasimharaja Assembly constituency MLA Tanveer Sait, MLCs C.N. Manjegowda and Raghu, Deputy Commissioner G. Lakshmikanth Reddy, Zilla Panchayat CEO S. Yukesh Kumar, Mysuru City Police Commissioner Seema Latkar, Mysuru City Corporation Commissioner M.K. Savitha, Additional Deputy Commissioner R. Aishwarya along with other officials, pro-Kannada activists, and dignitaries were present at the event. 17224b0d06a5d6de.title: Plea in SC seeks to verify Ram temple stands on land adjudicated in dispute
17224b0d06a5d6de.summary: A plea has been filed in the Supreme Court seeking the constitution of a committee or a commission to determine whether the Ram temple at Ayodhya stands on the exact premises and land which was adjudicated by the apex court in its 2019 verdict. In a landmark judgment delivered on November 9, 2019, a five-judge constitution bench of the apex court had paved the way for the construction of the Ram Temple by a trust at the disputed site at Ayodhya. It had directed the Centre to allot an alternative five-acre plot to the Sunni Waqf Board for building a new mosque at a "prominent" place in the holy town in Uttar Pradesh. In a unanimous verdict, the top court had ruled that the 2.77 acres of disputed land where the demolished Babri Masjid once stood would remain with a central government receiver and be handed over to a trust within three months for construction of the temple. The plea filed in the apex court has sought a direction for an independent survey or demarcation of the premises

99cdd265811fec81.summary: SEBI Chairman Tuhin Kanta Pandey on Saturday said the regulator is continuously working to make the country's capital markets more accessible, efficient and resilient, with a core approach focused on facilitating capital formation, improving ease of doing business and strengthening investors' protection. 00acd14ca3d9f6fc.title: Andhra civic polls: TDP, YSRCP workers clash in Pulivendula; 22.08% turnout by 11 a.m. | LIVE
00acd14ca3d9f6fc.summary: Updated - November 01, 2026 01:09 pm IST Election staff leave for their assigned polling stations with election materials and other essential equipment ahead of the November 1, 2026, municipal elections in Vijayawada. Personnel were deployed to various polling stations to ensure the polling process ran smoothly and in an orderly manner. | Photo Credit: G.N. Rao W orkers of the ruling Telugu Desam Party (TDP) and the YSR Congress Party (YSRCP) clashed in Pulivendula, the home turf of YSRCP chief and former Chief Minister Y.S. Jagan Mohan Reddy, during Andhra Pradesh’s urban local body elections on Sunday (November 1, 2026). Stones were thrown in some wards before the police brought the situation under control. Polling elsewhere, so far, has been largely peaceful, State Election Commissioner Anil Chandra Punetha said. The overall turnout in the State reached 22.08% by 11 a.m. Smaller towns are voting faster than the big cities: Jammalamadugu in Kadapa district had recorded 60.92%, while Visakhapatnam, the largest corporation, was at 13.34%. Voting for 100 urban local bodies, 13 municipal corporations and 87 municipalities and nagar panchayats, began at 7 a.m. It will end at 5 p.m. Votes will be counted on November 3. Also Read: Arrangements in place for polling in 222 wards across NTR districts Eight municipalities and nagar panchayats are not voting at all: Allagadda, Dachepalli, Darsi, Gurajala, Kamalapuram, Piduguralla, Proddatur and Rayachoti. Their chairpersons and ward members were all elected unopposed. The polls were originally due on October 28. They were put off on the Supreme Court’s directions after complaints that candidates had been prevented from filing nominations. State Election Commissioner Anil Chandra Punetha and Secretary A. Mallikarjuna reviewed polling across the State through webcasting on Sunday. Some 13,500 CCTV cameras have been installed at polling stations, following the Supreme Court’s directions. Collector S.Ramsundar Reddy and election observer Tej Bharat have been monitoring the election process in Vizianagaram as well as other parts of the district. 8a44c3e8b4b62d58.title: Justice Sanjay Kishan Kaul on his memoir ‘Without Fear or Favour ‘and the executive’s growing influence over the collegium system
8a44c3e8b4b62d58.summary: Updated - November 01, 2026 08:59 am IST Justice Sanjay Kishan Kaul Judge of Supreme Court of India, in New Delhi. | Photo Credit: Sandeep Saxena Few judges have offered as candid an account of the inner workings of India’s higher judiciary as former Supreme Court judge Justice Sanjay Kishan Kaul. In his memoir, Without Fear or Favour (Juggernaut), he reflects on a judicial career spanning over two decades, offering a ringside view of the politics surrounding judicial appointments, the executive’s growing influence over the collegium system, and the quiet power struggles simmering beneath the judiciary’s institutional facade. The memoir also offers a rare glimpse into the deliberations preceding some of the apex court’s most consequential judgments in recent years and the dilemmas confronting judges when called upon to reconcile competing interests. In an interview at his residence in New Delhi, the veteran jurist reflects on the need for systemic reforms and the challenges of preserving judicial independence. Photo: X/@INCIndia via ANI. U.K. Prime Minister Andy Burnham has said his government is open to the idea of formally apologising for Britain’s historical role in the slave trade, although he ruled out financial reparations. There have, for long, been calls for Britain to apologise and offer reparations for slavery and its colonial past, including in India. 5ad7bef16bff48b4.title: Ayur AI Integrative Diabetes Centre launched in Chennai
5ad7bef16bff48b4.summary: Published - November 01, 2026 12:55 am IST - CHENNAI The Centre aims at combining traditional Ayurveda with modern diagnostic tools and medicines and AI-driven health assessment to develop individualised approaches to diabetes management. | Photo Credit: Special Arrangement An Ayur AI Integrative Diabetes Centre, which adopts an interdisciplinary approach to diabetes management, blending traditional Ayurvedic knowledge, modern medicine, and artificial intelligence, was inaugurated at Dr. RK Diabetic Foot and Podiatry Institute here on Saturday. The Centre aims at combining traditional Ayurveda with modern diagnostic tools and medicines and AI-driven health assessment to develop individualised approaches to diabetes management, said the Institute’s founder and director, Rajesh Kesavan. A clinical study involving about 100 patients has reported promising outcomes, with a 50% improvement in diabetes management and reduction in blood sugar spikes. At the centre, dietary interventions will be customised based on individual body composition and metabolic profiles for diabetes management. An AI kiosk will facilitate AI-based health assessments. Ayur AI founder Bala Pesala said the holistic intervention aims at achieving diabetes remission. Samir Kumar Brahmachari, former Director General, Council of Scientific and Industrial Research, and Bandi Venkateshwarlu, assistant director, Regional Ayurveda Research Institute, Ministry of Ayush, also spoke. b2a54e49cada5fe7.title: Minister distributes welfare assistance at grievance redressal camp in Egmore
b2a54e49cada5fe7.summary: Published - November 01, 2026 12:44 am IST - Chennai As part of the programme, a bank loan of ₹1 crore was handed over to an area level federation through the women entrepreneurs branch of Indian Overseas Bank. | Photo Credit: Special Arrangement Minister Rajmohan distributed welfare assistance to beneficiaries at a special grievance redressal camp held in the Egmore Assembly constituency in Chennai. As part of the programme, a bank loan of ₹1 crore was handed over to an area level federation through the women entrepreneurs branch of Indian Overseas Bank (IOB). Additionally, women self-help group members received bank loans totalling ₹8 lakh through IOB under the Tamil Nadu Women Entrepreneurs Empowerment Scheme implemented by the Department of Micro, Small and Medium Enterprises. In another initiative, a scooter fitted with an adapted wheel attachment worth ₹1,18,500, was provided to Premkumar, a person with a spinal cord disability to support his mobility. c26e86f97531b3ec.title: VIS–The Hindu U-15 inter-school football tournament draws to a close
c26e86f97531b3ec.summary: Published - November 01, 2026 12:31 am IST - Chennai: Students of Velammal Matriculation Higher Secondary School, Mogappair, receiving the trophy and cash prize. | Photo Credit: SPECIAL ARRANGEMENT The third edition of the Vellore International School (VIS) U-15 inter-school football tournament, in association with The Hindu, concluded at the VIS campus near Kelambakkam on Saturday. The tournament witnessed participation from 64 teams representing schools across Chennai, Tiruvallur, Kancheepuram, Chengalpattu, Vellore, and Tiruvannamalai. It also featured around 14 government and government-aided schools. Young footballers demonstrated their technical abilities, tactical understanding, as well as sporting discipline through a series of competitive encounters. Velammal Matriculation Higher Secondary School, Mogappair, emerged as the champions for the second consecutive year. Don Bosco Matriculation Higher Secondary School, Egmore, secured the second place, while Dr. Guruswamy Mudaliar Thondaimadala Thuluvala Vellala Higher Secondary School, Sowcarpet, finished third. The winning teams received cash prizes – ₹1,00,000 for the champions, ₹75,000 for the runners-up, and ₹50,000 for the second runners-up. Individual honours were also awarded to outstanding performers. VIS Chennai Chairman and VIT vice-president G.V. Selvam said, “We began the tournament with just schools from Chennai. This year, we have extended it to six northern districts of Tamil Nadu. Next year, we hope to extend it to other States as well.” Chief Guest Sayed Sabir Pasha, Technical Director of the All India Football Federation, said that while hosting a tournament with 64 schools is a great achievement, the tournament should grow further and feature more schools. 6380088cf6d071d2.title: IIM-Bangalore records 100% summer placements, with median stipend at ₹2 lakh per month
6380088cf6d071d2.summary: Published - November 01, 2026 01:18 am IST - Bengaluru The Indian Institute Of Management-Bangalore. | Photo Credit: File photo The summer placement for the 2026-28 cohorts at the Indian Institute of Management Bangalore (IIM-B) concluded with all 608 participating students securing offers from 128 organisations during the placement week from October 26-29. Consulting accounted for a little over half the recruitments at 50.7% of all offers, according to a release from IIM-B. The median stipend for the batch was ₹2 lakh per month and the average ₹1.95 lakh per month. A record number of offers were made by Accenture Strategy, at 123. The process saw strong recruiter participation across consulting, finance, product management, sales and marketing, general management, and analytics domains. “The cycle also saw increased hiring by leading technology companies, along with a rise in first-time recruiters, who accounted for approximately 40% of participating organisations,” said the release. Tapas Ranjan Pati, head of Career Development Services, stated, “Management Consulting emerged as the most preferred domain, accounting for more than 50% of the offers, followed by Finance/Investments and Product Management Roles. Legacy recruiters, including global FMCG giants and leading Indian conglomerates, continue to recruit in significant numbers.” The placement committee said that the season witnessed strong participation from legacy and new recruiters, with approximately 40% being first-time recruiters. dd44aa9a5a1e9c68.title: Rajasthan IPS officer removed after ACB probe ordered against IAS husband
dd44aa9a5a1e9c68.summary: Published - November 01, 2026 12:52 am IST - JAIPUR The Rajasthan government on Saturday placed an Indian Police Service (IPS) officer, Prashakha Mathur, on awaiting posting order (APO) after an investigation by the Anti-Corruption Bureau (ACB) was approved against her husband and senior Indian Administrative Service (IAS) officer Shikhar Agrawal. Mr. Agrawal, who was also sent on APO earlier this week, is facing charges along with his family members of purchasing 40 villas in luxury resorts operated by a private firm in Udaipur and Alwar districts by allegedly abusing his position and influence and extending “undue benefits” to the firm. While Mr. Agrawal was serving as the Additional Chief Secretary (Industries) and additionally held charge of four public sector corporations, his wife Ms. Mathur, a 1995-batch IPS officer, was posted as Additional Director General in charge of Planning, Modernisation and Welfare. The ACB has alleged that Mr. Agrawal gave benefits such as relaxations in resort construction conditions, approvals without verification of certificates and special concessional packages to the firm. The alleged purchases of villas were made in the names of Mr. Agrawal and Ms. Mathur, their two sons, and Mr. Agrawal’s parents-in-law. The ACB has registered a Preliminary Enquiry (PE) and launched an investigation into the allegations of abuse of official position, conflict of interest, and extending undue benefits to the firm in question. ACB Director General Govind Gupta said the properties were allegedly purchased at prices substantially below their market value. The ACB’s probe will examine whether the alleged benefits caused substantial financial losses to the State government and whether Mr. Agrawal and his family members acquired assets disproportionate to their known sources of income. c5fef672503edc6f.title: Two persons held for possession of country-made guns, explosives
c5fef672503edc6f.summary: Published - November 01, 2026 12:44 am IST - VELLORE Two persons, including a farmer, were arrested for possession of two country made guns and crude bombs near Pallikonda and Pernambut towns in Vellore on Saturday. Forest officials identified the arrested persons as U. Chandru, 21, a tribal from Irular community, and G. Srinivasan, 39, a farmer. Initial inquiry revealed that Srinivasan has been cultivating paddy and groundnuts on his two acre farmland. Forest officials said that, based on a tip-off, a special team conducted searches at his house and farmland, and found country made guns, explosives, nets, torchlights, and batteries. Forest officials said that Srinivasan procured guns from his contacts in Kerala. He used pellets to hunt monkeys, rabbits, and spotted deer in forests surrounding Jawadhu Hills. In a separate incident, forest officials arrested Chandru, who was allegedly loitering with a country-made gun in the area. The team nabbed him during a regular patrol and seized the country-made gun, pellets, and explosives. Forest officials said both arrested persons were lodged at Central Prison in Vellore. Further probe is under way. Published - November 01, 2026 12:44 am IST Terms & conditions | Institutional Subscriber Comments have to be in English, and in full sentences. acceb48e5c340e5d.title: City’s golu displays honoured at ‘Kolu Kondattam’ contest
acceb48e5c340e5d.summary: Published - November 01, 2026 12:45 am IST - Chennai Winners of The Hindu Downtown ’s Kolu Kondattam – Golu Contest 2026 at Vels University on Saturday. | Photo Credit: Special Arrangement Winners of The Hindu Downtown’s Kolu Kondattam – Golu Contest 2026 were felicitated at the grand prize distribution ceremony held at Vels University in the city on Saturday. Now in its 16 th edition, the contest invited readers to showcase the Golu displays they set up at home during Navaratri. This year, television actor Sujitha visited the participants’ homes and appreciated their Golu arrangements. The prizes were awarded across five Downtown zones. The first prize was bagged by Kala Nagarajan, Sudharshan Sundhya, Swetha Swaminathan, Kala Kuma, and Bhanumathy S. The second prize winners were Karthic R., Anupama and Bharati, Divya Sathya Narayanan, Usha Gopalan, Mythili Nithyanand, Hemalatha Prakash, and Annapoorani V. The third prize winners were Padmini Mahadevan, Nirmala Madhavan, Neha C. Mouli, Saipooja Lenka, Sridevi Arun, and Chitra Kuppusamy. Consolation prizes were also presented across all five zones and in the Kolam category. Gopuram Products was the presenting partner. ITC Mangaldeep, Dheepam Lamp Oil, and Prince Jewellery were the co-power partners, in association with Poorvika Appliances. RMKV, Narpavi, S. Ramalingam (Insurance Adviser and Mutual Fund Distributor), Sundari Silks, and T.T. Asafoetida were the associate partners. Punjab National Bank was the banking partner, and Giri Trading Company was the divinity partner. Cafe Coffee Day was the food partner, Vels University, Tiruvanmiyur, the venue partner, and Repute, the water partner. Gifts for the winners were sponsored by Medimix, Naga Foods, P.S. Tamarind, Hi Laptop, Vivekananda Sarees, DIFA, RAS Chekku Oil, Maestra Electric Cooker, Cotton House, and Hanbao. 2a5f565e213d767f.title: Metrowater launches second phase of RWH awareness campaign
2a5f565e213d767f.summary: Published - November 01, 2026 12:27 am IST - CHENNAI Teams of Chennai Metrowater officials on Saturday launched the second phase of a rainwater harvesting awareness campaign across the city. A press release said 79 multi-storied buildings across various zones of the city were covered as part of the campaign. Residents were urged to maintain their RWH structures to facilitate better groundwater recharge during the Northeast monsoon. The campaigns will cover more buildings every Saturday. The water agency has also written to various commercial buildings, including theatres, and educational institutions, highlighting the significance of maintaining RWH structures. As on October 26, the teams had covered 81 multi-storied buildings across the city zones, the release said. The autorickshaw driver was accused of sexually assaulting an eight-year-old girl while driving her to school in his vehicle. 89c635675562c8c6.title: K.V. Thiruvengadam memorial oration delivered in Chennai
89c635675562c8c6.summary: Published - November 01, 2026 12:31 am IST - CHENNAI The first of the events planned for a year-long celebration of renowned clinician and teacher, the late K.V. Thiruvengadam in his birth centenary year, was held on Saturday, a press release said. The Padmashri Prof. K.V. Thiruvengadam Memorial Oration was delivered at Sree Balaji Medical College and Hospital, by S.R. Chandra, former professor and head of neurology, NIMHANS, Bengaluru, on ‘The Patient Speaks, the Doctor Thinks and the Research Begins’, offering a compelling perspective on the centrality of clinical reasoning, attentive history-taking and thoughtful patient evaluation in medical diagnosis. This was held alongside Medcon 2026, a national conference on movement disorders. The event was organised by the Padma Shri Prof. K. V. Thiruvengadam Centenary Celebrations Committee, under the aeges of the RVR Foundation. The oration was followed by the Prof. S. Sethuraman Memorial Oration, delivered by A. Muruganathan, former professor, The Tamil Nadu Dr. MGR Medical University and director, API Physicians Research Foundation, on ‘Blood Pressure and Movement Disorders: The Bi-directional Link’. About 300 medical professionals participated in the conference, said V. Ramachandra, scientific chairman of the conference. Other sessions included talks on the basal ganglia, radiodiagnosis in movement disorders, managing early Parkinsonism, management of advanced Parkinsonism and surgeries and their effect on movement disorders. a9300ec6c74c318c.title: Two arrested for attempting to determine sex of foetus in Tirupattur
a9300ec6c74c318c.summary: Published - November 01, 2026 12:38 am IST - TIRUPATTUR Two persons were arrested by Vaniyambadi Taluk police in Tirupattur district on Saturday for conducting a sex determination test and attempting abortion of a foetus. Police identified the arrested persons as K. Indrarani, 60, and S. Geetha, 45. They are residents of Chittoor district in Andhra Pradesh. Initial inquiry revealed that V. Jagadeesan, 34, and his wife J. Pavithra, 28, both wage labourers, have two daughters. As Pavithra became pregnant again, the couple reportedly got in touch with Indrarani and Geetha through agents to conduct a sex determination test, and found that the fetus was a girl. As the couple did not want a third girl child, they allegedly sought help from Indrarani and Geetha to abort the foetus. Subsequently, the accused came to Jagadeesan’s house in Girisamudiram village on Saturday. Based on a tip-off, a team of health officials led by N. Kalu Sivalingam, District Health Officer (DHO) and S. Aravind, health officer, inspected the house and found medical equipment. Police said, along with police personnel from Vaniyambadi Taluk, the team conducted an inquiry with the suspects, who confessed that they were roped in by the couple to abort the foetus. Police said a case was registered under the Medical Termination of Pregnancy (MTP) Act, 1971. Later, two suspects were lodged at a sub-jail in Tirupattur town. Further probe is under way. 503a66fb1ea7f878.title: CM approves 2,345 additional posts in Delhi Fire Services
503a66fb1ea7f878.summary: Published - November 01, 2026 12:33 am IST Chief Minister Rekha Gupta has approved the creation of 2,345 additional posts across various categories in the Delhi Fire Services (DFS), strengthening Delhi’s firefighting and emergency rescue services, the CM’s Office (CMO) said on Saturday. The Chief Minister said it was essential to strengthen the fire service in line with the city’s growing needs to ensure the safety of Delhi’s residents and save lives. Under the restructuring, the number of posts will be increased across various ranks and categories, including Deputy Chief Fire Officer, Divisional Officer, Assistant Divisional Officer, Station Officer, Sub-Officer, Leading Fireman, Fire Operator, Peon and Gardener, as per the CMO. “This will increase the availability of personnel at every level, from senior supervisory positions to frontline staff engaged in firefighting and rescue operations. It will also help streamline the department’s organisational structure, ensure better discharge of responsibilities at different levels and improve its efficiency during emergencies,” the CMO said in a statement. Ms. Gupta said that Delhi’s rapidly growing population, expanding urban areas, densely populated settlements, high-rise buildings, industrial establishments and complex infrastructure were creating new challenges for firefighting and emergency services. “Every minute matters in the event of a fire or any other disaster. Adequately trained manpower, a strong leadership structure and the ability to respond quickly play a decisive role in protecting people and their property,” she said. e9ec351dddf4cdf9.summary: Updated - November 01, 2026 01:35 am IST - CHENNAI Devotees of the Sri Muthukumaraswamy Temple, popularly known as Kandhakottam in Rattan Bazaar in Park Town, are worried about the conduct of the Kandasashti festival this year. "Usually, tickets for the Laksharcharnai during the annual festival are sold just after Vijayadasami. Till date, the administration has not started selling tickets. Every year around 35,000 tickets each priced at ₹300 are sold to devotees who want to participate in the archanai that is slated to start on November 10. There is no sign of the conduct of the festival so far," said A. B. Srinivasan, a 65-year-old devotee. Saravanan, another devotee, said that this year would be the 99 th consecutive year of the Kandasashti festival during which grand concerts would be held. "Participants of the archanai would be given prasadam, including a bucket. Tenders for procuring various items, such as pandals, coconuts, bags, and flowers are yet to be called for. We hear that the executive officer has gone on leave and another person has taken charge," he said. The over 500-year-old shrine, is a scheme temple, meaning it belongs to a particular community — in this case, the Berri Chettis. A five-member team was chosen from the community as trustees last year and they have also been in charge of the daily administration of the temple. "He has gone to the bank and taken signatory powers without informing us. We seem to have absolutely no powers in the day-to-day running of the temple. The court had directed the Hindu Religious and Charitable Endowments Department to interfere only if there was any problem relating to the conduct of the temple. 398c7ff5a8c2a714.title: Cab driver arrested for abusing elderly woman and throwing her luggage on road
398c7ff5a8c2a714.summary: Published - November 01, 2026 12:51 am IST - CHENNAI A 37-year-old cab driver was arrested for abusing and threatening an elderly woman and throwing her luggage on the road after a dispute over the fare in Elephant Gate. According to the police, Shreyas, 21, a college student residing on Thirupalli Street in Sowcarpet, lodged a complaint with the Elephant Gate police station. According to his complaint, on October 28, his uncle, aunt and grandmother booked a cab through a private taxi app to travel from Chromepet to Sowcarpet. His uncle and aunt got down at Elephant Gate, while his grandmother asked the driver to drop her off at their house on Thirupalli Street. However, the driver allegedly dropped her about 200 metres from the house. When the fare displayed on his mobile phone was ₹488, the driver demanded more money. Even after the woman paid him ₹500, he allegedly threw her luggage on the road, verbally abused her, and threatened to kill her before leaving the spot. Based on Shreyas’s complaint, the Elephant Gate police registered a case under relevant provisions of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita and the Tamil Nadu Prohibition of Harassment of Woman Act, and launched an investigation. The police arrested Mohammed Shahjahan, a native of Papanasam in Thanjavur district. 6ca4aa1ac235f655.title: Tamil Nadu government orders withdrawal of 65 cases against NEET protesters
6ca4aa1ac235f655.summary: Published - November 01, 2026 12:50 am IST - Chennai The Tamil Nadu government has ordered the withdrawal of 65 criminal cases registered against around 1,800 people who participated in protests against the National Eligibility-cum-Entrance Test (NEET), following instructions from Chief Minister C. Joseph Vijay. Several protests against NEET were held across Tamil Nadu between May 10 and July 31. A total of 65 criminal cases were registered at various police stations against around 1,800 protesters. The cases are pending at different stages. The Chief Minister was apprised of the cases registered against those who participated in the anti-NEET protests and their current status. Following his directions, the State government carefully examined the matter and issued an order to initiate necessary legal procedures to withdraw all 65 cases. 04172c2e83a2497a.title: Sinkhole at Kolathur due to Chennai Metro Rail’s tunnelling work
04172c2e83a2497a.summary: Published - November 01, 2026 12:42 am IST - CHENNAI An autorickshaw partly fell into a sink hole at Srinivasa Nagar in Kolathur due to Chennai Metro Rail’s tunnelling work for the phase II project on Saturday night. According to officials of Chennai Metro Rail Limited (CMRL), around 8.30 p.m., a stationary autorickshaw partially slipped in as a sink hole occurred. Since the driver was not inside the autorickshaw, no one was injured in the incident. Tunnelling work has been under way in this location to build an underground network as part of corridor 5 (Madhavaram to Sholinganallur via Kolathur) for the Phase II project. “The workers poured concrete and have carried out repair work at the location. This could have happened due to settlement from the tunnelling work,” an official said. 6b4c9c8ff29a02f3.title: Isro's GSLV successfully places NVS-03 satellite into 'designated' orbit
6b4c9c8ff29a02f3.summary: India's independent regional navigation satellite system NavIC was restored to its minimum operational configuration of four satellites on Friday as ISRO successfully launched its navigation satellite NVS-03, which was placed into the designated injection orbit by a GSLV rocket. The second-generation navigation satellite NVS-03 with indigenous and procured atomic clocks has a wide array of applications including civilian use like real time tracking of trains, vehicles, and shipping vessels. Further, the NavIC constellation is an important component of the 'one nation, one time' project, ISRO chief V Narayanan said after the successful mission launch. The NVS-03 satellite is all set to complement three other navigational satellites in operation including the NVS-01 and it will strengthen infrastructure for a robust IST with the government recently notifying the Legal Metrology (Indian Standard Time) Rules, 2026. 84c2008d60e1c7c2.title: IGL Q2 result: Net profit plunges 93.5% to ₹24 crore on higher gas costs
84c2008d60e1c7c2.summary: Indraprastha Gas Ltd (IGL), the country's largest city gas distributor, reported a sharp 93.5 per cent decline in standalone net profit for the September quarter as a substantial increase in input gas costs eroded margins, offsetting higher sales volumes and revenue. Net profit fell to Rs 24.38 crore in the second quarter of 2026-27 from Rs 372.51 crore a year earlier, despite an 8 per cent increase in sales volumes and a 26 per cent jump in gross turnover. The company said its average daily gas sales crossed the 10 million standard cubic metres per day (mmscmd) mark for the first time, rising to 10.06 mmscmd in the July-September period from 9.31 mmscmd in the corresponding period last year. Gross sales turnover increased to Rs 5,999.13 crore from Rs 4,431.63 crore, reflecting higher sales as well as the impact of increased gas prices. b4d11997adf86a36.title: Beyond gullibility: On digital arrest scams
b4d11997adf86a36.summary: Published - October 31, 2026 01:06 am IST Chief Justice of India Surya Kant’s exasperation , during the Supreme Court’s hearing on October 29 on the “digital arrest” scams , that people still fall for such scams despite abundant warnings and orders from the Court is understandable. About ₹800 crore has been lost to these scams this year even after recoveries, a hefty sum from the savings of individual victims. But this is not merely about gullibility. Scammers posing as CBI or police officers succeed because their victims, older citizens in particular, defer to or fear law enforcement. When Indian police are widely seen as high-handed towards ordinary citizens and as serving only the powerful, the threat of an “arrest” over a video call cannot be that implausible for many. That said, the Court’s pressing of the Reserve Bank of India to finalise its KYC Amendment Directions, 2026, which require banks to flag suspected mule accounts and put temporary debit holds on them, is welcome. CBI investigations have shown that mule accounts are central to scammers laundering their proceeds after duping victims and that bank staff have, in some cases, helped open them. With the availability of complete transaction histories and AI tools, banks can now spot anomalous transactions faster. The Attorney-General’s assurance that the directions will be in force by December 31 is also welcome. c6695201f3e69211.summary: Updated - October 31, 2026 06:11 am IST GSLV-F18 NVS-03 mission accomplished. Photo credit: X/@isro The Geosynchronous Satellite Launch Vehicle (GSLV-F18) on Friday (October 30, 2026) successfully launched the NVS-03 satellite from the Satish Dhawan Space Centre in Sriharikota, according to the ISRO. Also read | Countdown progressing for ISRO’s crucial GSLV-F18 launch carrying navigation satellite NVS-03 The GSLV-F18 with the NVS-03 satellite lifted off from the second launch pad of the spaceport and, 18 minutes later placed the satellite into the intended geosynchronous transfer orbit. “The GSLV-F18 vehicle has successfully and precisely injected the NVS-03 satellite weighing 2250 kg in the intended elliptical orbit. Let me congratulate each and every team member of ISRO, industrial partners, academia for this outstanding accomplishment,” ISRO Chairman Dr. V. Narayanan said. NVS-03 has reached its intended orbit, says ISRO The GSLV rocket carrying the next-gen navigation satellite NVS-03 lifts off from Sriharikota Spaceport. 18.46 minutes later, the GSLV-F18 is expected to place the NVS-03 satellite into the intended geosynchronous transfer orbit. Cryo-stage performance of GSLV rocket normal ISRO’s live coverage of the GSLV-F18/NVS-03 mission will begin at 11:20 pm IST on October 30, ahead of the scheduled 11:51 pm launch from Sriharikota. ISRO’s NVS satellite launch programme has seen considerable gaps between missions. NVS-01 was launched in May 2023, followed by NVS-02 in January 2025, a gap of 19 months. The next satellite, NVS-03, is scheduled for launch in October 2026, nearly 20 months after its predecessor. The pace of launches has also been affected by setbacks in ISRO’s broader mission programme. The space agency recorded three failures in six missions launched from Indian soil between January 2025 and January 2026, adding to the challenges of maintaining a steady launch schedule. c1472de631cd1612.title: Heavy polling in second phase panchayat elections for Sarpanch, Ward Panch in Rajasthan
c1472de631cd1612.summary: Published - October 31, 2026 04:25 am IST - JAIPUR Women voters walk towards a polling station to cast their votes during the second phase of the Panchayat elections (Sarpanch) in Ajmer. | Photo Credit: ANI A heavy polling took place in the second phase of village panchayat elections for Sarpanch and Ward Panch in 22 districts of Rajasthan on Friday (October 30, 2026). While 45 Sarpanches were earlier elected unopposed, as many as 3,626 village panchayats went to polls and 1.06 crore voters exercised their franchise. The highest voter turnout was recorded at 84.37% in Jaipur district’s Rampura Dabri. Voters arrived at polling booths in large numbers, enthusiastically, with elderly people and women seen standing in queues to exercise their right to vote. People turned up to vote despite light rain and drizzle at places such as Kotputli-Behror, situated on the Jaipur-Delhi national highway, and the Malakhera area in Alwar district. Counting of votes started immediately after the polling ended, while the results were expected to be declared by late night. Residents of Karanpur village in Dausa district’s Mahwa area boycotted polling in protest against the delimitation exercise, while the villagers at Dausa’s Pyara Ka Nagla and Jalore’s Bawatra and Dayalpur did not turn up for voting in protest against the change of their panchayats. Rajasthan gram panchayat polls: second phase held amid reports of minor clashes, protests Rival groups of villagers in Kotputli-Behror’s Majra Aheer and Jodhpur’s Sangariya Phata clashed over allegations of bogus voting. Police intervened at both places and brought the situation under control.
