0c619ef70855dd06.title: Delhi BLOs to record reasons for removing names of eligible voters
0c619ef70855dd06.summary: Published - October 31, 2026 04:30 am IST - NEW DELHI Details of an elector being recorded at a special camp in New Delhi. | Photo Credit: SUSHIL KUMAR VERMA Booth Level Officers (BLOs) in Delhi have been asked to record why eligible electors were earlier marked absent, shifted, dead or duplicate (ASDD), and why those traced during re-verification are unwilling to submit Form 6 to get their names back on the rolls as new voters, The Hindu has learnt. The instructions come amid the ongoing re-verification of 47.56 lakh names dropped from the draft roll published on August 31 after being placed in the ASDD categories. On Thursday, the Election Commission of India (ECI) pushed the deadline for publishing Delhi’s final electoral roll to December 22, marking the fourth such revision. As per the revised schedule, the deadline for filing claims and objections has been extended by 26 days, from October 30 to November 25, giving eligible electors more time to seek inclusion in the final roll during the ongoing special intensive revision (SIR) drive. The disposal of claims and objections will have to be completed by December 15. A new ‘Remarks’ column has been added to the BLO mobile application to record details of the re-verification exercise. This field will be used to record why an elector was placed in the ASDD categories during the enumeration phase, whether the person was found residing at the registered address and, if eligible, why the person was reluctant to submit Form 6. The column will also be used to record cases in which an elector is found at the registered address but has already enrolled in another constituency. BLOs have been provided with the ASDD lists, along with the corresponding addresses, and instructed to conduct door-to-door visits to verify the voters’ details. 60f4661931bde0bf.title: Keralam Chief Minister calls for protecting Vembanad lake system
60f4661931bde0bf.summary: Published - October 31, 2026 07:00 am IST - KOCHI Chief Minister V.D. Satheesan releases B. Madhusoodana Kurup’s book, ‘Exploring the Legacy of Fishing and Farming below Sea Level: Vembanad-Kole Wetlands of South India’, by handing over copies to former Fisheries ministers K. Babu and S. Sarma at a function held in Kochi on Friday. | Photo Credit: Special Arrangement Chief Minister V.D. Satheesan has called for steps to protect the ecology of the Vembanad lake system, which has come under severe stress due to a host of factors including climate change. Mr. Satheesan was speaking at a commemorative function organised here to pay tributes to noted fisheries expert B. Madhusoodana Kurup who passed away recently. Kurup, who co-authored the book, ‘Exploring the Legacy of Fishing and Farming below Sea Level: Vembanad-Kole Wetlands of South India,’ with Sileesh Mullasseri, had brought out issues facing the lake ecosystem, which has shrunk to 10,000 sq. km. from its original extent of 40,000 sq. km. Anthropogenic activities and impacts of climate change have adversely affected the lake system, which is spread over three districts of the State and sustains the lives of millions. He had also put forth a series of projects for the revival and protection of the lake, Mr. Satheesan said. The Chief Minister suggested setting up a chair at the Kerala University for Fisheries and Ocean Studies (Kufos) in Kurup’s name to take forward the academic and research activities initiated by him. Kurup was the founding Vice-Chancellor of the university. Mr. Satheesan released the book by handing over copies to K. Babu and S. Sarma, former Fisheries ministers. Fisheries Minister V.E. Abdul Gafoor presided. Mayor V.K. Minimol, T.J. Vinod and Mohammed Shiyas, MLAs; K.V.P. Krishnakumar, councillor, Kochi Corporation; A. Bijukumar, Vice-Chancellor, Kufos; M. Junaid Bushiri, Vice-Chancellor, Cochin University of Science and Technology (Cusat); and P.C. Hari Govind, Registrar, Cusat, spoke. Publish

05beb36896da58a1.title: Fiscal deficit rises to ₹7.14 trillion or 42.1% of FY27 target in first six months
05beb36896da58a1.summary: New Delhi: India's fiscal deficit widened in the first six months of FY27, as capital spending and subsidy outlays continued to rise. Fiscal deficit, or the gap between government expenditure and receipts, stood at ₹ 7.14 trillion at the end of September, latest data from the Controller General of Accounts (CGA) showed. This amounts to 42.1% of the full-year budget estimate, higher than 36.5% in the corresponding period of the previous year. At the end of August, the fiscal deficit had stood at 41.9% of the annual target. The higher proportion of the budgeted fiscal deficit already incurred in the first half of FY27 indicates mounting pressure on the government's fiscal balance, with expenditure growing faster than the pace of deficit accumulation seen in the year-ago period. The Centre has budgeted a fiscal deficit of ₹ 16.96 trillion, or 4.3% of GDP, for FY27. It is relying on robust tax collections and higher non-tax revenues in the coming months to meet this target. The fiscal deficit is typically financed through borrowings. The widening gap assumes significance as the government has cut its FY27 market borrowing by nearly ₹ 1.2 trillion and now plans to raise ₹ 7.86 trillion through dated government securities in the second half of the fiscal year, as Mint reported on 25 September. The Centre now expects to borrow ₹ 15.995 trillion through dated securities during FY27, compared with ₹ 17.2 trillion estimated in the Union budget, according to the finance ministry 's borrowing plan released in consultation with the Reserve Bank of India (RBI) on 25 September. “The impact of higher subsidy outgo as well as front-loading of capex has led to a much higher H1 fiscal deficit compared to previous fiscal year, with the increase being 4.6 percentage points. 05beb36896da58a1.raw_facts: New Delhi: India's fiscal deficit widened in the first six months of FY27, as capital spending and subsidy outlays continued to rise. Fiscal deficit, or the gap between government expenditure and receipts, stood at ₹ 7.14 trillion at the end of September, latest data from the Controller General of Accounts (CGA) showed. This amounts to 42.1% of the full-year budget estimate, higher than 36.5% in the corresponding period of the previous year. At the end of August, the fiscal deficit had stood at 41.9% of the annual target. The higher proportion of the budgeted fiscal deficit already incurred in the first half of FY27 indicates mounting pressure on the government's fiscal balance, with expenditure growing faster than the pace of deficit accumulation seen in the year-ago period. The Centre has budgeted a fiscal deficit of ₹ 16.96 trillion, or 4.3% of GDP, for FY27. It is relying on robust tax collections and higher non-tax revenues in the coming months to meet this target. The fiscal deficit is typically financed through borrowings. The widening gap assumes significance as the government has cut its FY27 market borrowing by nearly ₹ 1.2 trillion and now plans to raise ₹ 7.86 trillion through dated government securities in the second half of the fiscal year, as Mint reported on 25 September. The Centre now expects to borrow ₹ 15.995 trillion through dated securities during FY27, compared with ₹ 17.2 trillion estimated in the Union budget, according to the finance ministry 's borrowing plan released in consultation with the Reserve Bank of India (RBI) on 25 September. “The impact of higher subsidy outgo as well as front-loading of capex has led to a much higher H1 fiscal deficit compared to previous fiscal year, with the increase being 4.6 percentage points. Officials on Friday (October 30, 2026) said no human casualties have been reported, but there are growing concerns over a large artificial lake formed near Taktsemakhang, about 2,000 feet downstream of Laya. The accumulation of water at the confluence of the flood-affected channels of Mochhu (river) has raised fears of another sudden outburst, which could be disastrous for downstream areas. Officials said they could not immediately assess the GLOF impact on Thursday night (October 29, 2026). Royal Bhutan Army personnel stationed at Taktsemakhang and people near Gasa Tshachu, a hot spring, were instructed to evacuate to a safer location. “Prime Minister Tshering Tobgay is in Laya to assess the artificial lake at Taktesakhang, while Industry, Commerce and Employment Minister Namgyel Dorji is monitoring the situation in Punakha,” a Department of Local Governance and Disaster Management official said. Punakha and Thimphu districts are south of Gasa, which borders the Tibetan Autonomous Region. These and other neighbouring districts were put on high alert for potential danger from the GLOF-induced artificial lake. Floodwaters washed away almost all public facilities in the area. 2bb490adffdd451a.title: High Court directs BU to collect charges from autonomous colleges only within parameters of UGC regulations
2bb490adffdd451a.summary: Updated - October 31, 2026 07:01 am IST - COIMBATORE Image used for representational purposes only | Photo Credit: The Hindu Bharathiar University was directed by the Madras High Court on Thursday, through an interim order, to collect charges from autonomous colleges only within the parameters of UGC regulations. Justice K. Surendar passed the interim order and listed the matter for hearing on November 25, 2026. The writ petition filed by Association of Self Financing Arts, Science and Management Colleges of Tamil Nadu (ASFASM TN) had sought a directive to the respondents: the State of Tamil Nadu represented by then Principal Secretary to the Government, Higher Education Department, the Registrar of Bharathiar University, and University Grants Commission, to desist from demanding and collecting affiliation fee, continuation of provisional affiliation fee and permanent affiliation fee from the Autonomous Colleges contrary to Clause 3.5 of the University Grants Commission (Conferment of Autonomous Status upon Colleges and Measures for Maintenance of Standards in Autonomous Colleges) Regulations, 2023. The association was also against the university’s insistence on prior approval for starting certificate/diploma courses and U.G./P.G. programmes, pointing out that it was a violation of Clause 10 of UGC Regulations, 2023. 8fe951e2cb488efa.title: Man sets house ablaze; firefighter injured in cylinder blast
8fe951e2cb488efa.summary: Published - October 31, 2026 04:45 am IST A 30-year-old man, described as an alcoholic, allegedly set his house on fire in northwest Delhi’s Jahangirpuri on Friday, triggering a massive blaze in which an LPG cylinder exploded and a firefighter sustained 25% burn injuries, police said. The police received a PCR call at 11.26 a.m. about a fire on the ground floor of a house in Jahangirpuri. Bharat (30), who lived with his mother, Raj Rani, allegedly set the house on fire. His mother was also present at the house when the incident occurred, the police said. While the fire brigade team was engaged in extinguishing the blaze, an LPG cylinder exploded, injuring Ankit (32), an Assistant Fire Officer with the Delhi Fire Service. He sustained burns to his face, hair and both hands, the police said. Ankit was initially taken to Babu Jagjivan Ram Memorial Hospital, where his injuries were assessed at around 25% burns. He was subsequently referred to the burn ward of the All India Institute of Medical Sciences for further treatment. Fire department officers said the blaze involved household articles and an LPG cylinder on the ground floor of the three-storey building. The police have registered an FIR against Bharat under Section 36(g) of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS) for mischief by fire. Further investigation is under way. Palem, Mr. Kishore directed officials to finish preparations well in advance and plan an orderly issue of material. With campaigning having ended at 5 p.m., he reminded parties, candidates, and agents that the silent period is in force. Voters will be given a pink ballot paper for the mayoral candidate and a white one for the corporator, and both are to be dropped in a single box. 74f97baf653e9aa4.title: Environmentalists express ‘serious concerns’ over Yamuna riverfront project
74f97baf653e9aa4.summary: Published - October 31, 2026 04:30 am IST A former Union Ministry Secretary and other environmentalists on Friday wrote to Union Jal Shakti Minister C. R. Patil and others, raising “serious concerns” over the proposed riverfront development project along the Yamuna in Delhi. They urged the authorities to ensure that no project compromises the integrity of the river, its floodplain and the national capital’s long-term flood security. The letter said several media reports over the past week had quoted Water Minister Pravesh Sahib Singh as announcing the initiation of the process for an MoU with the Sabarmati Riverfront Development Corporation Limited (SRFDCL) for a Sabarmati-style riverfront development project along the Yamuna in Delhi. “We wish to underline that replication of a Sabarmati-like riverfront development plan cannot resolve the crisis of Yamuna pollution, floodplain mismanagement and flood threats; it will only worsen the situation. The Government first needs a scientifically sound plan to restore the river’s environmental flows, reduce pollution load, protect its floodplain and understand the causes of its changing flood behaviour,” the letter said. The letter was signed by Shashi Shekhar, former Secretary at the Ministry of Water Resources, River Development and Ganga Rejuvenation; Bhim Singh Rawat of the South Asia Network on Dams, Rivers and People (SANDRP); environmental activist Bhavreen Kandhari; and others. The signatories urged the Central government Ministries concerned and the Delhi government to ensure that no project compromises the Yamuna’s integrity, its floodplain and the national capital’s long-term flood security. “Public resources should be directed towards addressing the causes of the river’s degradation and flood risks, rather than undertaking large-scale riverfront development plan,” the letter said. 17f0ee319a7537c7.summary: Published - October 31, 2026 01:17 am IST - CHENNAI The Tamil Nadu Urban Habitat Development Board (TNUHDB) has identified 20 locations across the State for reconstruction of ageing tenements during 2026-27 and plans to build greenfield resettlement sites in Perambur and Madurantakam. TNUHDB Chairperson Ku. Pa. Krishnan, in an interaction with journalists on Friday, said that the reconstruction projects involve demolishing existing ageing tenements and constructing new housing units at the same locations. Residents can return after the work is completed. The Board has identified a total of 70 sites for reconstruction across the State, which will be taken up in phases, he said. The TNUHDB also appealed to residents of 23 dilapidated sites to temporarily vacate their houses in view of the ongoing northeast monsoon. Of the 23 tenements identified in its safety advisory, 14 fell within the locations proposed for reconstruction this year, for which a Government Order is to be issued in the coming week. The remaining nine have been additionally prioritised for safety during the monsoon in view of their dilapidated condition. The 23 tenements include Srinivasapuram, V.O.C. Nagar, Old Block Vyasarpadi, Nagooran Thottam, Annathai Kuppam, Nallankuppam (Old), N.V.N. Nagar (Phase-II), West Cemetery Road, Pallakumaniyam and Kabali Thottam, and Rukmani Nagar. Mr. Krishnan said the Board was willing to undertake reconstruction of structurally weak buildings but residents’ cooperation in vacating the premises was essential. Citing Srinivasapuram, where tenements constructed in the 1970s had deteriorated over the years, he said the Board was ready to rebuild the houses and hand them back to the residents. Two new settlement sites will come up in Perambur and Madurantakam, with Mullai Nagar identified as the location for the Perambur project. Both projects are expected to have over 450 housing units. A G.O. will be issued in the coming weeks, said Ramana Saraswathi, Managing Director

f77cd49b7d46836b.title: Probe into synagogue arson in Keralam’s Kochi intensified: Chennithala
f77cd49b7d46836b.summary: Published - October 31, 2026 07:00 am IST Central agencies are currently gathering information related to the case. The probe into the alleged synagogue arson case has been intensified by constituting a special investigation team (SIT) under the Assistant Commissioner of Police, Ernakulam Central, in accordance with the directions of the Deputy Commissioner of Police (Kochi City), Home Minister Ramesh Chennithala has said. He was replying to a submission on the matter raised in the Assembly by T.J. Vinod, MLA. Mr. Chennithala said the Ernakulam Central Police had registered a case under Section 326(g) of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita against Ebin B. Paul, a native of Ikkaranad. The Minister further said that Sections 15 and 16 of the Unlawful Activities (Prevention) Act (UAPA) had also been added to the case after investigators obtained information suggesting possible extremist links of the accused. Central agencies are currently gathering information related to the case. c2e2ddbb5421332d.title: Future Group's Biyani brothers face lenders' ₹800 crore recovery push
c2e2ddbb5421332d.summary: This is a Mint Premium article gifted to you. Subscribe to enjoy similar stories. The Delhi High Court has sought details of assets held by Future Group promoters Kishore Biyani and his brother Rakesh Biyani as lenders move to recover nearly ₹ 800 crore in dues linked to personal guarantees given for loans to group companies. A bench of Justice Vinod Kumar on Friday issued notices to the brothers and directed them to file affidavits disclosing their assets, including bank accounts and shareholdings, within a week. The court will hear the matter next on 19 November. The petitions have been filed by Catalyst Trusteeship Ltd and Phoenix ARC Ltd under Section 9 of the Arbitration and Conciliation Act, 1996. The lenders have sought directions requiring the promoters to disclose their assets and financial interests, furnish security for the outstanding amounts and refrain from selling or transferring assets that could affect recovery. They have also sought details of the brothers' personal and beneficial assets, including bank accounts, investments, securities and interests in companies and limited liability partnerships (LLPs). The lenders have expressed concerns that assets could be transferred or disposed of before their claims are resolved. The dispute involving Kishore Biyani dates back to December 2017, when L&T Finance extended loans totalling ₹ 375 crore to Future Entertainment Pvt Ltd, backed by his personal guarantee. After the Covid-19 pandemic hit the company's business, the loans were restructured in June 2021 to around ₹ 262.2 crore, with Biyani providing a fresh personal guarantee. The lenders allege that a promised investment of ₹ 250 crore by Future Brands Ltd in Future Entertainment was never made. They also claim that insolvency proceedings against another Future Group company triggered a default under the loan agreement. CDSL has been directed to pay the penalty within 45 days, failing which recovery proceedings may be initiated. In its 102-page order, Sebi said CDSL had violated several regulatory requirements during FY2023-24, following an inspection of its operations. The violations included failure to communicate reasons for rejection of pledge requests to the depository participants of both the pledgor and pledgee, non-compliance with prescribed procedures for handling Client Unpaid Securities Accounts (CUSA), inadequate measures to prevent unauthorised data transmission and shortcomings in disaster recovery operations.
